"...Right." He was reluctant to agree, but at least he left it alone without an argument. "So long as you are safe."

"I am. I told you I'm training and everything."

"And you won't stay here now that you're home?"

I... paused.

"No. But I'll visit a lot more."

He nodded, accepting that more easily than I thought he would.

"And this friend of yours." He paused. "Sairaorg. He's another...student?"

"Training buddy." I shrugged. "And my best friend."

He smiled.

"I'm glad. He seems like a good kid."

"Yeah, he is. He's got my back."

"That's fantastic."

I debated telling him that we'd fought a dragon together yesterday just to see if he still thought that at the end, but common sense won that battle.

This time.

"I won't ask any more than that if you're not willing to tell me." He leaned over and opened a drawer on the desk and rummaged through it a little before pulling up a folded sheet of paper and handing it over to me.

I took it with a frown and unfolded it. There was a number scrolled there in neat little script.

"Your mother-" I stiffened reflexively before forcing myself to exhale. "-worked with a lot of people over the years before you were born, when she was more heavily involved with the other side of the world. She had a few friends she kept in contact with."

"So this is-?"

"One of her closest. A satyr called Gleeson Hedge." Another complicated look flashed over his face for a second. "He's... not a terrible source of information if you wanted to ask questions about the other side, or about Camp Half-Blood in particular, or anything else like that."

If that last part were any more begrudging you'd have had to pry it out of him, but there wasn't any real anger or worse there.

Just frustration - And man did I know the feeling.

"Thanks." I slipped the note into the pocket of my hoodie. "Is that it?"

"She loved you."

For a second, I didn't register the words.

Then I took them in, and my breath hitched.

"I know you don't want to hear it." He rushed to talk over, and there was something so desperately pleading in his eyes that it made me swallow the words halfway through. "But you deserve to know this much, at least. A demigod's parents don't have an easy time of it - some more so than others. Kids that attract monsters, absentee gods, and all the care and attention you need almost constantly with all the challenges piling up. Some of them can get bitter. Resentful. Hateful."

A pause.

"The worst can even take it out on their kids. Blame them for all they missed out on." Our eyes locked. "Your mother loved the life that I hated. Being on the other side of that veil was a ride she never wanted to hope off of - and then she had you."

A sickly, unpleasant feeling began to pool in my gut.

"I-"

"You were the best thing that ever happened to her."

"..."

"She said it to me herself. All the adventures, all the fights and the thrills that came with them - none of them were worth missing even a single day with you. Not one." He laughed lowly, and the sound was tinged with exhaustion and something so achingly sad and familiar that it had my hands spasming for no particular reason at all. "Her words, not mine."

"..."

"I wanted to make sure you knew that, if nothing else. She loved you in a way that made my head hurt. I don't think I ever even came close to understanding it until Katie was born, and she never once regretted having you. I kept a lot of secrets from you growing up, and she kept even more, but it was only ever to make sure you were safe, and that truth never changed the entire way through."

"..."

I couldn't talk.

I couldn't stop staring at him.

I couldn't even breathe.

"You were loved, Dan." His voice sounded shakier than I'd ever heard it. Cracked through with emotion. "You still are, and you'll always have family here. I don't want you to ever forget that."

...

"...Okay."

One quiet whisper, and that was that.

I didn't say anything else, and neither did he

I also didn't pull back when he tried to press me into a hug a little later.

Instead, I just closed my eyes and held myself in place until the sensation of being flayed raw faded away.

It took a while.

...​

A few hours later, I stepped outside the apartment with Sairaorg, and we went down a couple of flights of stairs and out into the street to get some air.

"Are you okay?"

"Never better. You?"

"Great."

He sounded more subdued than I'd ever heard him before.

Any other day, and I might've questioned why he suddenly seemed so off, but not this one.

Call it good perception, or just a lucky hunch, but after sitting in a room with my family - and having him watch me sit in a room with my family - I think I knew exactly what it was.

And when the impulse to do something about it came to me, I didn't have it in me to hesitate at all.

"Hey Sai?"

"Yeah?"

"When we get back, maybe we should visit your mom."

A lightning bolt couldn't have made him stiffen as fast as he did.

I didn't stop.

"I know the Sleeping Disease is a big deal, but Chiron might be able to help if we bring him in on it. I might be, too." It was a metric longshot, but what kind of sorry excuse for a friend would I be If I didn't even try? "It can't hurt to look into it, right?"

For a long couple of minutes, he didn't say anything.

Then his shoulders dropped, and he sighed like he'd been holding it in for the better part of a year.

"Thanks, Dan."

Two words, and they were loaded with more meaning than you could fit into a college-grade essay.

I heard it all anyway.

His voice sounded a little wet, but I didn't say anything about it.

It was only fair - he didn't say anything about the redness in my eyes either.

"Anytime. And one more thing."

I don't know when or how the idea hit me, only that it did, and I couldn't get it out of my head.

Maybe it had something to do with being back home in this world.

Maybe that's what made me think of this one adventure a certain son of the sea god may or may not have already had and what it could possibly mean for us - or it could have been something else entirely.

Honestly, I don't think I cared anymore.

"If Chiron and I can't help, then something else might be able to." Slowly, I turned to look him dead in the eye. "Have you ever heard of the Golden Fleece?"


...​

#773
Spoiler: AI Art of Young Sai and Dan.


Sometimes, Sairaorg liked to sit back and think about what his life would have looked like if he hadn't been born as the failure of the Bael.

Well, actually, 'liked' was a strong word.

Every once in a while - and less and less as time went by - he'd end up falling backwards into a half-baked imagining of what could or couldn't have been if the roll of the cosmic dice had come out differently for him, all the way back in the beginning.

If he'd been born with demonic power surging through his veins and Destruction crackling at his fingertips like there was no tomorrow, the way a 'proper' Bael heir should have been.

Some things would have been impossibly different.

Never having his mother be humiliated and effectively set aside, or being stripped of his heirship, or having to train nearly as hard as he did every day, or even meeting Chiron and Daniel eventually.

Definitely not the same way, if ever.

Other things would have been... exactly the same, honestly.

His father would still have been a raging ass. The circles of people he rubbed shoulders with - or liked to pretended he lorded over, anyway - would still be smarmy, vindictive and sometimes downright poisonous.

Worst of all, since the Sleeping Disease would still be a thing, an inevitable black mark on any life he could have had one way or the other, he would've ended up losing his mom down the line anyway.

That was the dealbreaker.

So, with the benefit of hindsight, if he had to look back and choose which way he could have ended up...

"Ow, ow, ow! Alex, not the hair! Why the hair!?"

... This would win by a mile.

He had to bite the inside of his cheek to stop from bursting out laughing as Daniel tried to say goodbye to his cousins... who answered this obviously terrible offence by clambering all over him like a pair of angry koalas and began attacking like he owed them money.

Or, Alex was at least, complete with yanking on his hair like a pair of reigns.

Katie just settled for kicking him in the shins repeatedly.

"You said you wouldn't leave!"

"And I'm not!"

She paused, eyes narrowed.

"...Okay, I kind of am, but-"

She started kicking again.

"Damn it, Katie!"

"Language."

Dan's aunt cut in, but Sairaorg saw the way she had to bite back laughter herself.

Her eyes were sparkling, and she looked like a weight had fallen off her shoulders since that awkward breakfast a couple of hours ago.

Yeah, Sairaorg hadn't missed that.

Then again, who would have?

"Katie, stop kicking your cousin."

"He deserves it!"

"Probably," Sairaorg whispered and gave her a thumbs up, and Dan stopped flailing against the girls to shoot him a dirty look.

Heh. Vengeance was sweet.

"Katie, this won't be like before." His friend finally managed to wrangle Alex off his head and crouched down a little to meet his other cousin eye to eye. "I won't be gone long, and I'll visit a lot more, promise."

"No."

"But-"

"No!"

"Katie-"

"Why do you even have to go!?" Her voice warbled a little, and Daniel suddenly looked stricken as her face scrunched up in frustration and her breath started hitching in a way anybody could tell was going to lead to tears sooner or later. "You just came back! It's not fair!"

"Katie..."

"Your cousin has to go to...school." It was his uncle that came to the rescue, stepping out from behind his wife and gently trying to soothe his daughter. "Somewhere a little too far away, sweetie. That's why he had to leave the first time, and why it took him so long to come back."

That... wasn't entirely inaccurate, technically.

A lie so white you'd think it was bleached, sure, but not totally wrong - Chiron's place was a school and a training academy all at once, just with two students and one hell of a teacher.

Better yet, it was exactly the kind of thing you could tell a kid when spilling the beans was obviously a no-no, and for so many reasons too.

Katie still looked mutinous though, biting at her lips and blinking her eyes furiously.

"But he just came back."

This time, even Sairaorg winced.

The pleading whine was heartbreaking.

"And he'll come back again." Her father leaned down to muss up her hair a little, before glancing at Daniel. "A lot sooner, I hope?"

It was a question loaded with hope, but Dan wasn't even looking at him as he pulled Katie into a hug with Alex pressed against his other arm.

"I'll visit every other day." He kissed the top of her head "You guys might forget me otherwise."

"No I wouldn't." She mumbled, shaking her head against his chest. "You promise?"

"I already did, didn't I?"

Alex perked up in his grip.

"Pinky promise?"

"...You know what, let's do that."

He set both girls down and promptly extended both pinkies outwards on the spot, and Sairaorg laughed under his breath again - even as he felt a little pang that hadn't hit him in a while.

He wondered what Magdaran was doing these days.

Him and his brother hadn't always been... distant.

They were friends once - proper family, or something close to it, but between their shared father's disdain, at best, and his mother who was a whole other bucket of worms, whatever pale ghost of a relationship they may have had never really stood a chance.

By the time Sairaorg and his mom had been banished in all but name, they'd barely spoken in months.

Now, years later, they might as well be strangers.

But that was a problem for another day, so he shook himself out of his funk just in time for Dan and his cousins to break apart.

"Now you promised. If you don't keep it, you're jinxed." Katie said, and Alex nodded firmly, little hands on her hips. "And I'll steal all your candy."

Everybody snorted, and Dan cracked a grin.

"Katie, do you expect me to believe that you and Alex didn't ransack my stash while I was gone?"

"..."

"Yeah, that's what I thought."

His aunt frowned.

"You have a stash?"

"..."

"Daniel?"

"Not anymore?"

Katie and Alex very carefully looked away. If they knew how they'd have probably started whistling innocently.

Their mother sighed and pinched the bridge of her nose "Oh my G-"

Ah, crapbaskets-!

"Let's not bring him up, please." Dan cut in right before she could finish the word, and Sairaorg sighed and shot him a grateful look. "Better not to tempt fate here."

He'd braced for impact, of course, and it might not have even had an effect at all what with the whole 'other world' thing - and that was still a trip and a half, wasn't it? - but when it came to the backlash devils got from hearing His name and just about anything that had to do with Him, it was better safe than sorry.

Sairaorg had gotten hit with it once a few months back when the two of them had gone out into the city, and that was already more than enough for one lifetime.

Just thinking about it stung.

Daniel's aunt blinked, before her eyes went a little wide.

"Oh, I didn't mean-"

"I know, Aunt Sarah. Probably wouldn't have done anything anyway, since you're not... you know," He cleared his throat awkwardly when she nodded back. "But we're better off not waving the red cape at fate anyway."

"Yes, that does sound smart." She agreed faintly, before her brows furrowed. "Wait, so Him too?"

She muttered that last part under her breath, but let the conversation drop as her husband wrapped a hand around her and rested the other on Dan's shoulder.

"You're off then?"

His friend nodded.

"Yeah, it's about time."

"Alright then. I'll walk you two out."

Technically, they didn't need to walk out when they could teleport on the spot, but Sairaorg supposed that it was the thought that counted.

Dan cuddled his cousins one more time, whispered something in each of their ears that had them all giggling in a way that was basically hardwired to make any parent in any world suspicious and rose to give his exasperated aunt a long hug before turning back to him with a nod.

"Right. Let's go."

At least the silence between Sairaorg's friend and his uncle as he walked them just to the front door wasn't nearly as loaded this time around.

Just... hesitant.

And expectant.

"I still have the keys to your mom's old place."

Dan blinked.

"The apartment?"

His uncle nodded.

"I haven't been back in years now, but I cleaned the place up good before I locked it up." The man pursed his lips. "There are probably plenty of things there you might want to look over when you have the time. If you ever want to visit-"

"I'll come to you." The answer came out a little dazed, and Sairaorg side-eyed him in a way that had him waving it off before he could ask the question. "Thanks, Uncle David."

There was a slow pause, before Dan jerked forward to give him a fleeting hug and stepped back again so quickly he basically jumped with an awkward cough.

Sairaorg couldn't a stifle his grin, and he caught another heated glare for it.

Not one word.

He blinked innocently.

I saw nothing.

Dan didn't look convinced.

Damn right you didn't.

His uncle didn't miss it, and he laughed a little as he extended a hand his way.

"Sairaorg, right?"

"Yes sir."

"Take care of my nephew, would you?" He shook his hand firmly. "You both seem like sharp kids, so make sure to watch each other's backs when you're off doing whatever it is you're going to do, alright?"

"Of course."

Sairoarg wouldn't have it any other way, and it must have shown on his face too because David Winchester's polite smile became a little more genuine.

"Good." He turned back to his nephew "I'll see you soon, Daniel. Don't forget what I told you."

"I won't."

And that was that.

The man unlocked the door, offered them one last firm nod, and then the two of them were walking out into the empty hallway and hearing the thing close and lock with a click behind them.

For a long moment, neither of them spoke.

It was only when the silence started getting vaguely uncomfortable that Sairaorg decided he might as well lead with the obvious here.

"Are you okay?"

Daniel shrugged.

"Fine."

Sairaorg raised a brow and stared flatly.

"...Okay, I could be better." He grimaced. "Some of the stuff we talked about... I don't know. Hearing it out loud kind of felt like my heart grew fists and decided to punch me in the gut for the giggles, and I'm still not sure I'm over it."

Sairaorg winced.

"That bad?"

"Just some stuff about my mom."

He didn't wince again, but it was a close call.

If there's one thing Sairoarg could get not wanting to talk about, it was his mom.

For all the many, many differences in who they were and where they came from, they really did have parallels that were nearly impossible to miss - you'd have to actively try just to ignore them.

Most of the time, that little tidbit was awesome.

He got a best friend out of it and everything, and he had no complaints there. Wouldn't trade him for the whole world and then some.

Literally.

Sometimes though - meaning right now, apparently - it just stung.

Mutually - and that was just for the normal reminders.

He wasn't touching the other thing with a hundred-foot pole - the idea that Dan had floated over to him a couple of hours ago.

His fists clenched and unclenched reflexively.

Nope.

Not a chance hell.

Getting stuck on a plan so fleeting you could squint and miss it was just a bad idea all around.

The smart thing to do was to figure it out at its own time, later.

Right.

... Except, thinking that wasn't actually helping any.

The traitorous flicker of hope at the back of his head might as well have been Holy Light for how dangerous it was to his self-control right now, and yet a part of him that was quickly getting impossible to silence or ignore was still reaching for it anyway. Never mind the risk of getting burned.

For all that Sairaorg was managing to keep his mouth shut - because he refused to be the kind of jerk who'd ruin Daniel's family reunion before they headed back home - he had spent the last couple of hours with his brain cycling through every emotion under the sun like one of those fancy spectacle roulette wheels you'd saw at big carnivals, and now he was just about ready to start vibrating out of his skin in the kind of excitement that was less 'sugary and cheery' and more 'scarily desperate'.

Seriously - It was concerning.

Maybe even more than he thought so himself, because he made the mistake of staying quiet a few seconds too long, and Dan took one look at him and immediately figured out where his mind was at, no words needed.

"We should get back. Talk to Chiron."

"Might as well." He agreed, trying not to sound too eager - which he probably definitely failed at, to be honest, but Dan didn't do anything beyond sighing wryly and reaching out to grab his shoulder.

"Ready?"

Sairaorg twitched.

And here they went again.

"Probably not?"

He didn't think he'd ever get used to... whatever it was that was happening when they jumped across worlds.

The concept was easy to brush past when they were running from one thing to the next, but that was more because he knew that trying to wrap his head around it would be a headache and a half if it even worked at all, so he was just rolling with the hits this point.

... Actually, now that he thought about it, it had only been a day since he found out about everything and went up against...Smaug.
...

"Huh."

"What?"

"I punched a dragon in the face yesterday."

"..."

"..."

Daniel stared at him funny.

"...Did you just finish processing that?"

"I think so?"

For some strange reason, he was only now remembering the feeling of those stupid-tough scales, scalding hot and glowing like molten metal beneath his fists.

He hadn't broken through, even with his Touki flared outwards to the highest peak he could drive it to, but Smaug's head had still snapped back from the force of his punches.

His punches.

The failure of the Bael.

...

Wild.

Just...wild.

Dan snorted, but he looked just as quietly excited at the reminder for all that he tried to play it cool.

"Stop smiling like that. You look ridiculous."

"No." Sairaorg countered reasonably, and his heart felt a little lighter than it did before. Just a bit. "I punched a dragon in the face."

One step forward and a hundred more to go, and that was just to start with, but a win was a win, and a tiny - and possibly a bit vindictive - part of him couldn't wait to see the looks on a few people's faces when he brought it up at some point down the line.

Thoughts for later.

Dan rolled his eyes, muttered under his breath dramatically and gripped a little tighter.

"Got it."

Finally.

They blinked out of existence.

...​

One trip later - confusing, eldritch, and likely existentially awful in ways that couldn't be described in any existing language ever, like a rollercoaster ride that looped through the Dimensional Gap itself and somehow didn't end up with you being eaten by the Apocalypse Dragon God living in that terrible void - they rematerialised in the Lonely Mountain.

Whoosh.

Immediately, a scalding wave of pure heat and fiery red light smacked them in the face like they owed it money.

"THERE YOU ARE, THIEVES!"

Sairoarg's jaw unhinged and Dan let rip an incredulous curse that would have had the original Lucifer himself wincing a little even as the two of them shot into a backward flight so fast it had the air around them tunneling and screaming from the explosive acceleration.

Smaug -the apparently very-not-dead dragon- loomed over to them live a vengeful titan wreathed in flames, maw unhinged and crackling with pure murder as his claws scrapped trenches against the cavern floor like knives scoring lines through wet clay.

"DID YOU THINK ME BEATEN!?" He boomed, and fire pooled in his open maw like a canon priming and ready to fire. "I AM SMAUG!"
...

Except... he wasn't?

Sairaorg registered it in the split second it took for him to cock back his fist, and for Daniel - who was still swearing like an opera lead reaching a crescendo, for the record - to unload his spear from the enchanted armband Chiron had given him yesterday.

The presence was missing.

That hungry, slithering draconic nastiness that reeked in ways that had nothing to do with the smell - which was still the stuff of nightmares all on its own - was just gone.

Come to think of it, even the voice was wrong - deeper and off-pitch in a way the stood out like a sore thumb if you had even a split-second to clock onto it.

And just like that, the jig was up.

Even if his eyes were telling him something different, the truth was glaringly obvious.

That's not Smaug.

The exact second that realization crossed his mind, they heard the snort.

Sairaorg froze.

Dan froze.

Hell, Smaug froze - or the image of him did, like someone had picked up the remote and hit the pause button mid-scene in a particularly campy horror movie.

The familiar voice snorted again, before devolving into genuine laughter as the bulk of the enormous dragon swallowing up everything in his line of sight flickered and faded away, the illusion melting into motes of dying light like a magical projector reel running out of steam.

Chiron stood there and continued to laugh, deeply and from the gut as the remnants of his spell fizzled out like they were never there at all.

He even wiped a tear from his eye and everything as they slowly floated down and just stared at him, the whiplash from heart-popping adrenaline to sheer disbelief shutting them up better than any number of head thumps ever could.

"The looks on your faces."

He raised both hands, chuckling, and something small, white and box-like appeared in his grip before he raised it their way.

There was a mechanical snap and a flash of light.

Then their teacher continued laughing.

"..."

"..."

"Is that," Dan's brow started twitching, chest still heaving from the ridiculous rush. His spear wavered and nearly slipped out of his suddenly slack grip. "-a freaking Polaroid camera?"

Chiron made a show of staring down at it in mock surprise.

"Truly, my student, your powers of observation astound me." His laughter finally petered out into an amused exhale, and his lips were still curved straight up as he raised the camera in their direction again. "Now smile. These are important souvenirs."

Snap - Flash.

They both stared some more.

"...was the jump scare really necessary?"

"I don't know. Was tangling with a dragon in its own lair for no conceivable reason at all necessary?"

...

Oof.

They were never going to live that one down, were they?

Dan opened his mouth, then closed it again before raising a finger in the weakest protest to date.

"I asked first."

"Necessary? No. But satisfying, however?"

Chiron's grin was pleased as punch in the most vindictive way possible.

"Immensely."

...

Sairarg's lips twitched, and his fingers spasmed like he was being tased.

Dan's shoulders shook, more than a little helplessly.

They both took a deep breath and met each other eyes.

...

""Pfft.""​

Then they started cracking up.

...​

So, as it turned out, Chiron had been real busy in the few hours that they'd been gone.

The proof?

Smaug's body had vanished, not a scale left behind, and there were nearly two dozen enormous shipping containers all in all, stacked to one side of the passageway leading up to the treasure room, and with a handful stacked a little further from than the rest in a way that had to be deliberate.

"Dragon remains." The centaur had explained, before twisting his hands like so and shrinking them in on themselves with the same kind of effort that Sairaorg used to fold his laundry and a display of space warping that made his brain hurt. "Sorted and cleaned. They'll need careful handling later to see what use we can get from them, but for now..."

He gestured to the piles and piles of heaping gold and valuables.

"There's a little room left, and I've cleared the bulk of any lingering draconic miasma from the hoard. Go pick anything else that catches your eye."

Dan perked up.

"Anything?"

"A trinket or two, nothing more. I've stored enough gold, gems, weapons and a few pieces and works crafted of a rather impressive thaumaturgically-active metal to thoroughly repay the effort you put into killing this mountain's previous tenant. Grab a few keepsakes that stand out to you, and we'll be on our way." He waved them away. "Off you go."

It didn't take them long to choose, either.

Sairaorg knew devils who'd drool over the chance to go through a mountain of treasure like this even if they were already stupid-rich, but it really wasn't his scene now that Chiron had done most of the grunt work for them, and in a hundredth the time too.

Daniel did end up going for the obvious though.

"Mine." He hefted the gold and silver-strung harp from before and cradled it to his chest like he was ready to run a victory lap with the thing. "I'm going to have so much fun with this thing."

"Try not to deafen us while you're at it."

He wasn't even kidding - the supernaturally off-pitch screeches his friend sometimes let rip in their spars were bad enough.

The last time it happened, Sairaorg's ears had nearly gone on strike.

Dan raised a brow.

"You're kidding, right? Figuring out how to turn music into a weapon is, like, the second thing near the top of my magic-stuff list right now."

Great.

"What's the first?"

"I'll get back to you on that one."

Translation: "I'll spring it on you mid-spar and try to look cool doing it."

Sairaorg smirked.

"You do that."

Counter-Translation: "It still won't help you win, but you do you, dude."

They could have gone back and forth all day, but Chiron was waiting for them, so they packed up the harp, grabbed a couple of cool-looking gemstones, and started trecking back up the literal ocean of gold.

Chiron had dented it, but only slightly. You'd have to be searching for the difference to find it, which was all kinds of crazy to think about.

Then a glint caught his eye, and Sairaorg left the thought to screech to a halt in his head as he spotted something worth more than a second look.

"Sai?"

"Give me a second."

He bounded up the hill of gold, and there it was, cresting the top of the pile.

How they missed it before, Sairaorg had no idea, but even Dan seemed stunned when he hefted the glowing, beating gemstone in his hand and marvelled at it.

"Woah."

"Right?"

It was no bigger than an apple and almost perfectly spherical, cut so cleanly it felt as smooth as glass in his grip, and it shone with a soft, silver-white radiance like brilliant moonlight and sleeping galaxies were trapped inside its heart.

The fractal rainbow shine reflected off of the gold beneath them and made even that glint brighter than it should have.

"Magic, you think?

"Maybe?"

Even if it wasn't - and Sairaorg wasn't feeling any great power from it - it still didn't make it any less...pretty.

"Now that's a souvenir." Dan nodded admiringly, and they exchanged another grin before he shrugged and patted him on the back, "Nice catch, dude. I'll ask Chiron if he's seen any more like it. Also, you're it now."

"I'm what-?"

Then he leaped over the hill of gold and started hightailing it back the way they came.

"Last one to Chiron's a rotten egg!"

"Oh, you cheating hack!"

He pocketed the stone and took off after him.

...​

The mood abruptly turned somber when Chiron finished packing away the containers, and led them back out the other path leading beyond Smaug's lair - into the first hall they'd crept into when they first entered the mountain.

Only this time, it wasn't empty.

Instead of a clear and gargantuan space, there were well over a dozen more wooden... coffins?

"What...?"

"You were gone for quite some time." He murmured, voice low in grave and solemn respect. "Enough for me to finish up here, and take a look around this mountain. I found books and engraved histories that I'll be translating later, and the remains of many dwarves hidden away in half-buried rooms and tunnels scattered across the place. I suspect they starved trying to hide from the dragon, or attempted to wait out a rescue that either never came..."

He trailed off, eyes passing over the coffins again.

Dull and unassuming, but Sairaorg couldn't stop looking at them - or get his stomach to lift from the pit it had dropped into.

"...Or simply failed entirely."

...

Ah.

This was a new feeling.

He wasn't sure what it was exactly, but he hated it already.

"Should we..." Sairaorg hesitated, trying to find the right words and probably failing abysmally. Those ingrained etiquette lessons he spent years of his childhood suffering through quickly came up short. "Do anything about them?"

"We don't know what their burial traditions look like, and if what you've told me about the Ravens who live across this mountainside is true, their kin will be returning soon." Chiron shook his head and reached over to gently pull him away. "I've given their dead the minimum of respect that is due by not leaving them in the state I found them in, as is only decent, but it's best that we let them handle what comes next by their own means.."

That seemed fair - in as much as any of this was.

To be starved in your own home...

He swallowed.

On the bright side, the memory of decking Smaug in the snout was now even more satisfying than it'd been just before.

Dan agreed, if the mutinous look in his eye and the way mouthed something about dragon scales and oven mitts and a few more words that seriously weren't safe for polite company were anything to go by.

"Come," Chiron herded them away. "It's time for us to return home."

"It doesn't really feel fair," Dan muttered a little more and a little louder, and their teacher hummed in agreement.

"It won't always. That's why you must use your best judgment." He patted him on the head as they left the hall behind. "And if it makes you feel better, we can visit in a few months. Pay our respects, and see what the returned dwarves make of this mountain."

They both perked up.

"Really?"

"Of course. Now let's get back - then you can tell me all about how your day went, and what exactly it is that's bothering both of you."

Ah.

He noticed.

Of course he did.

Sairaorg swallowed again. "Okay."

They walked the rest of the way in silence.

...​

For once, the trip back to their world wasn't overwhelming.

Sairoarg was too nervous for that - instead, they appeared in Chiron's backyard with the familiar stumble and stutter of reality and immediately followed him into the house without a word.

Nobody spoke up until they'd cleaned up, changed, and came back down to sit at the kitchen counter while Chiron poured out three mugs of tea and finally settled in to listen.

"Well?"

Telling about Dan's visit to his family was the easy part. It was only when he waited expectantly for what came next that things finally got difficult.

Sairaorg had no idea how to start himself.

"Should I-?"

"Yeah, you can go first."

His friend nodded, before turning back to Chiron.

"Quick question, teach - what do you know about the Golden Fleece?"

Chiron raised a brow.

"An old artifact, now lost. Flayed from the body of the golden-wooled ram Chrysomallus, who was sent by the cloud nymph Nephele to rescue her mortal children Phrixus and Helle from death when they were due to be sacrificed to the gods, and then was sacrificed by Phrixus himself in turn to show gratitude and appease Lord Zeus. Later the target of many a king and hero's ambitions, and the quest of Jason and Argonauts needs no explanation." He took another measured sip of his tea. "It possessed significant power for an object that was allowed to rest in mortal hands in that era - it granted its wielder the magic to bend the winds to their whim, and it could likely be used to impose their will on others by acting as a conceptual catalyst for 'Royal Authority.'"

Dan... stared.

Just a little.

"Wait, air powers and mind control? That's what it did?" He hesitated, face twisting in confusion. "Not... healing?"

Chiron's brow rose a little higher.

"No. I'm assuming then that the one you're familiar with-" 'From your world', he didn't have to say "-was different?

"Uh, yeah. The one I know has the power to heal anything - even people who've been cursed to transform into other objects or immortals who've been shredded into itty bitty little pieces." He paused. "Well, I'm not actually sure about the last one, but it's likely, and it's a solid yes on the first one."

"Impressive." Chiron offered with the same energy of someone commenting on the weather before he leaned over to pour himself another refill of tea. "And why the sudden interest in long-lost mythological artifacts?"

"Well..."

"Yes?"

They could slowly have led up to it.

Really they could have - but ripping the band-aid off and going for broke was basically half their personality at this point, so...

"I have a pretty good idea of where it is back in my world, and we want to go get it."

Credit where credit was due - and there was a heck of a lot of it due at this point - Chiron didn't even blink.

"Why?"

Here, Daniel finally stopped talking.

Instead, he nudged Sairaorg with his elbow.

All yours, man.

Sairaorg cleared his throat and forced himself not to fidget hard when Chiron's patient gaze shifted over to him.

"What do you know about the Sleeping Disease?"

...​

By the time he was done talking, his breathing was a little ragged, and he was squeezing the countertop hard enough that it was a miracle the marble didn't start splintering beneath his fingers.

If they noticed, neither Chiron nor Daniel pointed it out.

Instead, the latter was downing his own cup with enough deliberate 'I don't see nothing' energy to power a city and the former was giving him this long, heavy look that made that no-fidgeting effort he was trying to put in completely useless in no time flat.

"I see," Chiron murmured at last, exhaling steadily and pinching the bridge of his nose. "I won't ask why you didn't come to me with this before - it was your story to tell-"

Sairaorg relaxed a little-

"-but there are several glaring holes in this little plot of yours."

And nope, he tensed right back up again.

"Holes?"

"Yes. Let's start with the obvious one." He pointed at Dan. "Do you know where to find this Fleece, and how?"

That... was a good question, actually.

Sairaorg hadn't even thought to ask before, too busy trying to wrangle the flare of hope the story had brought up before he ended up setting himself for a failure so crushing he might as have had the moon dropped on him.

Daniel stiffened.

"I-" He struggled to find the words. "I have a... limited touch of foresight?"

Sairaorg stared.

"From your father?"

Apollon was the god of Divination and Prophecy, right?

"...You know what? That actually works - let's go with that." He grinned, before the expression died out under Chiron's look. "Besides, I'm ninety percent sure that there are only two places it can be, and I know how to find out for sure."

"How?"

"My uncle gave me the number of one of my mom's old satyr friends - they work with demigods back home in that camp I told you about, and we can cross the place of off the list if we call him and check in beforehand. If it's not there, it'll be in the Sea Of Monsters."

Sairarog stared some more.

"The what now?"

"Think of it as this magically-enclosed zoo habitat out in the Bermuda Triangle, only it's stuffed full of all the old-school Greek sea monsters from the myths, maybe a few new ones, and all the zookeepers probably got eaten a whole long while ago. The Fleece should be on an island with Polyphemus, the blind cyclops from the Oddessey."

"...What?"

Daniel nodded sagely.

"Yeah, I get that. Trust me, this stuff gets wild when you really think about it."

"We'll circle back to that." Chiron raised a finger. "Second point - After we arrange a visit so that I might see your mother's condition for myself-"

"You mean you will?

...

It took him five solid seconds to realize that he'd just blurted the words out, and by then Chiron was already looking at him in a way that was half-questioning, and half-exasperated.

"Did you think I wouldn't?"

"No, I-!"

He couldn't get the words out - it felt like someone had built a brick wall halfway down his throat and covered the thing in with cement just to be safe.

Dan snorted into his mug. "Idiot."

Then he yelped as Chiron nailed him upside the head.

"That's enough out of you."

Sairaorg's eyes weren't stinging.

They weren't.

Despite himself, he laughed.

It sounded a little off, but who even cared anymore?

"You're so dumb."

"Sai, your skull is thicker than industrial-grade steel. You have zero room to talk."

"Heh."

"Boys." Chiron snapped his fingers their way, but he was smiling as he did. "Focus. Assuming that we visited the Underworld, say, the week after next - Do you have any idea what your father would do should he find out where you've gone, Daniel?"

His friend paused.

"Apollon?"

Chiron sighed, and then he smacked him again.

"Ow! Hey!"

"One day, you will learn to stop asking stupid questions, and I will rejoice. Until that blessed time, answer this one - what do you think your father will do should he find out that his acknowledged and only demigod child ended up in the Underworld? In Devil territory no less?"

Dan hesitated, before looking at Sairarog, who grimaced.

"It would be bad?"

Very likely.

Most pantheons didn't like devil-kind - outright despised them, even, because his ancestors had basically gone out of their way to tick off pretty much everyone under the sun and made a hell of a showing off it too.

Pun unintended, but totally fitting.

Chiron turned to Sairaorg too.

"It would be the equivalent of a devil pillar heir somehow receiving an invitation to the Vatican and actually accepting it." He said flatly, and Sai's grimace this time was more of a full-body flinch than anything else. "To put it plainly? If you go down there and one hair on your head so much as shifts the wrong way, your father is liable to wait only long enough until you're out of harm's way before reducing anything, everything, and everyone within whatever distance he pleases to a glass floor - And that would just be to start with."

Dan paled, and somehow managed to look confused too - like he couldn't believe his divine parent would go that far for so little.

If Apollon were anything like the devil Lords Sairaorg had known and heard of, he absolutely could could and would.

"That would be bad."

"Indeed." Chiron agreed seriously, before lifting a third finger up. "Though all of that is irrelevant in the face of the most important detail - you are asking to go on a quest, and for all that you've improved tremendously in the last eight months, I don't think you're ready."

...

"What?

"You aren't ready yet." Their dumbfounded looks wash over him like waves breaking against the shoreline. "Quests are serious, deadly business - I imagine that remains as true in your original world as it does in this one. I've never willingly sent a student into one unprepared, and I'm not about to start now."

"But..." Dan staggered over the words. "We fought a dragon."

Chiron was unmoved.

"Impressive, but I'm unconvinced. One showing isn't enough. I need more than that, and while we were always heading there by the end of the year, the little display has convinced me that a change in schedule is in order. We've ironed out your basics since we started training - now it's time to see how far you can push past them. "

"What does that mean?" Sairaorg felt his heart clench like something had reached into his chest and decided to crush it in their grip like a squeaky stress ball. "What do we have to do?"

Their teacher smiled and downed the last of his tea, before carefully setting the mug down.

"Tomorrow, I'll start ironing out the details for a trip to the Underworld. I imagine you need to let someone know to expect us, Sairaorg?"

He nodded mechanically.

"Good. I'll work around that schedule - in the meantime, though, the two of you will be sparring."

Dan blinked.

"Against each other?"

Because they already did plenty of that, no reminders needed.

"No." Chiron's eyes flashed with something neither of them quite caught, but sent shivers down their spines all the same. "Against me."

...​

The next twelve hours were the longest of his life.

Sairaorg couldn't eat.

He couldn't sleep.

He could barely breathe easily.

When dawn came the next day, he was already down in the kitchen by the time Dan walked down the stairs, Courage nipping at his heels.

He took one look at his face and sighed blearily.

"Couldn't sleep, huh?"

"Not a wink."

"I get the feeling."

That was that, for the first half-hour.

He took the stool next to him, made a bowl of cereal, and then they just sat side by side and waited tensely in the kind of companionable silence had gotten used to over the last year - the benefits of having a friend after going so long without.

Sairaorg even managed to relax a little - until Chiron trotted into the room, looking as composed as ever, and found them already waiting for him.

"You're ready. Good."

He clapped his hands, and the three of them vanished on the spot.

...​

"This won't be like your other spars, and I'm not talking about the change in opponent."

Chiron's voice was iron as he led them out into the middle of the valley... that was also in the middle of nowhere.

Two enormous rocky plains that stretched up into mountains crowded them in side by side, with an enormous rock wall in front of them where Chiron stood, and what seemed like literal miles of green forest stretching out behind.

Sairarog wouldn't have been surprised to find out that they weren't even in Greece anymore, though he didn't have it to care or ask as a particularly cold chill brushed back his hair and carried the with it the scent of dew and Chiron's words over despite the distance between them.

"You want my blessing to go on a quest? You'll have to earn it."

There was a flash of green light, and Chiron's clothes morphed into gleaming bronze-tinted armour that covered his upper half perfectly. He stretched out his hand, and his staff appeared in his grip.

"Ah, crap," Daniel whispered, worried, and Sairaorg knew why.

It felt different.

The air, the tone he took with them, even the staff - it felt dangerous.

This wasn't going to be like before.

Not even close.

"Today, you are going to hurt." Chiron declared, like an executioner sharpening the blade right in front of his victims. "You might also break. What comes next will be nothing short of brutal, and we will not be stopping until you don't have it in you to move anymore. You've learned the basics - now you learn how to fight."

The word landed like it had more weight than it should have, and their teacher's eyes had never been that intense before.

Like he was daring them to back out.

Sairaorg would never admit it, but it was enough to make him hesitate, the way you'd instinctively flinch back from sure and certain danger.

Then he remembered What was at stake here.

Mom.

He had to prove he was ready.

Both of them did.

His fists clenched, and he took a deep breath right as Daniel nodded.

"Ye-"

He didn't get to finish the word, or the thought.

He didn't even see Chiron move, vanishing in place only to reappear right in front of him, and he sure as anything didn't see or feel the fist that caught him in the gut and folded him over it like a lawn chair, before propelling him back into the air so quickly it might as well have been teleportation.

Not at first, anyway.

His eyes and brain only caught up when he was already hundreds of feet away, rocketing into the distant but absurdly quick-growing tree-line and slamming right through it like a hot knife slicing into butter.

Then the pain hit like a freight train, almost as hard as Sairaorg hit the greenery and kept going as the momentum had him carving through them, rows and rows of hundred-year-old trees erupting into storms of flying bark and splinters if they weren't actively being torn out of the ground from the force of his passing.

By the time he regained enough control to pop out his wings - and they screamed in bloody protest every step of the way - and caught himself in midair, the spot Chiron had struck him from was so far away he had to squint to see it.

That, or it might have been the excruciating pain in his everything that was doing it, starting from the creaking and almost definitely cracked ribs and radiating up and down his spine like waves of muted fire and to sharp knives stabbing at the inside of his nerves.

"Ughgh."

He'd never been hit that hard.

Never - not once in his entire life, even in the last near-year's worth of training.

Nausea bubbled in his gut, trapping him in that cursed, awful half-state where you hurt too much to throw up no matter how badly you wanted to, and it was only pure, nearly mindless will that had him flapping his wing and rocketing over the tree line and back into the fight.

It took him less than a minute to soar back in a straight and furious, and by the time he managed that the the place already looked like it had been pulled through time from a battlefield in the Great War.

The ground had ruptured. The grass was on fire. Smoke rose everywhere.

"You wanted to go on a quest like this?"

Chiron's mouth didn't move, but the air rumbled with his words anyway - and whether they were meant for him, Daniel or both was anyone's guess, because his teacher was clashing his staff against his friend's spear with blows that rippled through the air hard enough that Sairaorg was feeling the vibrations at back of his teeth.

"Too slow."

For his part, Dan wasn't attacking - he was barely managing to block, chest heaving and panic clear on his face as every other hit rattled his arms, and then Chiron feinted and twisted his spear in a way that put his weight against Dan's.

"Damn it!"

It was no contest, and Serpent's Downfall went flying into the air like cheap trash.

The next thing he know, Chiron's entire hand was wrapping around his mouth and face and lifting him clear off the ground before he began galloping straight towards the mountainside, holding him directly in front of him entire time.

"Too weak."

Dan yelled in genuine terror and erupted into golden light, reinforcing himself with as much power as he could while simultaneously trying to sear and blind Chiron all at once, but the centaur didn't even flinch as he shot right into the mountainside and drove him headfirst into solid rock with the most horrendous sound of splintering rock and muffled screaming that Sairaorg had ever heard.

"Stop-!"

Too late.

Chiron kept him pressed into the stone as he changed tracks, shooting off to the left and dragging him through it, literally carving a trench into the mountainside using his head as a tool while he flailed in his grip and in unimaginable pain.

It was horrifying, and it made Sairaorg roar with fury.

"Stop it!"

He shot down like a missile, fist cocked back and Touki flaring outwards, but Chiron didn't miss a beat - he abruptly flung Dan up and switched his vice grip to his ankle, before rounding on the spot and swinging him into Sairaorg like a bat at speed and equally stupid force.

They slammed into each other like boulders in the middle of a rock slide, and the impact was so jarring it made something in his chest crack and the air erupt from his lungs so suddenly he never saw the staff coming until it caught the side of his face in one brutal swing.

Stars exploded across his vision right as they dropped straight down - for all the good it did.

They didn't even hit the ground before he was on them again, hooves lancing down in a way that would have caved in their chests if they hadn't scrambled along the dirt in a desperate attempt to put distance between them.

"You need to be better."

"Better this!"

Dan's roar was so garbled he might as well have been underwater, but a burst of condensed sunlight and magic lanced out of his hands as he threw them forward all the same - no spell, just power and anger.

In response, Chiron raised two fingers, and the beam struck and scattered like it'd been filtered through a prism.

He didn't even flinch.

"Really, Daniel?" He shook his head as his other hand rose, and the air filled with the scent of ozone as honest-to-Lucifer lightning crackled across his fingertips. "That was just inefficient - let me show you how it's done."

Sairaorg's blood froze as the world tinted in shades of green and electric blue, and the roar of thunder tore out across the valley right before-

"REACH OF SUNLIGHT!"

-The lightning bolt utterly eviscerated the spot where they'd just been heaving in the very second Dan tackled him and whisked them away in a flash of sunlight

...​

Unlike the world-hopping, there were no borderline insanity-inducing panoramas as Dan's teleportation spell took hold and transported them to the top of the mountain peak to the right of the valley, so high up that the air was paper-thin and the view would have been amazing if Sairaorg's heart wasn't actively threatening to pack its bags and climb out his throat in sheer panic.

He was also start to feel faint around the edges.

Was that shock?

"What..." Daniel heaved, trying to catch his breath. His eyes were somehow both blazing with light and glazed over, and there was a savage wound across his forehead leaking rivulets of blood down his face and binding his hair in quickly matting clumps. "...the fughghdd!?"

The word tailed off as he retched and nearly face-faulted.

That head wound was apparently even worse than it looked.

Come to think of it...

Sairaorg gingerly touched his head, and swallowed a scream through gritted teeth at the matching cut in just the same place, and the less said about the blurry vision and the state of his skull, the better.

"Y-you tell me." Even with Chiron's warnings, this was so completely off the rails he'd be tempted to laugh hysterically if he wasn't so afraid that his ribs would just give out from the effort. "What did you just do?"

It took him two seconds too long to answer.

"Teleportation spell. Got the idea from Courage." Even his breathing was still off, harried and grasping. "My hound is a creature of darkness, so he can travel through it. I'm a demigod of light, and my father's sun touches the surface of the entire world. I can go anywhere."

"...Good for you."

"...Thanks."

Talking was good, as stupid as they probably sounded - it and the adrenaline helped take away from the absolutely ludicrous pain lancing through their everything.

He tried to get off his knees and back onto his feet, and it genuinely felt like he was being tortured.

"W-What now?"

Even talking hurt.

Why did talking hurt?!

"I-" Dan never finished. His eyes suddenly went wide, and he moved to tackle Sairaorg again, this time just flinging them off the edge of the cliff and forcing them right into a wild, uncontrolled flight. "Move!"

Three seconds later, Chiron's arrow hit the mountain peak, and promptly erased it from existence in an explosion so large it could probably be seen from outer space.

Thousands of tons of gravel, dirt and waves of fire shot up into the stratosphere in a localised hurricane, and the gale-force winds that sprung out of it furiously batted at them like the palms of an angry god trying to swat them out of the sky.

It worked too.

As they fell, more arrows rained down from the sky, and they had to break apart to twist and weave as everything in sight and range became a living minefield.

Boom.

Boom.

Boom.

How they ended up on the ground so quickly, Sairaorg couldn't even remember - his ears were ringing too loudly, the spots in his vision would probably make medical professionals cry, and Chiron was suddenly right there no!

The super-amped sound - if you could call it that - that came out of Daniel's mouth as he tried to stagger him was a crime against nature and would have probably permanently damaged his hearing, but he didn't manage to get through the first note before Chiron backhanded him hard enough that his jaw and spine couldn't possibly have made it out of the experience unscathed.

He tumbled away and their teacher tutted.

"Predictable."

Then he raised his hand and caught Sairaorg's blindly thrown fist without so much as looking in his direction.

The air trembled. The ground heaved.

But Chiron's hold didn't waver.

Sairaorg felt something in him shake as his teacher shook his head.

"And disappointing."

Up became down and then up again as he swung him over one shoulder like a sack of potatoes, letting him hurtle to the ground before adding, in an almost conversational tone:

"Greater Curse Of Atlas."

Sairaorg died.

...

...

...

...

...

That had to be it, right?

What else could happen when the entire world goes monochrome grey, when gravity and what felt like space itself fold in from above to squash you flat like a bug, and when whatever small part of you that can still feel registers the sensation of your bones and flesh being ground to dust and pulverised meat as you choke on the iron tang of a mouthful of blood?

Death, that's what.

No question about it.

...

...

...

Except - why did it still hurt so much?

"How disappointing. Is this the sum of your strength?"

Sairaorg couldn't answer him. He could barely focus on the words.

But he still heard them.

"RAGH!"

He heard that too.

Daniel leaped back into the fray, arm stretched out as his spear came soaring back into his grip like a fiery missile, but to Chiron he was about as threatening as a wet kitten charging down a four-by-four.

"Back for more?" His staff deflected the first furious jab easily. "At least try to do better this time, why don't you?"

He lost track of the words and unintelligible screaming after that, and his vision went pitch black at the edges as the eternities - or seconds, who knew - passed by.

But the words still echoed in his head.

'Is this the sum of your strength?'

Over and over again, they repeated - and the voice wasn't just Chiron's anymore.

His father's smug condescension wrapped around it too, and then the people who tried to make a joke out of him, and everyone else who thought that that the failure of the Bael was pathetic enough that they could mock him to his face and within his hearing without having to worry about a single consequence to follow.

Not one.

...

And they were right.

Then.

...

...

'Is this the sum of your strength?'

...

...

No

No, no, no.

No.

It wasn't.

He wasn't done.

He still had a promise to keep.

Mom.

By the time he registered that he was screaming - faintly, because sound inside the bubble of the Greater Curse moved differently, he was already up on his hand and knees.

His spine quivered and threatened to snap. His muscles stretched to the point of tearing. Something inside his chest - not his ribs, those were already pretty much done - felt like it was on the verge of popping.

Maybe a lung.

Maybe his heart.

It didn't matter.

Sairaorg still stood anyway, powered by blood, spite and sheer freaking grit, and pushed back against the weight of the invisible burden in a way Atlas himself never could.

It wasn't enough - he was still trapped.

So he reached out.

Senjutsu, or the druidic arts, or any of a dozen other names Chiron had taught them weren't something they'd touched too long.

Sairaorg had still been refining his Touki, moulding and shaping it - the forces of the outside world where still out of reach.

Or they had been.

Slowly, with his teeth gritted hard enough to shatter diamonds, he reached out.

His Touki flared as it stretched thin and wafted off of him, and his soul thrummed like a second heartbeat as it brushed against the power of the World around him.

Quiet but ever-present, like the hum of a generator that ran so smoothly most people never even noticed it was there.

But he wasn't most people, and he wasn't going to stop at just noticing it.

Come to me.

His Touki shuddered as he tried to connect it to the invisible lines of power running across the World, making it all up.

I need your help.

Senjutsu reinforcement. The next step in his training.

Something he'd never managed before, but needs must.

Now.

For another infinitely long moment, nothing happened.

Now.

Instantly, something changed.

His body straightened. His shoulders evened out, and his limbs spasmed as his veins caught on fire. Pure power surged into him like an unstoppable tide and Sairaorg's soul reveled in it, even as the grass at his feet wilted and the air went from cold to downright arctic.

He didn't even notice the change.

Instead, he looked ahead, to where Chiron was driving Dan back and getting ready to flatten him once again with contemptuous ease.

Their eyes met. His widened.

And Sairaorg roared, pulsing with enough Touki that he glowed like a star himself, and punched the air.

Logic dictated that the effort would do nothing.

Logic also dictated that Sairaorg could never amount to much, so as far as he was concerned, logic could crawl into a hole and damn-well cry about it.

His fist struck, and with a sound like a breaking glass, Chiron's spell shattered.

So did the air as he tunneled through it in the next instant, flying so fast that even the centaur's eyes grew in surprise right before he flickered out of the way of the ballistic blow.

This time, his fist hit the ground and unleashed a cataclysm.

The ground burst. Dirt and soil heaved upwards in an enormous wave, and the trees as far as the eye can see away toppled over and snapped as they were pulverised at the roots.

The entire valley trembled from the sheer force.

When it was done, Sairaorg nearly was himself.

His arm hung limply at his side, broken in at least two places. His other limbs felt like lead weights, and his Touki spluttered weakly and felt frayed, like a worn rope.

It was terrible.

Somehow, though, he was still smiling so wide and with so many teeth it would have given hardened veterans nightmares.

"You..."

He looked up.

"You jackass." Dan descended from the sky and matched his grin with his own, and through bloody teeth at that. Like him, he was nearly vibrating in delight. "Where the hell do you get off showing me up like that?"
...
"...Ha-UGh-heh."

It hurt to laugh, but Sairaorg still managed to snicker even as his nerves rebelled, complete with torches and pitchforks and all that good stuff.

"What can I say?"

He clenched his good fist and raised it right up in challenge.

To who, he wasn't quite sure, but it was still a challenge he intended to carry out.

A goal he would achieve, and if the heavens themselves were his enemies, biblical or otherwise?

He'd punch them too.

"I'm just getting started."

"Good." They both turned in place as Chiron trotted out of the cloud of dust, idly twirling his staff in his grip. His smile, though... "I was beginning to get bored, and we aren't even close to finished."

It was the proudest Sairaorg had ever seen him look.

"Of course we're not done." Dan scoffed, and raised his spear up high as he rose back into the air. "You think I could live with myself if I let Sairaorg pull a move like that without matching it? His head will get too big!"

"My head will get too big?"

"Talk later, Sai! I need to show you both how it's done!"

"Yes."

Chiron actually laughed, and spread his arms out wide. Green light in a strobing aura, and Sairaorg realized with a start that he was finally taking just a little bit seriously.

Or maybe that was just wishful thinking.

Dealer's choice.

"That's the spirit! Come at me with everything you have!"

Dan laughed right back, totally lost in the moment - that, or the excessive blood loss was finally getting to him - and pointed his spear forward.

"Ignite, Serpent's Downfall!"

The spear exploded with fearsome dragon fire, overflowing until it became a lance of orange and gold, hungry and ready to let loose. In seconds, it shone so brightly it overshadowed the world itself, and cast everything in a hellish shade of red.

And he would know.

Hah.

Faced with that, what else was Sairaorg supposed to do but cock the one fist he had left and start bouncing on his feet himself?

"""Let's go!"""​

Then they all charged right ahead, and everything dissolved into carnage of the most amazing kind.

...
