#1,080
"Augusta."

I didn't know who this lady was supposed to be, but even if I hadn't seen the way Regulus reacted to her flames and felt the aftertaste they seared into the air myself, or clocked in on the fact that Magnus and his surviving cronies seemed about ready to seize from sheer terror at her presence alone even though she'd just saved him from death by rampaging lion, it still would have only taken me one look at her to know she was bad news.

The kind you read about under tragic, scary headlines, or caught on the news broadcasts you watched when there were absolutely no kids around to traumatize.

The icy smirk was a red flag, but it was the look in her eyes that really gave the game away - cold and sharp, and somehow just barely leashed, like the calm before the mother of all storms.

"Well, Magnus?" She drawled coolly, staring down at him like he was something she'd scraped off the bottom of her shoes and wasn't best pleased with the effort it took to pull that off. "Nothing to say? Cat got your tongue?"

No response - the mutilated wizard's mouth opened and closed, jaws flapping uselessly as he stared up at her.

She snorted derisively, and her gaze flickered all across us, dismissing Magnus, lingering on Sai, and actually pausing on me for a split second. I met her gaze without flinching, because that was almost always a terrible move in messy spots like this.

Slowly, her lips curved up with a hint of knowing.

I couldn't tell how much of a bad thing that was - only that it so obviously was a blind monkey could write a college-grade essay on it alone.

"I thought as much. Though to be fair-" She finally turned, still vaguely addressing Magnus, and that gleam in her eyes got about three shades brighter as they landed on Regulus. "-That there is certainly no ordinary cat."

The Nemean Lion shifted, and his head slowly tilted to one side - not hesitant, not even close, but more assessing, like he was trying to figure out what flavour of crazy he was looking at and what exactly he wanted to do with it.

"You-"

That's when Magnus's brain apparently finished running a system reboot and he abruptly gained his voice back.

"No!" He snarled, and if he was anyone else, anywhere else, I'd have probably called nine one one, because the man was just about foaming at the mouth. "You don't-! I won't let you take it-!"

He couldn't even finish a sentence; he was raging so badly, and Augusta just tutted, looking awfully amused.

"Deep breaths, Magnus." She waved at him in the most faux-encouraging and condescending way I'd ever heard - the way someone would talk to a toddler if they absolutely despised the little tyke and wanted to make them just as miserable. "Go on, use your words - you can do it."

Maybe a little predictably, Magnus exploded.

"I WON'T LET YOU TAKE MY POWER! I WON'T LET YOU WIN AGAIN!"

Augusta took in that little display, and then blinked lazily.

"What power?"

Good question - because if he was somehow talking about Regulus, then the blood loss must have officially ganked whatever vaguely functional excuse for brain cells he had left, and I don't think anybody would believe that the guy had started out with all that many in the first place.

Unfortunately, Magnus didn't see it that way through what had to be a haze of pure-red ballistic fury, and a howl of rage clawed its way out of his throat.

He raised the hand he had left and slammed his clenched fist down against the dirt in front of him with so much force you didn't need to hear the snap to know that something in there was broken.

"Oho?"

The familiar shifting of magic rose up into the air. Off-white sparks crackled off his fist in a gleaming sheen before it burst like a soap bubble, sending a wave of flickering light out across the valley floor. A split-second later, the ground between them ruptured, and spectral shadows poured out like the rising tide, and began to take shape.

Or shapes, actually - there was no rhyme or reason to it.

Some of them grew outwards and solidified into hulking mannequin-like warriors and parodies of medieval knights, decked out in plate armor with swords, spears, axes and whatever the heck else you could imagine off the top of your head.

Others were animals - enormous bears and wolves and canine predators out of somebody's nightmares, all with phantom-black fur and fangs and bristling claws too crooked and wrong to exist without magic putting in the work to make sure all the pieces played nice with one another while the blood-thirsty monsters rampaged and ran wild.

And those were the nice ones.

The rest were either blobs with too many teeth and eyes that looked at you from too many directions all at once - I know, I don't get it either - or... things I didn't know where or even how to begin to describe, and that should tell you plenty, because I've seen stuff at this point.

The eerie part was the silence - shadows didn't make sounds, after all, so in no time flat there was a small army of utterly quiet and just as blatantly rabid.... familiars?

Summons?

Whatever.

Point is, they were there, chomping at the bit and readying to throw themselves into the kill, and they weren't the only ones either - Magnus's cronies decided to throw their crappy hoods into the ring and join in too.

One raised his hands, and a dozen spell circles pieced themselves into rows of four in front of him like an interlocking grid, charged with all kinds of building nastiness - the kind that ramped fast and made my skin prickle in a vague but equally dangerous warning.

The second guy pointed up at the sky, and the clouds directly above us darkened. The air pressure changed and filled with static, and the smell of ozone kicked in so fast it was like someone had blown a deodorant can's worth of the stuff in a closed room.

The last stepped back and actually unsheathed a dagger, long and curved with a gnarly serrated edge. Then he waved two fingers in front of him like he was smearing color onto an invisible canvas, painting a symbol I didn't recognize in blue light before he shimmered and vanished from sight.

And all the while, Augusta just stared.

"Really?"

She didn't seem impressed or worried.

Hell, she looked downright bored - and maybe a little incredulous too.

"Golems of darkness, and amateur party tricks?" No, I take that back - definitely incredulous. "Against me?"

Magnus just snarled, eyes wild.

"Die!"

She snorted.

"Original."

He spat out something so hateful and animalistic it was more inhuman sound than an actual insult - though trust me, the insult was there and wow was it ugly - and swung his hand out like he was firing off a starter gun.

Instantly, the army charged across the gap between them and started clambering up to the ledge where she stood, almost trampling over itself as all hell broke loose... for about three seconds.

Then Augusta smiled.

"Well alright then. If you insist."

She leaned forward and tapped one foot against the earth, almost daintily, and the next thing anyone knew, the ground bubbled up with a grinding scree and erupted in a row of growing poisonous green spikes that skewered about half of them in one go. Where they struck, the shadows hissed, steamed, and melted into sludge that probably counted as a crime against nature no matter where you went in the world.

The rest of the rabid shadows didn't hesitate to leap over them and the growing mess, not the least bit bothered or even aware of the fact that their chances of success had basically - and obviously - started in the negative numbers and just dropped from there.

No survival instincts at all - just sheer murderous auto-pilot.

In response, Augusta raised a single finger.

"Burn."

And you know what?

They did, and spectacularly at that - she swiped that finger their way and bathed them all in a wave of surging purple fire so ravenous it almost felt alive - like a sentient flamethrower with an attitude.

The second the last one vanished, her hand snapped straight up and shimmered just in time for the clouds that had been steadily darkening to slam the eject button like it owed them money, and down came the lightning everyone had seen coming twenty miles away, complete with an unnatural crescendo of booming cracks like the roar of machine-gun fire dialled up to eleven.

She didn't even flinch as the bolts struck her outstretched palm and did jack all, pouring through a fractal array of lights and beginning to coil around and down her arm like a tamed serpent at a petting zoo. Then, just as quickly as she'd gathered it, she lobbed it down to meet the discharge of the dozen spell circles aimed her way without a second thought.

Boom.

Raw lightning hit structured magic and promptly exploded in ways that would have burst eardrums like pop-rocks and killed ordinary people from the shockwaves alone, and Augusta barely slowed her roll even as the shmuck who'd fired at her got blown back went ragdolling across the valley like the main character of a cheap video game.

One down.

"How dull." Then her gaze sharpened, and her other arm abruptly shot off to the side and closed around something with a sharp crunch. With a howl of pain, the croney who'd pulled his best impression of a chameleon suddenly faded back into view, the nasty-looking dagger slipping from his slackened fingers as her hold on his mangled wrist tightened. "And did you really think that would work? I could see you the entire time."

He didn't answer at first, besides the sudden tortured grunt of pain as he staggered down to his knees - Then he let rip a rapid-fire string of words that was or probably should be illegal to put in anything even close to that order ever again.

Just... yikes.

"Dear me." August gasped theatrically, free hand pressed against her chest. "Is that any way to speak to a lady? What would your mother think?"

We never found out - Maybe Augusta pushed a nerve, or maybe he was just sick of hearing her talk over the sounds of the bones in his wrist getting ground to powder in her grip, because he suddenly moved.

Another dagger appeared in his free hand with a shower of sparks and motes of scattering light, smaller than the last but glinting under the sun with an edge just as sharp, and he jabbed it up and into her side with a single, furious roar.

Or at least he tried.

With a clang that sounded oddly like metal striking more of the same, the point bounced off. A spell circle or something close to it shimmered off the ripples on Augusta's cloak, and she didn't give him a chance to try again.

Or so much as breathe, if we're really keeping count.

One second he was writing in her grip. The next - if even that - the world flared purple and a pile of ashes was crumbling at her feet and scattering into the breeze.

Gone, just like that.

"Points for gumption, if nothing else." The mockery was even and brutal as she rounded back on the Magnus and his last lackey - the one who'd called down lightning on her. "And then there were two."

Said lackey took one look at his odds for survival - or, you know, the bright red and critical lack thereof - and panicked, trying to pull a redux of the same move on what had to be fear-driven hysteria.

And again, the operative word here is tried.

He got as far as raising his arms up at the remaining cloud cover before Augusta raised hers, palm facing outwards towards him.

And then she closed it into a fist.

For a fleeting instant, nothing happened.

Then he... folded.

Literally.

He was yanked off the ground and, with a sound that was half wet tearing and all sickening snapping, violently twisted in on himself like the world's most deranged origami display.

He managed to get off one muted scream before his lungs were shredded and pasted in his collapsing chest, and then he imploded with a shower of flying gore.

A beat later, Augusta let her hand drop, and the uneven lump of flesh that used to be a person hit the dirt with a heavy thud.

...

At this point, you might be wondering where the rest of us were during all of this - Sairaorg and I, and Regulus to make three.

That's an easy one - we were right there.

Well, off to the side and clear of the mess and collateral - Sairaorg's reinforcement was on so high you'd need a tank shell to ruffle his hair, and I was basically a glare hazard with how much concentrated sunlight I was giving off - but you get the idea.

Regulus stood apart from us, and closer to the carnage, but that part didn't need an explanation. His invincible hide was literally the stuff of legends.

As to what we were all doing there in the two minutes - give or take - that Augusta had needed to massacre the wizards who stood against her...

That one was even easier - we just stared.

Regulus observed the nightmarish fiasco with all the patience of a predator scoping out prey, but Sairaorg and I stuck to our spots and took it all a little differently.

It wasn't terror, or panic, or anything like that - though I'll fess up and admit that watching one human be reduced to ash and the other turn into a bloody pretzel one after the other, and with the casual ease that Augusta had done it with too...

It was a special kind of horrifying.

The rest of it had been like watching a single car crash spiral into a flaming pileup in seconds - you couldn't look away even as everything went right crap - and Augusta's purple flames were still making my instincts go haywire.

Every spark I locked onto made my heart beat faster, and the mix of adrenaline and power pulsing through my blood acted up until it felt like my skin was three sizes too small to keep it all in.

I couldn't let my guard down. This mess was somehow still in the opening act, and I could tell that things were about to get hairy.

I just could.

From the way he was still ramping up like a spiritual bomb priming itself right next to me, Sairaorg was with me on this one.

"What's wrong, Magnus?"

Augusta was still going - or wrapping up, at least. I wasn't stupid enough to think she'd forgotten about us, but she was either putting on a show or so caught up in the one she'd already started that we were just her accidental audience, and I wasn't about to trip that landmine if I could help it.

Not right this second.

"Done, are we?" I'm pretty sure nobody who'd ever known him would have been surprised, but Magnus didn't look like he was... all there as she continued to mock him - Pale and haggard, torn between terror and black rage, like a man who was quickly losing whatever cheap excuse of a grip he'd had had before, and damn quickly too. "No more desperate gambles or pitiful sorcery to throw my way?"

"...H-Hate You..." He whispered, eyes bloodshot, before it rose back into an uneven snarl. "Everything you have should be mine!"

"Is that right?"

"I am the greater sorcerer!"

She stared down her nose at him for a second, and raised a single brow.

The silent judgment was scathing.

"Clearly."

His eyes flashed.

"Everything about you is a lie! That's not your power! I am the one with true skill!"

She smiled.

Somehow, the expression was downright vile.

"And yet there you are on your knees and in the dirt, and there you'll die when I'm done with you."

"You damned bit-!"

The word died in his throat as Augusta raised a finger, and let the tip spark with about a candle's worth of purple fire.

Barely that, even. It looked nearly harmless.

Nobody was fooled.

I could feel the danger from the one little ember right in the back of my teeth.

"I think I've heard enough." She declared, and Magnus somehow managed to pale again until the shade of his skin was near-inhuman from total terror. How he was still awake to pull that off was anyone's guess, but it wasn't going to last. Not with the final malice laced through Augusta's voice. "If you're not going to be entertaining on your deathbed, I might as well wrap things up here and start cleaning up the mess you made."

"No, wait, damn you-!"

Her smile widened in satisfaction, like she'd just scored a victory she'd been patiently expecting for who knows how long.

Considering the blatantly desperate pleading in Magnus's voice now, maybe she had.

"Goodbye, Magnus-"

"No-!"

"Hold it."

Instantly, the game changed.

Both of them stilled as Regulus's growl tore through the air between them with a vengeance and a wave of rippling presence.

Augusta's eyes snapped over to him, and Magnus nearly face-planted with a gasp.

For a moment, nobody else spoke up, but the warning was obvious in the Nemean Lion's stare.

Then he started padding over.

Calmly. Carefully. Not a care in the world.

Augusta didn't say a word as he strolled right up to Magnus's cowering form and loomed over him, golden eyes sharp.

Then he turned to glare up at her.

"A debt is owed, and it belongs to me."

...

"...Fair enough."

She actually shrugged.

Magnus just croaked - metaphorically and very literally.

"I-"

Too late.

Regulus swiped his paw and tore his face and half his head clear off with all the effort of someone swatting a fly.

...

...

...

"What the hell?" I heard Sairaorg mutter in disturbed disbelief, and as the scent of iron and something sharper quickly filled the air, I reared back with a matching grimace.

What even was this mess anymore?

Regulus grunted in something that might've been grim satisfaction as Magnus's corpse toppled over in front of him, and Augusta took that in for all of a second before she hummed and drew his attention back to her.

"A bit anticlimactic, honestly, but I suppose that dragging it out would have gotten stale eventually." The smile she gave Regulus was different from all the others - fascination crossed with delight that bordered on total glee, like Christmas had come early and she was barely holding herself back from running for the presents under the tree "All's well that ends well there, oh fearsome Longinus."

So she knew who and what he was.

Not that hard to guess, but I noted it down anyway.

"After all, there are far more interesting matters to get to now that my house cleaning is over and done with. But first things first," She continued, and bowed her head with a theatrical flair. "Augusta Hawthorn, Second Generation Witch of The East and humble member of the Wizards of Oz."

A pause.

The slow, deliberate kind.

"And,"

Something about her voice sent a wave of cold creeping down my spine.

"-Last but certainly not least,-"

And it got worse. I don't even know how - just that it did.

Her smile stretched past the point of comfort, and the hammer dropped.

"-The wielder of your fellow Longinus Class Sacred Gear."

...Oh.

"Incinerate Anthem."

Oh.

...

...

...

We are absolutely, magnificently, royally screwed.

"...Beyond all words." Sairaorg agreed in a whisper that was just as faint as mine, at which point I realized that I'd said that aloud.

Luckily, neither of the two monsters in front of us noticed.

Yet.

I wasn't even afraid - the shock and the immediate 'how the hell do we survive this' instincts clobbered that over the head and locked it in the trunk.

Purple flames, and a feeling that set off all our collective alarm bells and strayed close to divinity.

It was stupidly obvious in hindsight.

First things first, though-

"Sai." I subtly - and very slowly - start stepping up and angling myself so he'd be behind me. Just a bit. "If things go bad, stay back."

He looked at me like I was crazy.

"The hell I will."

"Don't be an idiot." I hissed right back at him "You know what that thing is."

He'd sat through the same crash course I could.

Incinerate Anthem.

One of the three Abrahamic holy relics, and a fiery death sentence to anything remotely 'dark' that wasn't a straight up-god or on that level - and even they only had it slightly better, because it sure as anything didn't play nice with pagan divinity either.

It was insanely, unfairly dangerous to me, but if a spark so much as floated Sairaorg's way, there wouldn't be enough ashes left of him to fill a soda can.

And he knew it too, because I could hear him gritting his teeth hard enough to give a dentist a heart attack even as I locked back in to Augusta and Regulus's conversation.

Which had become a staredown in seconds, with neither looking to give ground.

If you could translate Regulus's answering look into words, it'd probably be something along the lines of 'I already don't like you, and I am actively considering ways to violently murder you.'

I'm not joking - he was just about radiating muted bloodlust, but if Augusta noticed, she didn't show it.

Then the silence broke.

"Naturally you, Regulus Nemea, need no introduction - and then we have the two surprises over there." Finally, the witch turned our way and looked us over expectantly. "A devil and a demigod, and apparently hand in hand to boot. How novel."

I tried not to grimace, and mostly succeeded.

"You know what we are?"

What am I even asking?

Of course she knows.

"Obviously, child." The way she said child just about dripped with condescension, and I immediately hated it. "Your kind are rarer than others in this day and age, but only just, and you're always quite... distinctive."

Her eyes panned over to Sairaorg, who stared back evenly.

"His, on the other hand... well, I'm more than familiar. I've suffered many a nuisance at their hands." Her expression shifted into something between a frown and an irritated scowl. "Devils. They pop up like infernal weeds chasing every other fleeting whim and are always ever so eager to stick their fingers into whatever it is they can reach for, the grubby little things."

Sai grunted.

"If you're expecting an apology-"

"Oh please. What exactly would that be worth to me?"

"Considering I don't have or really want to give you one?" Sai looked her dead in the eye and deliberately shrugged. "You tell me."

"Ha! A hint of spine, I see."

She sounded pleased too, like she'd just watched a trained puppy pull a neat trick.

That, or kicked it instead - the lady seemed like that special kind of psychopath.

"You're already doing better than the last one. In one sense, at least. Abysmally low demonic power on the other, but I suppose that's hardly a metric for value in these things. The last one had plenty of it, and I still incinerated him just as easily as I do the rest of the chaff."

And there's the barely hidden threat.

In way, I was almost glad she turned back to Regulus then and dismissed us for a beat - it gave me time to send a trickle of magic down into my storage band and grab onto my bow and its quiver as each materialized in either hand.

That was step one.

Step two needed time.

"Regulus Nemea," She went back to addressing him and unknowingly gave me just that. "I have never worshipped a god, but of all the ones I might consider paying respects to, the Abrahamic fellow stands at the top of the list. His creations - his Sacred Gears - are power enough, but those of the Longinus class? Those that grant the right wielder the potential to kill gods?"

She laughed, and it was closer to a cackle than anything else.

"Glorious! A gift that borders on the peerless. From the moment I mastered Incinerate Anthem-"

"Oh, and here we go."

Regulus didn't roll his eyes - lions can't physically do that - but he did roll his neck and his whole head in a way that stopped Augusta's speech dead in its tracks.

"Ah?"

I don't think she took the interruption well.

"Mortals like you... you never change, no matter what the era." He snorted, and the derisive contempt there matched the stuff Augusta was putting out earlier tit for tat. "You fall backwards into power that doesn't belong to you and let it go straight into your puny little heads until you're so drunk on it you can't tell up from down or left from right. It's pathetic and irritating at best."

He barred his teeth, an annoyed growl rumbling past them. His mane shifted with the vibration of it.

"Do you have any idea how many other Longinus wielders have come looking for my own over the millennia? How many talked a big a game and boasted of 'their' power and 'their' might until someone took the time out of their schedule to squash them like bugs?"

His growl deepened, growing jagged and impatient. His paws pressed the ground so hard we could all hear it start to splinter.

"None of them were special, and neither are you. You want something, just like they all did, so get over yourself, and get to the damn point."

...

"As you wish."

Hoooo boy.

Her easy smile didn't shift, but something in Augusta's voice changed - it got sharper, and more pinched.

The insults had landed hard.

"I try to keep an eye on all potential and active Longinus wielders I get word of. Call it a hobby, if you will." She explained, still with that same voice. "It's how Magnus found yours."

Regulus stilled.

"He fancied himself my competition in our organization." She snorted like the idea was a bad joke - and considering what we'd all seen, it pretty obviously had been. "A bit of an old, festering grudge there that Ionely ever entertained for the comedic value alone. As it were, as foolish as he was, he knew he couldn't hope to match my Incinerate Anthem, and so he coerced one of my underlings to give a pass on the information he needed to find an equal source of power - hence you, and the unpleasantness that came to pass."

No response, but the silence was so tense and loaded it nearly had its own gravity.

"I see your rage, but rest assured that I had nothing to do with it - perhaps I would have made a move, given time, but Magnus thoroughly jumped the gun there, and you took your... rather cathartic revenge, I imagine." She paused and gave him a 'what can you do' kind of look... but the simmering anger was still there if you knew to look for it. "Regardless of how it happened, however, you are free. Somehow reembodied despite the regulations of Heaven's System. This fascinates me more than you could possibly imagine."

She spread her arms wide.

"Join me. Allow me to study you, and the means by which you've regained a corporeal form despite the workings of your Sacred Gear, and in return - take your pick."

"Take my pick?"

"I have resources and power beyond most any other mortal. Whatever you want will be yours, within reason and in exchange for your compliance."

...

"My... compliance?"

Regulus sounded... amused.

The kind of amused you get when you're so utterly furious you loop right back into accidental laughter.

The tension skyrocketed, and Sairaorg shifted next to me.

A silent countdown had started.

"You wizards and witches really don't know when to shut up and save your miserable lives, do you?"

Augusta matched his off-pitch fury with her own. Her head leaned forward expectantly, and the brim of her hat tilted over her face until it seemed like her eyes were cast in shadows.

They still gleamed, though.

"I don't appreciate the insult."

"Do I look like I care?"

She might've twitched at that.

"That's a refusal, then?"

"What do you think?"

"I see."

Suddenly, she turned back to us.

Her expression cooled some more.

"I'd tell you two infants to leave now that things are getting difficult, but there might be value left to wring from you after all. " She focused on me. "The demigod in particular-"

Regulus roared.

Point-blank, with no warning - a great thundering wave of force and rage that carried the air forward with it and hit like the shockwave of a bomb, tearing through the valley and the ledge Augusta stood on.

It crumbled underneath her, stone breaking apart like glass, dirt blown back into the air, but she barely stumbled after leaping back to avoid the worst of it.

Sairaorg and I didn't move either, beyond bracing for impact.

Not at at first.

The dust cloud swallowed her, until she was almost a silhouette hidden in the falling debris.

Then her voice rang out.

Sharp. Angry.

And fixed in the worst kind of way.

"Fine. We'll do this the hard way."

My eyes widened, and I was already launching an arrow her way even though I knew it was futile - a tongue of purple flames burned it out of the air with a whip-like crack, and then it started to swell.

Damn it.

"Scram!"

We all did - even Regulus. He rounded back and leaped up in a ballistic arc, and Sairaorg and I blinked away out of the valley and up into the air above the greater mountain range.

A second later, it exploded.

Incinerate Anthem's flames ignited like a second sun, and the eruption swallowed the valley in a blink of an eye - then it rose past it.

Trees and greenery turned to dust. Rock glowed red hot or burst like popcorn kernels. The heat jumped a thousand degrees, and the feeling of Holy Power riding it was so thick it felt like the stuff was trying to reach down our throats and punch us in the lungs.

What the hell was this quest!?

Sairaorg cursed, but I could barely hear him, because Augusta voice chose right then to roll across the sky like a thunderbolt even as the glow from her flames tinted everything in shades of violet.

It was unhinged - and we weren't even the targets of it.

Just footnotes and collateral damage

"You want me to get to the point? Have it your way."

Something began to take shape in the growing firestorm below.

Regulus roared again, a thousand times louder, shining golden and bellowing enough that Mount Eyrmanthus seemed to recoil in terror under the force of it, but he only slowed it down.

The flames stuttered and went right back to taking shape - an enormous one.

"Rise, My Fire Giant ."

...Yeah, that just tracked, didn't it?

The shape solidified, and it was just what it said on the tin - a titanic, hundred-foot-tall figure of roiling purple flames with hollow pits for eyes and a crucifix hanging off its back - one that managed to gleam with light that overshadowed the monster carrying it.

"Impress me, Regulus Nemea, and I might leave something of you intact for study."

Credit where credit was due, Regulus didn't back up. His paws slammed against the ground, and another earthquake struck like a viper. The fire giant didn't back up, but the flames that made up its feet wavered and somehow made it stumble.

Actually, no - it didn't stumble.

It deliberately tipped forward and lunged, far faster than anything that size had any right to be, and Regulus became a blur to dodge the literal handfuls of holy flames reaching out to crush him.

Around them, the terrain started to melt.

All the while, the two of us hovered above and watched.

Can you blame us?

Sairaorg glanced at me, just as out of his depth.

"What do we do?"

I could barely hear him over all the carnage.

"We can-"

Honestly, I have no idea what I was going to say there.

I never got to finish anyway.

"Interfere and die? I agree."

Everything - and I mean everything - happened far too fast after that.

Augusta's voice came from everywhere at once, just like before, but my instincts howled this time.

Sairaorg's too, from the way his Touki flared with brilliance - and then we both felt it, right before I saw it out of the corner of my eye.

A human hand, wreathed in even more of those stupid purple flames, lunging right for the back of Sai's neck.

I didn't think - I just moved.

I pushed him away, just about smacking him in the face with my bow, and he went flying off like a comet with a panicked yell.

Idiot move, I know - I should have teleported us - but again, I didn't think.

I just got him out of the way.

Then Augusta's hand - because she'd somehow appeared right behind us, floating on a miniature cyclone of air - caught the end of my bow.

Fire.

It crumbled to cinders in my grip, and the spark caught on.

No-!

Before I could even twitch, the flames covered half my arm and part of my shoulder, burning through my reinforcement and the hoodie underneath - then me.

It burned.

I burned.

Not enough to destroy the limb - The flames winked out and Augusta reared away before that, surprise in her eyes.

She hadn't meant to do that.

Good to know - I barely registered that even as I soared away, and I only did that because the pain didn't hit at first, breathless with fear.

"I-"

Then it did, all at once.

"▅▅▅▂▅▂▄▅▃▃▄"

Everything blanked out except for the sensation of sheer, brain-stabbing cold - why was it cold? - spreading across the burns I couldn't even look at through my suddenly blurry vision.

The Holy Power was overwhelming on top of it - it felt like it was trying to snuff the part of me that it hated most of all.

The divinity I got from my dad.

Then the burns started pulsing.

A long, tortured, and keening rasp crawling its way out of my throat without a hint of grace or dignity.

I nearly toppled right out of the sky, I couldn't even think or do anything - Augusta could have killed me right then and there, and I wouldn't have even seen it coming.

Maybe she could have tried, too, except Sairaorg took one look at me and went absolutely berserk.

His eyes went white with fury. His muscles swelled and heaved, and his spiritual presence detonated.

It slammed into us like a tidal wave, and things got weird.

Air pressure changed. Light twisted oddly. The clouds rumbled and thundered overhead overhead. Down beneath us, the wildlife that was being torn apart by Regulus or reduced to ashes by the Holy Fire Giant twisted unnaturally. Some of it decayed and fell apart.

Other plants erupted out of the ground in absurd bursts, vines and weeds and roots growing explosively before collapsing and being torn apart under their own unsustainable weight.

The part of me that was trying not to splutter out into unconsciousness and fall to a fiery death below knew what it was.

It was a messy, uncontrolled sneak-peak into the true potential of Senjutsu - the manipulation of the world's natural energies and phenomena by way of the spirit.

Too bad I couldn't enjoy it through the haze of mortal agony, but good for Sai anyway, right?

Surprise, surprise, but Augusta didn't think so.

"At least have the dignity to die quietly!" She snapped, and her hand caught fire as Sairarog bull-rushed her like he meant to rip her in half with his bare hands.

If it wasn't for the Hoy Flames ready to surge his way, he probably could have.

No.

Somehow, I found the strength to move.

To focus.

It was the hardest thing I've ever done - I hurt in a way that pretty much redefined the word form.

Zero stars, and worth a terrible Yelp review.

But I managed it.

Remember step two?

The one that needed time?

Augusta was stronger than us. Leagues stronger than us - or at least flat-out more dangerous by way of the Sacred Gear.

But that didn't mean one good hit that bypassed that wouldn't take her down - she was still mortal. Just one, because that was all the chances she'd give us.

Fine.

Back down on the ground, just past the valley where Regulus had deflected it and sent it flying to before, a speck of light that I'd been focusing my power on glinted and shone red-gold.

Probably for the best. Incinerate Anthem would have destroyed it otherwise.

Augusta didn't notice it, at first.

Too busy preparing to dust Sai as he rocketed her way, fist cocked back and promising bloody murder.

She did notice it when I pointed her finger my way, but by then I was already grinning like a lunatic from sheer pain and snarling at her.

"Archer's Support!"

The spell kicked in, and Serpent's Downfall came hurling up through the air, propelled by its own miniature inferno and gaining speed with every passing second. By the time it was right under us - less than a second after it took off, the inferno of cursed flames was half the size of Augusta's Fire Giant.

And for the first time since this started, I saw her panic.

Sairaorg ducked under the whip of holy flames she threw his way, and she threw up about a hundred spell circles in an instant, layered in terrifying synergy.

That was her biggest mistake - she should have focused on Sairaorg, because he hadn't thrown his punch yet.

Then he was suddenly right there, next to her, and doing just that.

The universe seemed to warp around his fist as he did, reality glitched - or maybe that was my brain threatening to pass out from the burn I was still only beginning to feel - and Augusta's shields shattered like glass with a cataclysmic implosion.

"No!"

Too late.

Even as she tried to dodge out of the way, Serpent's Downfall found its mark.

We didn't stick around to see it happen.

A blink, and we reappeared a mile away as, for the second time in as many minutes, everything from one end of our line of the sight to next detonated into a fiery nightmare that burned the sky itself.

That was the good news.

A moment later, the feeling of overwhelming Holy Power in the air dropped like it'd just jumped off a cliff. In the distance, Regulus's roars also abruptly cut out as the Fire Giant collapsed.

Like a puppet with its strings cut, it just tumbled over, and the flames dispersed and winked out in the eerie silence that followed.

That was the better news.

Bad news time - the second we teleported, I finally lost the fight and started falling out of the sky.

"Dan!"

Nope, sorry.

Your Daniel Winchester program is currently experiencing technical difficulties - please try again when even the air brushing past my slow-roasted limb doesn't feel like an active war crime.

Unfortunately, Sai didn't get the memo.

He shot down and reached out to grab me as I tumbled towards the earth ground, whatever sound came out of my throat when he unthinkingly latched onto my bad arm was more unholy than all seventy-two devil pillars families down in hell, and then some.

It was so bad - and accidentally power-boosted - that he nearly dropped down with me.

My bad, but I was more focused on my arm and whydoesitstillburncold?

It wasn't pretty.

Just because I couldn't look at it didn't mean I couldn't feel it.

That was all I could feel.

I'm not sure how he got us back to the ground after that, because things got a little fuzzy, but by the time I tuned back in, he was rummaging through his pocket desperately and only just keeping me standing by the grip he had on my good-shoulder.

The less said about the other one, the better.

"Got it!" He tore the summoning flyer out of his pocket and lit it up with "Anton's on his way."

"Bet he is." Talking was good. It was distracting enough that I could go at it until the creeping unconsciousness caught up to me and I didn't have to focus on why my vision was going black at the edges. "His Lord Sairaorg is calling for him. He's gotta come running."

Did I sound a little slurred?

Probably did.

"...Really?" He was starting to sound strange - faraway and distant. "Now?"

"Sai, my whole arm and a part my back both look and feel like undercooked rotisserie chicken. Including the one time a hellhound nearly disemboweled me, I am literally in the worst pain of my life." I glared at him - or tried to. My eyes kept flickering open and closed, and everything seemed to be spinning like a yo-yo "Let me have this."

"...Sure."

"Hah! No take-backs forever, sucker!"

As if to agree with me, the shadows at my feet bubbled, and out popped Courage.

I genuinely forgot about him there.

"Hey buddy. Where'd you come from?"

He didn't bark at me the way he was supposed to - instead, he sniffled at me before recoiling at the sight of my arm.

Real encouraging, that.

"Thanks-"

Sai suddenly cursed, letting go of me and punching forward without warning.

"Yo-uu wretches. G-i-ve it bac-k!"

Oh, for the love of dad!

Augusta was suddenly present - somehow - and shimmering into view in front of us.

The wave of destructive power nearly threw her off her feet, but I'm guessing she held on by sheer spite, because that was all she had still going for her.

Her clothes were blackened rags clinging to burned flesh. The right side of her body looked like overcooked lobster, and the left was halfway gone with her arm missing entirely and part of her face eaten away like something had taken a bite out of it. The eye there was gone too, and I'm pretty sure it was dripping down her side like bubbling goo.

Even her hair had burned away, leaving a mess of boiled flesh that popped and blistered in real time.

The smell of it was awful.

The one eye she had left was clouded in what had to be more pain than I was feeling - and let me tell you, that was an achievement - and enough hysterical madness to put evil gods and dragons to shame.

"How are you even alive?"

She didn't answer. I don't think she could even speak anymore - her tongue seemed to be burning in her own mouth.

"D-d-i-ie!"

Never mind. She still had the important stuff down.

... I feel loopy.

She scrambled towards us, but Sai's second force-punch tore her off the ground sent her flipping back with an audible snap.

Even then, she didn't die.

Her hands started scrapping against the dirt as she tried to pull herself back up again, and bits of her were actively breaking off under the strain.

It was messed up.

Even Sai stepped back a little, looking green.

Why wasn't she dying?

Like she'd heard the thought, her eye slowly panned back up to me.

Utter malice beyond what should have been humanely possible raged there.

"K-ill y-o-uo!"

"Enough."

I didn't even question it anymore.

Neither did Sai.

We just watched on as a golden blur leaped out of the acrid smoke behind her and descended on her like the hammer of a vengeful god. Augusta never saw Regulus's paw coming until it shattered her skull like an egg and finally put her out of her misery.

The sound echoed out between us before petering out.

"..."

"..."

"..."

"Man, you're just a professional kill-stealer, aren't you?"

Sai choked.

The lion stared at me silently, then tilted his head in quiet consideration.

"You don't know when to shut up either, do you?"

"Nope!" I said cheerily, and then reached and recalled Serpent's Downfall, just in case I needed it. "But at least I don't monologue."

Or at least that's what I think I said.

I really can't remember anymore.

I do remember the familiar teleportation circle lighting up between us, but only after my spear came hurling back out of the air.

I moved to catch out on some god-forsaken reflex, only I did it with my burned hand, and it smacked right into my palm full force the way it always did.

That took me to my knees with a scream so strangled it was barely more than a whisper, and everything else just about whited out.

But not enough that I didn't feel Serpent's Downfall... tremble in my grip, like something in the wood was bouncing against the walls and trying to get out.

Before it even slipped from my mangled fingers, whatever it was raging inside the spear surged out of it like off-purple smoke and leaped up through my arm and into my everything.

I couldn't have fought it even if I tried, and something inside my chest clicked into place.

Almost on cue, Courage recoiled and started barking up a storm.

Huh.

Wonder what that's about?

Sairaorg yelled out something garbled, and it sounded it like he was underwater. I managed to look up right as Chiron and Anton stepped out of the circle, eyes wide.

Hey, that's good.

I even managed to smile.

"Hey Teach. You're right on time."

Then I pitched forward and promptly blacked out.

...​

Extra:

By the time the goddess appeared in Chiron's home, about half-hour later, Sairaorg barely even reacted

He felt... hollow.

Exhausted in that special kind of way people get when they feel to much too fast and then crash down from that emotional rollercoaster all at once.

Artemis appeared in the entry hall between one blink and the next, their presence subtle but blatantly solid in a way that was hard to describe. His Senjutsu pinged off her like a metal detector gone haywire.

"Lady Artemis."

She didn't wait for him to bow.

"My nephew?"

How a question could come off as both that and a command so effortlessly, he didn't know.

Didn't much care right this second either.

"Chiron's healing him."

He said he'd be fine. Dan would be fine.

...

He pushed him out of the way.

His fists tightened.

If Artemis noticed, she made no mention of it.

"Good."

A pause.

"What happened?"

Before he could even try to answer, she raised a hand dismissively.

"Never mind. I'll get it from Chiron." Her silver eyes looked him up and down, expression unreadable. "And just to be safe, you should make yourself scarce. Now."

He... blinked.

"Why?"

For future reference, questioning a god or goddess is a special kind of stupid nine times out of ten.

This time, though, he got a straight answer.

But not from Artemis.

Nobody appeared in front of his eyes, but another presence slammed down from above like judgment day had come calling.

Fiery. Overwhelming.

And furious beyond all comprehension.

"WHO D̶̡̡̧̛̮̗̭͔͈̲͎̺͎̗͖͔͓̙̱̲̞̜̜̥̦́͊͛͑̈̇͑̾͌̎̉͒̀̊̄̊͛̕͠A̴̪̺̺̹̣͆̎̋̓̈́͑͗̈́͘R̷̨̛̛̯̝̈́̓̈̍̽͌͗̂̀̃̆̓̀̇͑̑̊̏̿̀̈́͒̀̓̎̆͘̚͠͝Ḙ̶̛̻͙̬̹̟͇͓͕̪̼͚̫͂̔̈͑̀̽͆́̂̂̅͛̽̀͂͂́̃̽̿͋̀̄͝͝D̶̡̡̛̪̭̺̠͓̻̥̪̗̹̲͔̩͉͍̝̙̹̣̟͎̩̙̦̹̪̗̊̀͌̉̉̎̔͗͒͂͆̈́́͑͒̎̿́̓͒͑͊̃̆͌̌͐̓̽̐͆̿̀͘͜͠͝͝ͅ -"

It reeled back and contained itself just as quickly as it had struck, which was good, because just those two words had nearly blasted Sairarog''s mind to smithereens.

He didn't even notice he was on the ground and gasping desperately until he blinked and realized that his forehead was pressed against the marble floor.

Artemis just looked resigned.

"Because of that."

"...Oh."

"Quite." she sighed. "This is going to be a long day."

...
