#1,286
Between the new summer schedule, RL responsibilities, and everything in between, writing this chapter kicked my ass.

On a brighter note, the Quest (The real one this time) should kick off next chapter!
I've mentioned this before, but, as a general rule of thumb, I'm a pretty light sleeper.

Some of it was hardwired instinct, and a part of the demigod package - like the ADHD. Just a symptom of that whole "Gotta keep moving so I don't die in any of various messy ways'' thing we had going for us, and honestly?

Probably for the best - some of it could be a total pain sometimes, but ending up as some random monster-of-the-week's morning or late-night snack because you picked a bad spot to get some shut-eye wouldn't just be tragic, but plain embarrassing.

Here lies Chucky Mcgee, son of what's-his-name.
Got munched on by a hydra while trying to catch some z's, the dumb schmuck.
RIP.

Seriously, nobody wants something like that written on their tombstone.

Another part of it was just plain old training - the number of times Chiron's dragged or had us dragged out of bed at ungodly hours of the night and in new and different - read: traumatizing - ways every time to get us to think fast or get smacked around like you wouldn't believe pretty much blurred together after a while.

On the bright side, it got the job done - most people trying to sneak up on me wouldn't be able to breathe in my general direction without more than even odds of it waking me right the hell up.

On the not-so-bright side, sometimes I could get a little... twitchy.

Sairaorg tried to nudge me awake this one time after I took a nap in the afternoon sun, and I nearly stabbed him through with Serpent's Downfall on sheer reflex.

Eh, nobody's perfect.

The point is, I usually wake up quickly.

Bink a couple of times, take a quick breath, and I'm ready to go - or dodge.

Whatever comes first.

This time, though, things started off a little differently.

I came back up to the land of the living slowly - almost lazily, if that was even the right word for it - and the first thing I clocked was the slow, pleasant warmth seeping through me from head to toe and back again, like the feeling you get when you down a mug of hot chocolate on a cold and snowy day, but somehow even better.

Then I heard the music - not a hit song or an ear-worm tune or anything crazy special like that, but this high and crisp noted melody that nudged me awake a couple of steps at a time and hit me with... well, I couldn't really tell you, but if good vibes were a musical piece, that'd be what I was listening to right then and there.

Finally, I blinked my eyes open to the sight of the ceiling I'd been sleeping under for over eight months and shifted in bed- my bed, I realized a little belatedly, but that only made sense, didn't it?

Where else would I be?

Then the music paused, and my eyes flickered to the side.

There was a familiar figure sitting there, carefully holding on to my gold and silver harp and staring at me carefully.

He was even sitting in the same chair as before, the totally-not-a-throne that he carted around for dramatic effect.

To be fair though, pulling fancy furniture out of thin air wasn't the worst thing a god could do to show off - and if we're going by classic Olympian standards alone, if no one's dying and no crimes against nature are actively being committed, you're about as in the clear as you're ever going to get.

"...Dad?"

Apollon smiled in greeting, and the expression was... real in a way that was hard to describe though the fuzzy post-sleep filter still stuck to my brain.

Fond and pleased, but also carefully measured - like it was designed not to be overwhelming on purpose.

"Good morning, son." He leaned over and put the harp back on my bedside table, next to a jug of water and a glass I couldn't remember putting there myself. "Awake at last, are we?"

"Mhm. Morning."

I slumped back against the pillow and blearily rubbed at my eyes. I felt slow - What time did I get in last night?

"What're you doing here?"

"Checking in on you. Oh, and admiring your instrument. Beautiful craftsmanship, and well-tuned too. Quite the prize."

As he spoke, the aura of sunlight and the warmth I'd been feeling pulled back, though it took its sweet time and lingered enough that the change wasn't abrupt.

Guess that explained that, at least.

"Thanks." I yawned under my breath as I raised my hands over my head in a sluggish stretch. "I got it from Smaug's-"

...

Wait, hold up, what?

My head snapped back over to him, meeting his bemused smile, and that was about the point where I really finished waking up, registered exactly who I was talking to and where, and nearly short-circuited on the spot.

Apollon.

By my bedside.

Right there.

My jaw dropped, and he grinned wryly.

"There it is."

I jumped off the bed.

Well, actually, jumped is a strong word. It was more like... very enthusiastic flailing in no particular direction at all, complete with a high-pitched yelp I'd take to my grave and a burst of medical-grade adrenaline that had me almost cartwheeling halfway across the room and nearly face-planting after getting tangled in my own covers like a total clown.

I'd tell you that it wasn't as embarrassing as it sounded, but come on - you know I'd be lying. I've seen and laughed at cartoon flicks that were more dignified than I was right then.

In my defense though...

What the actual hell is this?

"Da-?" The word died in my throat - the same way a part of me did in absolute mortification and something close to panic when I remembered that I'd called him that to his face. "My l- Apollon. Sir."

Damn it.

I swear it took real effort not to cringe as I looked him in the eye and willed myself to keep a straight face, and not just because I fumbled three times trying to look for the right word.

There's a rude awakening, and then there's the stuff that's just outright a hazard to your mental well-being.

I'll give you three guesses which one whatever was happening now was, and the first two don't count.

"There's no need for that." His smile didn't dim, exactly, but it went a little exasperated at the edges - that, or tired. "I've already told you that you don't need to stand on that kind of formality with me."

"...Right. I'll... remember that."

I lied with a smile so fake you'd think it was made of plastic - or at least an attempt at one that probably came out more wary and helplessly confused than anything else.

Not my best work, I know, but it couldn't be helped - my heart was still beating just a little too quickly for comfort, and for all that his presence was non-threatening and mind-trippingly easygoing, it still had my instincts manning all stations and running pre-flight checks in case things got messy.

If Apollon noticed, he didn't show it.

Credit where credit was due and all, because he had a celestial bronze-grade poker face.

"Uh... can I ask...?"

Why in literally any other god's name are you in my room?

I didn't say that aloud - mostly because you couldn't pay me to take that tone with him, parent or no - but he beat me to the punch anyway before I could think of a better way to phrase it.

"What do you remember?"

I blinked.

"Remember?"

"From your little quest, and your battle with the-" His expression darkened mid-word, so quickly and dangerously that I had to fight the urge not to flinch back at once. "-witch."

Wit-?

Boom.

Just like that - like a switch had suddenly been flipped - it all came rushing back to me.

Quest.

Regulus and the Wizards of Oz.

Augusta.

Well, what do you know?

A second ago I'd have never believed that anything could make me forget about Apollon ever existing in the same space as me for any length of time ever, but that sure did it, because I turned on the spot and scrambled for the mirror hanging against the wall like it owed me money.

I didn't even bother rolling up my sleeve, either - the phantom memory of my arm lighting on fire kind of pressed the issue a little too much for just that, and I ended up yanking the shirt clean off to stare at my...

...

...Completely unblemished skin?

"What?"

I stared at the limb like it didn't belong to me, because the last time I'd seen it - just this one glance out of the corner of my eye, followed by a whole bucket of solid nope - it looked more like a pricey Halloween prop that had somehow ended up on the wrong side of an angry blowtorch, or else something that would have had Frankenstein's monster trying to sue me for cribbing on his style.

I'm not even going to think about how it felt, either.

Now, though?

Normal.

Completely and totally.

I rolled it at the shoulder, clenching and unclenching my fingers easily. I even poked and ran over it with my good hand - the other one, at least, and it felt just as peachy as it looked, the skin and muscle underneath exactly what they were supposed to be.

Tip-top shape all around, like I'd never been injured at all.

"Holy crap," I whispered, and it was more reflex than anything.

"Holy, yes."

The words carried through - not that they really had to. Apollon could probably hear a mouse fart twenty miles down the road if he wanted to.

"Crap, though? I'd hope not. I'll have you know I take great pride in my skills as a healer."

He sounded lightly amused, and when I remembered I probably shouldn't keep my back to him and quickly turned back over, he looked like it too.

That, and patient.

Waiting.

I quickly put my shirt back on and coughed.

"You healed me?"

Obvious question, I know, but walking on eggshells around him and triple-checking every word coming out of my mouth was just the way I roll at this point.

That, and I was divided between so many other questions I didn't even really know where to start.

What happened after I blacked out, and how long was I out of it

Where'd Sairaorg and Courage get off to?

Why are we currently sharing a zip code and what can I do to change that?

The last one was for the bonus points, and my blood pressure.

"Of course I did." He nodded easily. "Chiron would have managed just as well, if in a little more time than I would have, but I took over the moment I arrived." He shrugged, but he didn't stop looking me right in the eyes. "Wounds caused by divine weapons and armaments - lethal or otherwise - are thaumaturgically and spiritually complex at minimum, and often abhorrently brutal in their effectiveness and long-term impact as a matter of principle. And those are just the standard examples - an Abrahamic Longinus, the one that you faced in particular-"

He shook his head, firmly and with a flash of something too quick for me to recognize - and that was an achievement right there because I was watching him like a freaking hawk the whole time.

"Your being a demigod did you no favors there. I have absolute faith in your teacher's prowess and sheer competence, but some things I refuse to leave to any kind of chance at all, no matter how slim."

There was a pause, and I nodded slowly as I took that in.

It made... sense.

"But how did you even know-?"

Ok, not an obvious question this time - a blatantly stupid one.

Chiron, obviously - and getting Apollon's attention when you were someone on my teacher's level was probably as easy as shooting a prayer his way and holding your breath.

He raised a brow at the second pause - awkward, I'll tell you that much - but he stepped right over it in the next beat.

"How are you feeling?"

Peachy. Like sunshine and roses.

"That's good."

"Indeed."

And see, that's where things got a little weird.

I was going to thank him - two words, easy like nobody's business, but when I opened my mouth, they kind of... stuck.

I don't even know why, but between the look on his face and the memory of Incinerate Anthem's fire lancing up my arm, it felt like I was trying to talk through a brick wall someone had built into my throat when I wasn't looking, and the silence just stretched from there.

A second passed.

Then another one.

At about the fifth - that being the point where I was ready to start considering the pros and cons of outright praying for my brain to get with the program, and screw the irony - he rose from his seat.

I tensed, also on reflex, and then I may as well have turned into concrete all the way through when he stepped forward, materialized right in front of me mid-step, and put his hand on my shoulder.

"I'm glad you're safe." He murmured, and, see, I didn't know what to do with the gentle warmth in his tone - the emotional whiplash was going to make me break out in hives at this rate. "I heard the story from your… friend-"

The split-second and almost grudging pause was definitely there, but it didn't linger.

"-and I'm most impressed." His smile curved upwards, bright and proud. "You continue to grow in leaps and bounds."

I stared at him slowly.

"I nearly got flash-fried by the world's most dangerous pyromaniac."

And just remembering that very much not dearly departed psycho - and the way she died - was going to make any future therapist of mine rich as sin... and leave them with all kinds of fresh issues of their own, probably, but if I can live with it, so can they, right?

Right?

Questions for later.

Apollon's expression strained at the edges at 'blink and you'd miss it' speeds, and the air got a little warmer.

Weirdly enough, it wasn't threatening.

Not to me, at least, and not any more than anything else I'd ever seen or felt him do.

"I'm aware. And I'll be… looking into that, in due time." Ominous. With a capital O - and I mean both the words and the look that passed over his face. "But a victory is a victory all the same, and you lived to tell the tale."

True.

The Ancient Greek Hero policy for victory in battle or war pretty much always boiled down to 'if you're alive at the end of it and in possession of most - if not necessarily all - of your bodily functions, you done good kid.'

Things could get messy after the whole surviving part was done and dusted, for all sorts of different reasons, but getting to that finish line first was kind of the priority.

Technically, I came out better than almost everyone in the really bad old stories - not a scratch on me, courtesy of literal divine intervention.

Still, it hadn't been so much a fight as it was twenty seconds of pure 'movemovemove', and a sneak attack I'd managed to land by the skin of my nearly barbecued teeth - and not on my own, either.

"It was a team effort," I admitted without shame. "I couldn't have done it without Sairaorg."

And that was the honest truth too, because - now that I thought about it again - that last punch?

The one that had shattered Augusta's shields before she could defend herself from Serpent's Downfall?

That had been something else - completely unhinged and off all the rails, a solid twelve out of ten.

He'd gotten even stronger than I think either of us had realized.

If I weren't where I was right then, I'd have probably grinned.

Good.

And speaking of ludicrous power in my immediate vicinity-

"Indeed."

Apollo's finally pulled back and let his hand drop off my shoulder, before moving to adjust his cufflinks with an easy, obviously practiced motion.

"Despite the reservations I may or may not have had stacked against him, your... friend continues to prove his worth."

Again, he said friend with the energy of someone who'd looked for and used so many other words for something they ended up burning out and rolling right back around to the original - like a tired, sort of begrudging compromise.

Which was more than fine over in this corner - compromises were cool.

I'd take what I could get, and Sairaorg would too.

"Granted, the bar I set for the rest of his kind is so low an ordinary earthworm could clear it in a single leap, but you'd be amazed how few of them ever really-" He paused and shook his head. "But that's another topic all on its own - we have more important things to cover."

"So he's alright?"

He shouldn't be anything but alright - he hadn't been hit, I'd made sure of that - but with our track record being what it was, you can never know for sure.

Sometimes it felt like fate and karma were just waiting around the corner with a bat and a couple dozen curveballs ready to go at the drop of a hat.

Apollon huffed an amused breath.

"I'm fairly sure he's currently out in the forest with Chiron and your new guest."

Cool.

Also, what?

"Guest?"

"The Nemean Lion."

I stared at him again - and I really had to stop doing that, but stopping to parse through this stuff was almost an ingrained reaction at this point.

"Regulus is here."

I thought about that for a split second and… it made some sense in the context of the future that would have played out who knows how many years down the line from now, but not so much in the present.

We'd had a single two-minute conversation, and then he tried to disembowel us.

Or maybe not, because he clearly hadn't been going anywhere close to all out while he was at it, but I'd buy a hat and eat it too if he wasn't having fun playing with his food - that being us.

I resisted the urge to scowl.

Cats - you could never tell with any of them. One second they're all regal and stuff, and the next they're screeching like hellspawn that put Sairaorg to shame and trying to claw your eyes out, the contrary jerks.

And this cat in particular…

"Your teacher invited him," Apollon explained, eyes flickering past me to the window and back. "The disruptions at Mount Eyrmanthus had to stop, or we would have personally gotten involved eventually. There are limits to what even a beast such as himself can get up to - or be allowed to - embodied Longinus or not.

He frowned at that even as he spoke.

"And that's another thing I'll have to look into in time."

I took that all in quickly.

"So he's just living out in the forest now? That's it?"

Why?

I mean, I kind of get it - being jumped by the gods because you were mucking about in their backyard and threatening to make a real nuisance of yourself was no one's idea of a good time, even if Regulus could make himself a lot worse than just a nuisance.

That doesn't mean he would want to - Hercules had ganked him way back when, and as big a deal as he was, the Olympians were even bigger. Looking for a fight with them after finally slipping the leash that had chained him to Heaven's System for thousands of years was probably right at the top of his 'When hell freezes over' and 'But why though?' lists.

But why come here?

Apollon must have read the question right off my face.

"I imagine he had no taste left for the place himself. Boar hunting is a game that dulls quickly, and the mountain range he terrorised likely lost its luster when he had his revenge. Chiron offered him a to put an end to the complicated mess, once and for all."

"So... that's it, then?"

Mission accomplished, just like that?

"Until he becomes a problem again, which he very nearly was, I am content to let the matter drop for now. Artemis is too, so all's well that ends well."

Then his eyes narrowed.

"Had he harmed you, rest assured that I would have been remarkably less content to sleeping dogs lie." He paused and tilted his head to the side. "Or lions, I suppose, but then we'd just be arguing semantics."

…huh.

I nodded slowly - and I actually believed him.

Not sure what to do with that realization either, so I shelved it and shrugged as casually as I could, given the circumstances.

"So now what?"

There was a pause, long and pointed.

Then the god sighed, and something about the sound put me right back on edge again.

"You've been out for about a day and a half."

I started.

"That long?"

"Healing you took only a fraction the time." Apollon offered, before sighing and pinching the bridge of his nose like he was trying to brace himself. "It was because of the other complication that I kept you under."

And there were the ringing alarm bells going off at the back of my head - I'd almost missed the damned things.

"Complication?"

If I suddenly sounded a little high-pitched, sue me. That's not a word you ever want to hear the literal god of healing say to your face.

Ever.

In response, Apollon inhaled before raising his head and looking me right in the eye.

Somehow, I managed not to jerk back from the intensity roiling around in there.

"Incinerate Anthem."

...

"What- oh."

I didn't even get halfway through asking before the memory hit me like a gut punch from the devil - and not Sairaorg this time.

In those last few minutes after Augusta's spectacularly gruesome death and the moment that I blacked right the hell out, I'd recalled Serpent's Downfall and nearly whited out from the pain.

But I'd still been conscious enough to feel my spear treble in my grip, and then I felt something else entirely flitting from it to me, and now that I wasn't in a whole new dimension of unspeakable fiery pain, the pieces clicked into place like clockwork.

My eyes went wide.

I knew exactly what Apollon - and all of it - meant.

After all, from all the lectures and the reading Chiron had made us sit through - and ignoring Regulus's whole irregular situation - Incinerate Anthem was pretty much the only Independent-Avatar class sacred gear on record known to be capable of leaving one user behind for another.

"Oh."

Instinctively, I closed my eyes and reached inwards the way I always did when I called up my divine power - only this time, I wasn't looking for the familiar warmth of sun-themed divinity.

I was looking for anything but that - and It only took me a second to notice it.

Power - only it wasn't mine.

Searing heat, and foreign power.

Holy power, and purple flames, and-

Damn it.

When I opened my eyes again, they were so wide the expression on my face was downright painful, the phantom image of a burning cross locked into place inside me and patiently waiting for just the tiniest poke or prod to come bursting right back out into the world on the double.

"Oh, God."

Apollon took that reaction in for all of a second before snorting and nodding sagely.

"That is the idea."

Great. More corny jokes.

Because that's exactly what this circus needed.

...​

"Let's begin, then."

So.

I didn't freak out.

That doesn't sound all that impressive on paper, since demigod heroes were supposed to be made of sterner stuff than regular mortals and all, but I think I deserve a few props for keeping a straight face after processing the fact that the sacred gear that had nearly, you know, incinerated my arm not two days ago on the dot had ended up using my spear as a glorified taxi service and latched onto my soul like something out of a supernatural lego kit.

Since no amount of panicked flailing and losing my cool would be enough to do all the nightmare scenarios popping into my head like pop rocks justice, I might as well not waste time getting hung up on any of them to begin with

That's maybe the smartest thing you've ever heard me say, I know, but none of my post-emergency practicality meant that I wasn't tense about all of this - and by tense, I mean I was hyper-friggin-aware of the fact that I had a pretty good example of the Abrahamic equivalent of nuclear ordinance wired into me from that second and every other one afterward.

Sounds fun, right?

"Breathe."

Apollon stood across from me, arms leisurely folded behind his back as he looked me over. The early morning sun rose up behind him and ended up framing him in a way that almost had to be deliberate, golden light and faint shadows cast against the backdrop of the garden right outside the house.

Very on the nose and everything - but not exactly helpful.

Needing the fresh air was the bonus perk of us taking this second walk out in the open, but the point was supposed to be figuring out what was supposed to come next, and having him stand there like a peppy gym coach with the most generic advice you could possibly aim someone's way was doing jack for me.

"I am breathing. All I'm doing is breathing."

He raised a brow my way, and I belatedly realized that I'd just talked back to him.

Crap.

"Sorry?"

"Don't apologize." He chided gently. "And don't push yourself. We have plenty of time."

That's where we'd have to disagree.

He was immortal - I very much wasn't, and I currently had a weapon of biblical mass destruction settling in to live rent-free inside of me after it jumped ship mid-fight without so much as knocking.

Sure, odds are I'd have locked the door and pretended not to be home if it had - at least at first, maybe - but it was the principle of the thing.

Having it just sit there in my soul playing high-stakes possum felt like having invisible hands strumming my nerves like guitar strings.

"Focus."

Right.

This shouldn't be hard.

Just a spark would do the trick.

I held out a hand in front of me and pulled on that foreign feeling I'd just found a little while ago, trying to gently coax it-

My hand went up in purple flames.

I flinched back so hard that my spine nearly cried uncle, and the flames winked out.

"Mother-!"

"Calm." Apollon's voice rolled over the air, heavy but not oppressive. The opposite, almost. "Don't let it startle you. You almost had it."

Little late for that, pops - my heart nearly beat the Olympic record for high jumps with how badly it jerked there, and for good reason.

That had been absurdly quick.

"I'm fine." I swallowed and cleared my throat, trying to play it off. "Just… terrible deja vu."

"Ah. I see."

He didn't tell me to stop trying, but I got the feeling that he wouldn't blink twice if I asked.

He might have even been waiting for it, too, because that last pause stretched a little too long for comfort.

Naturally, that made me buckle up and double down - Because I'm all kinds of contrary like that.

"I'm fine." I wasn't, duh, but 'fake it till you make it' was a classic for a reason. "Here goes."

My fingers spasmed as I centered myself and tried again, pulling on the otherness I was quickly getting more and more familiar with and, just like before, it chose to play ball and came surging outwards like a dog called to heel.

Whoosh.

Purple fire burst into existence again, almost eagerly, and this time I locked myself in place out of pure spite even as the flames covered one hand and then the other like they were swallowing up kindling doused and soaked through with kerosene.

Don't move

I kept my feet planted and my back straight, before focusing on the light show I was bringing to the surface with every passing second.

Controlling Incinerate Anthem's flames wasn't instinctive, like with my sunlight.

They didn't fight me or try to buck against the reins I was trying to loop around them, but I needed to put in a kind of conscious effort I'd never had to before.

Slow, and steady.

The flames warped. For a second, I could have sworn I felt... resistance, almost, like they didn't like that.

Like the gear didn't like that.

For all I knew, it probably didn't.

Great. Off to an awesome start already.

Then it happened again when I tried to push.

Not violent. Not messy.

But bucking against invisible restraints.

The flames started surging higher, and I unclenched my literally fiery fists and swallowed down the frustration beginning to well up in me before it fed into them and made everything spiral into something messy.

Sacred Gears are intuitive like that, aren't they?

Chiron still hadn't let me live down the flower bed incident - I didn't want to find out what would happen if I set the whole forest on fire, and let's not even talk about the house.

A minute passed.

Then two.

Three.

You get the idea.

"Steady." Apollon voice carried over, even if he made no move to step closer. "Affirm your control."

I'm trying here, I wanted to say, but nearly every bit of my attention was divided between watching the flames like a hawk and trying to reach for the sacred gear nestled inside of me with every ounce of control I could muster.

Come on!

A stray spark caught my eye, and I belatedly realized that there were little flecks of gold in there, mixed in with all the crackled violets and purples.

Familiar gold - my gold.

...

"Huh," I whispered, tilting my head a little to the side. "How about that?"

That's my power in there too.

Somehow, clicking that piece into place made something else inside of me straighten and sharpen at attention all at once.

Simmer down, I thought, then I commanded it aloud for good measure.

"Now."

Instantly, the flames shrank. The glow died down, and the heat dropped twenty degrees so abruptly that I only just clocked in on the fact that the temperature had been getting to me, beads of sweat running down my skin.

What an odd feeling.

"Better. Now dismiss them."

"Way ahead of you," I muttered under my breath, inhaling lightly before I willed them to die out. "And scene."

Like flipping a switch, they just vanished, and so did the aftertaste of Abrahamic Holiness.

No pressure, no recoil, no muss, or any kind of fuss.

It was almost eerie how quietly they faded away, though I probably couldn't tell you exactly why off the top of my head.

You had to be there, I guess.

"Well, I suppose it's official now." When I glanced up at him again, Apollon looked downright proud, even if he was quiet about it. Restrained, even. "The Holy Cross is undeniably yours. Congratulations are due."

That was….

"Are they?"

The question slipped out of me almost automatically, and Apollon paused, before looking at me funny.

"You tell me."

Figures.

I went to answer, and then I hesitated.

I know that, in theory, this was a good thing.

Not to beat on the dead horse here or anything, but this was a Longinus. - A shiny gizmo that would make almost anyone not already a monster of power in this world green with envy, assuming they weren't an absolute idiot who wouldn't know how to use it properly.

No, actually, scratch that - even an idiot could get plenty far with one of these, because almost all of them seemed to run on plug-and-play rules once you figured out how to tap into them.

All of that was true.

But...

"It's not really mine though, is it?"

Sure it was a force multiplier and a terrifying boost all wrapped up into one, but even getting past how flat-out dangerous this thing was, and how unreliable a weapon that could up and decide to ditch you halfway through a fight for whatever reason it felt like rolling with was - cough, Augusta, cough - it still boiled down to this one sticking point that stood out like a sore thumb.

"I guess just it feels like a cheat," I muttered and awkwardly rubbed the back of my head. "All this time training and I just get... handed a weapon like this?"

I liked getting stronger, but this wasn't like that.

I worked for all my other skills and tricks - this was just pure luck dialed up to eleven.

His brow rose as he took that it.

"You were hardly handed it, though I'll admit that circumstances worked out in just the right way for you to come out ahead, injuries notwithstanding." Pretty sure we both almost winced there. "And I'm fairly certain Chiron makes it a point to teach his students-"

"I know, I know." Ordinarily, I'd have never interrupted him, but the more time I spent around him, the harder it was to keep my hackles up without good reason. "A tool is a tool, and it's better to have the advantage and be safe than sorry."

It's why Sairaorg still trained with his weapons and took to his axe like a duck to water even if he preferred using his fists over any of them.

"But it's different when the tool is a god-killing weapon," I argued, running a hand through my hair. "I'm not in that weight class - not even close - and I don't want to get there because a Longinus carried me there."

Regulus had said something to Augusta, back in that valley.

About how Longinus wielders he'd met over the years had lucked out in ending up with one of them and let it go to their heads so far and so fast that they came out the other end as total tools, and not half as impressive as they actually thought the were.

I don't want that to be me - not that it ever would be, because I'm not an idiot, but... it still felt scummy.

Apollon just nodded knowingly.

"You want to get there on your own merits, do you?"

"Pretty much? I guess?"

"And should I be concerned that my son apparently wants to grow to kill gods himself, then? Deicide is a very tricky business, I'll tell you that much."

"Wait, no! That's not what I-"

Abruptly, he laughed.

"I know what you meant, and I am proud." That sent another jolt through me, and keeping a straight face suddenly became that much harder. "And if it makes you feel better, that new gear of yours is a 'Longinus' in name only, given that it has never actually been used to kill a god of great power in its own right."

What?

"What?"

"Oh yes." He chuckled after dropping that one on me. "Regardless of the propaganda, of all thirteen Longinus class Sacred Gears in existence, only five of them have been used to kill gods of significant, notable power."

He even held up a hand and started counting them off for good measure for good measure.

"The Zenith Tempest, The Boosted Gear, The Divine Dividing - on account of that horrific Juggernaut Drive for both." He added belatedly, "The Telos Karma too, and, of course, the one that gave them all their name-"

"The Spear." I finished for him, because it didn't take a genius to figure that one out. "The True Longinus, that which pierced the side of Christ."

Also known as the 'If you're not strong enough to snap your fingers and kill its wielder immediately, just leave' spear.

I'm not kidding - according to Chiron, that thing is just never worth the trouble.

"The very one." Apollon agreed. "So if you think that simply possessing Incinerate Anthem is enough to put you on that level, you're sorely mistaken - but in a good way, I would think. Ambition and the drive to act on it are only ever a danger when you let them overtake your good sense, and from what I've seen so far, you're hardly at risk of that."

...

Chiron might disagree with that.

Even if he didn't, that didn't make me feel better.

Or maybe they did, a little, but I was still hesitating, and I guess it must have shown, because he didn't stop there.

"If it makes you feel any better, Chiron is perfectly capable of sealing the gear while you train."

I perked up despite myself.

"Really?"

"Oh, easily. Even mortals with the right means can lock away Sacred Gears, and Chiron is far beyond that. I was tempted to do it myself, even, depending on how this conversation went. I was even prepared to remove it from you entirely."

...

"That's an option? Wouldn't that have killed me?"

That was how these things went, didn't it?

.... I couldn't remember.

He frowned heavily.

"Of course not. Any god of sufficient power and skill can remove a Sacred Gear from a mortal, though I'll admit they tend to be few and far between across pantheons. The exponentially more difficult problem is holding onto them afterwards and preventing Heaven's System from recalling them, but that's a whole other sort of matter."

Well.

The more you know.

"Then this isn't as big a deal as I thought?"

Even as I asked it, a part of me slowly started unwinding, and it finally felt like I could breathe a little easier again.

"Not particularly, no." He answered, almost cheerfully, and I nearly smiled.

I didn't want to get stuck with a cheat code and have it carry me through my fights - the idea felt gross in more ways than I could count off the top of my head - but if I could still level up without it, and if it was just another surprise up my sleeve...

...

Yeah, I could work with this.

Worse comes to worst, I could just have it sealed away or removed, right?

"Though to be fair, your possessing it will likely be… politically interesting at some point down the line."

On second thought...

"Politically interesting?" I asked gingerly, and he waved it off.

"A pagan demigod holding on to an Abrahamic Holy Relic, and that one in particular?" He shrugged. "There'll be... implications, both within and without our pantheon, but it's nothing for you to concern yourself with at this point."

"How come?"

And how exactly does he figure, because that doesn't sound like the walk in the park he's trying to make it out to be.

"Because I'll be dealing with it."

"..."

Never mind then.

The iron in his voice was a whole bucket of steaming no.

"I'll leave it to you, then."

"I thought you might." He agreed dryly. "Any more questions?"

I shook my head - I knew better by now.

"Then we're all done. Right on time, then. Your teacher and your friend are back, along with company."

"Comp- oh."

I saw them right as he stepped to the left, out of my line of sight - Chiron and Sairaorg, marching out of the tree line with Artemis of all people a few paces to the left, arms folded behind her back as her silver eyes narrowed at me.

Then she relaxed a fraction and nodded in greeting.

Chiron and Sairaorg, on the other hand, lit up at the sight of me.

Or at least Sai did.

Chiron just smiled, bemused, and raised his hand to match my wave.

Because of course he did.

"Hey!" I grinned properly this time. "What've you guys been- oof!"

That's when Sairaorg tackled me to the ground so fast we went rolling across the garden floor like an overgrown tumbleweed.

Because of course he did.

...​

"Pass the orange juice."

"Trade you for the bacon?"

"Done."

Breakfast that morning was a little surreal.

You'd think nothing would be that for any of us anymore at this point, but something about wolfing down sausages and toast with the god of the Sun and the goddess of the Moon on either end of the table respectively was a little... much.

Just a bit.

"Here."

I blinked as Apollon beat Sairaorg to the punch, leaning over to grab the pitcher before he could. Sai almost recoiled as the god leaned forward, not that I could have blamed him.

"Thanks."

"Drink." He chided carefully. "You need your vitamins."

Then he threw me for a loop when he held out his free hand, allowing a small, unassuming flask to materialize in his hand before uncorking it with his thumb.

Across the table, Artemis rolled her eyes.

"Really, brother? Mother-henning?"

"Not a word out of you." He wagged a finger her way even as he poured a few drops of what looked like liquid gold over into the orange juice and let it shimmer oddly before regaining its color. "I've seen you with your huntresses and their children. You have no room to talk."

"I have plenty."

"And I have pictures that say otherwise."

Her eyes flashed.

"What pictures?"

He smirked smugly before pouring me a glass and sliding it over with a conspiratorial wink.

"Apollon, what pictures?"

Like I said - Breakfast was surreal, like I'd been teleported onto the set of a cheesy sitcom.

I didn't hate it, though.

Then I took a sip of the OJ, and it felt like downing a glass of Gatorade mixed in with something warm and syrupy, which sounds absolutely disgusting, but trust me, it worked.

"Nectar." I blurted it out, and he nodded warmly.

"A little pick-me-up to kick off your day."

Nice.

"Speaking of the day, my lord and lady," Chiron finally spoke up after clearing his plate, looking as unbothered and at ease as he ever does around here even when both gods turned to stare him down. "Can we expect you to stay for lunch? Because I have quite the schedule planned for my students after we finish going over their quest in detail-"

Sai and I both winced, and I don't think I have to tell you why.

Use your imagination.

"-And I'd like to know if you'd prefer I plan around you, or invite you to take part."

"There's no need for the formality, Chiron." Artemis huffed a breath, and Apollon agreed with a nod.

"And we won't be imposing on you for much longer. I have to go see a group of wizards about some reparations."

The wording of that sentence niggled at me, but Chiron just raised a brow and nodded.

"The Land of Oz, then?"

"But of course."

"Poor fools."

"Fools, absolutely. Poor?" He shrugged, but his eyes flashed gold and back in a sudden burst that was full of implied meaning. "We'll see in due time."

I stared, and the pieces started connecting a little too quickly for my liking.

"Uh, is this about-?"

"Moving on now." Apollon clapped his hands and rolled over my words like a particularly gentle bulldozer. "Artemis has some business to share with the rest of the class."

All of us turned to stare at her, and she sighed.

"You're exhausting."

"I am a delight."

"You're something only arguably fit for polite company. Sometimes many things of that nature." She muttered, before abruptly sitting up in her chair and fixing her gaze on me.

Suddenly, the whimsical aura they'd had going for them all morning long seemed to vanish, and that distinct edge of godliness came careening right back to smack us all in the face.

"Nephew."

I nodded carefully.

"Aunt?"

"I gave you a task." She tilted her to the side. "One more dangerous than I had anticipated."

"We still managed it... technically."

We did find Regulus, and even if things had spiraled out of control pretty much immediately from there, that still counted as mission accomplished.

Probably.

I hope.

"Yes." She agreed easily enough. "And I owe you a promised reward."

And then she turned to Sairaorg, who swallowed but didn't flinch away.

"Devil."

"Lady Artemis."

"See that you don't give me a reason to regret this."

And before he could ask, she leaned forward and poked him in the middle forehead with her forefinger.

Bam.

The pressure in the room shifted, and Sai let out a quiet gasp and rocked back in his chair as a silver sheen flickered over his skin for a few seconds before wafting out again.

That wasn't hard to figure out either.

"You gave him your blessing."

To that, she merely nodded.

"I promised."

She said it like it was supposed to be answer enough, and I guess it pretty much was.

"A great reward indeed." Chiron agreed, before leaning over to pat Sairaorg on the shoulder. "As I'm sure my student will attest once he gets over the garbled shock."

Garbled shock was right - his pupils had expanded, and he was staring off against the other wall like it held all the secrets of the universe behind the plaster.

...I wondered what he was sensing through his senjutsu.

Chiron gave him a pointed look and waited patiently.

"..."

"...Any time now, student."

"..."

"...Daniel, would you-?"

I kicked Sai's foot under the table, hard.

What?

I'm not missing out on an invitation like that.

"Ow!" He yelped and his eyes shifted back from glassy to focused as he glared at me, before remembering that we weren't alone. "Oh! I- uh - thank you, Lady Artemis."

"It is only an edge, no different than the blessing I gave my nephew. Its value depends on your effort, though I'll admit that I will be expecting far more than I ordinarily would from a child. For a devil as young as you are, your spiritual growth is truly impressive."

It was a mild compliment, but it had a lot of weight to it.

Chiron seemed to agree, too.

"High praise."

"It is only the truth - and speaking of the truth, it's past time we took our leave." She shook her head, and gracefully rose from her chair. "Apollon."

"Fair enough."

I started when he rose too, and just as smoothly - I was expecting him to argue the point.

"That's it? You're leaving."

Just like that?

"Needs must. We both have matters we need to attend to sooner rather than later." He admitted, and he sounded genuinely putt-off about it too. You couldn't fake that kind of irritation. "But don't worry - rest assured, I'll be keeping an eye out for you, as ever and always."

Another time, and I might have been resisting the urge to tell him that that was the worrying part.

Except...

It wasn't.

Not as much as it would have been before.

"Thank you."

He sighed in exasperation.

"I've told you before, you don't have to-"

"No, seriously."

Then my mouth moved on autopilot.

"Dad."

He stilled.

I did too, but...

...

Eh, screw it.

I'll deal with the consequences when they blow up in my face and not a second before.

"Dad," I repeated, just to prove a point. To him or to myself was anyone's bet, though. "Thanks. I mean it. For-"

Healing me?

Sticking around and explaining stuff?

Just showing at all?

"-Everything." I finished, a little lamely, but I don't think anybody around me noticed, much less minded it.

Apollon stared at me for a long second, before breaking out into the warmest - and fondest - smile yet.

He even leaned over the table and ruffled my hair for good measure.

"I'll be seeing you, son."

And then he dissolved on the spot, fading a way in a wave of golden motes and vanishing entirely.

We all stared after him for a second.

And then Artemis clicked her tongue.

"He is going to be in an insufferably good mood for the rest of the day." She sounded exhausted, before flickering a tired smirk my way. "Well played, nephew."

Um.

"That's not why I-"

"Oh, I know." Her smile softened. "That just makes it better. Until next time, all."

And then she took a page out of his book and melted away in a shower of silver light, and both gods were gone just as quickly as they'd arrived.

...

For a long minute, nobody spoke.

Then I cleared my throat.

"So. That happened."

Thunk.

That sound?

That was Sai's head hitting the table and rattling all the plates.

Honestly, fair enough.

"Why."

"Why what?"

Genuinely asking here. There's so many reasons to be regretting all of our recent life choices that it's hard to settle on just the one.

"Everything."

Yeah, that tracks.

"That's the most insightful question I've heard from you all week, Sairaorg." Chiron mused, stirring a sugar cube into his cup with all the patience of a saint. "Well done."

I stiffled a laugh.

Sure it was this side of hysterical, but I had good reason a hundred times over at this point.

Sai did too, which made me hold back on the laughter a little more.

Then he looked up at me with this look, and I lost my smile altogether.

"Sai?"

"I'm sorry."

Woah.

He sounded miserable, like the word had punched him in the gut on its way out

"...What're you talking about?"

"Augusta."

...

Oh.

Oh.

"I sensed her, but she was there so fast and I didn't move in time-"

"Sai."

"-and the next thing I knew she the flames were burning across your bow and up your arm-"

"Sai."

"-so sorry, I didn't-"

"Sai."

He stopped.

Thank dad. That was getting physically painful.

"Stop it."

"I-"

"I'm serious."

"But-"

"I will lunge across this table and clock you in the face." I looked him dead in the eye as I said it. "You know I will."

He opened his mouth... then closed it again when he realized that, yeah, I totally would.

Didn't look any happier about it, though.

Chiron just snorted and sipped his tea.

Me, though?

"Dude."

I decided to nip this thing in the bud right here, and right now.

I held up a hand.

Then I closed it into a fist, and aimed it his way.

His breath caught.

I just grinned.

Silently. Not a word beneath us.

We didn't need them.

Slowly, he matched my grin, and raised his fist to meet mine, and all was right in the world.

"...I do owe you a bow, though."

"A bow-?" My jaw dropped - Augusta had destroyed my bow. "That b-!"

"Ahem."

-aaaaad woman! Right Chiron?"

Sai sniggered.

"Smooth save. Really."

I kicked him under the table again.

Chiron didn't seem to mind the squabbling.

There was a proud glint in his eyes as he looked from me to Sairaorg and back again, even if he didn't speak up at first.

Not until he took us both in, nodded to himself, and then started off with what was about the last thing I expected him to drop on us right then and there.

"A month. Maybe two at most."

Sairaorg and I blinked, glanced at each other, and went right back to staring at him again.

"...Which means...?"

"That's the time I'll be assessing you, starting from today. If I'm satisfied at the end of that period, I'll let you go off on your quest. Your real quest."

Sai choked, and I jerked back in my seat like I'd been electrocuted.

"What?"

It wasn't surprise, or excitement - just pure bewilderment.

That's what he was starting with?

Not the mess we'd just wrapped up with?

Not the gods who'd shown up and the up and left almost as quickly?

Why even? - wait.

Why hadn't he started talking about the mess we just wrapped up?

My eyes narrowed, and I squinted at him suspiciously.

Chiron wasn't like the two of us - or, honestly, just me. He didn't go off on random tangents without a reason or three behind everyone, and he sure as anything wouldn't start today, and now of all times.

"Why start with that of all things?"

Chiron smiled.

No, wait.

Let me rephrase that, just to set the scene.

Chiron smiled.

Sairaorg and I both paled on que.

"Because I'm being merciful." He said, almost gently. Almost. "I'm giving you something to look forward to before we begin. A light at the end of tunnel, so to speak."

And wasn't that the most terrifying thing I've heard all week?

Sairaorg swallowed.

"Begin?"

"Oh yes. Let's start by going over everything you did wrong two days ago, and how best to avoid such mistakes in the future." He smiled some more. "With practical examples."

...

"I should have stayed unconscious."

He didn't disagree.

"You really should have."

Predictably, my day went downhill from there.

...

#1,361
A canonical interlude that takes place after the last chapter and before the next, and wasn't included before because it didn't quite fit the vibe and ending of the last one.
The Land of Oz.

Suspended in the Dimensional Gap and anchored to no one realm in particular was the magical domain and nation of Oz.

It first came to be when a rogue branch of the Grauzauberer magician's associations fell under new management when the original founder - a notably ambitious and suitably infamous mortal by the name of Johann Georg Faust - did what mortals tended to do with delightfully predictable consistency and just died.

Naturally, his death meant that control of his organization was passed onto his contracted devil - an infernal annoyance by the name of Mephisto Pheles.

Perhaps that explained the state of it in the modern day and age- it was, after all, quite literally godless from its very inception.

Regardless, a devil came to rule Grauzauberer.

Some accepted this.

Others didn't.

Dramatics of the explosive and murderous varieties ensued, and when all was said and done, the splinter group that parted ways from the original took to the Dimensional Gap and founded the Land of Oz as a new magical haven - and likely one audaciously impressive attempt at overcompensation, but that last part was anyone's guess in truth.

A nation rose, a land was established, divided between four witches of North, South, East and West and their elaborate castles and personal domains, and one gleaming Emerald City right in the center of it all.

And, again, all with very minimal divine interference, outside of patrons and interested meddlers.

There were plenty of reasons for that - but one of the greatest was almost insultingly straightforward once the chips were out on the table.

It wasn't their stomping grounds.

Most gods - as a general rule - were inherently unsubtle beings where it counted. Their very existence was a declaration of superiority, and their right to rule the world around them as they best pleased.

But the Land of Oz existed in the Dimensional Gap - And there was only one ruler of the chaotic void between worlds, and there existed not one being or god beyond the Infinite Ouroboros that would dare challenge the Apocalypse Dragon Of Dreams for his kingdom.

But that didn't mean that gods couldn't...pop in for a visit, so to speak.

They just had to be very, very careful.

Apollon liked to think he was just that, even if his arrival above the Emerald City of Oz was anything but subtle.

Sunlight bloomed above the gleaming city, and a wave of sheer power tore through the skies and painted it in shades of gold and fiery orange. The entire realm seemed to shudder as he materialised into being far above the Royal Palace, wearing an expression of deceptive calm.

Then he opened his mouth, and spoke.

"Hear Now My Words and Bow Your Heads."​

The words weren't just sound - they were universal meaning and almighty declaration, and everyone heard.

Everyone.

"I Am Hekēbolos - The Far Shooter."

"I Am Loimios - The Pestilintial"

"I Am Pythios - The Pythian."

"I Am Phoebus - The Brightest"

"I Am The Sun. I Am Apollon."

"I Am G̷̜̓̕o̴̢͎̻͆d̷̜͕̝͒̒."​

His eyes, his face - his entire form erupted with brilliant radiance, and his light shot forth and stretched until it could be seen and felt from every corner of Oz.

"And I Have Come For Judgment."​

Then he began to descend, and down below, the screams began in earnest.

...​

Across the Land of Oz, a goddess idly watched her brother's sweeping descent, before panning her gaze back to the castle and the sprawling estate.

Augusta Hawthorn had been this nation's venerated - if that was even the right word, which most would doubt - Witch of the East, and her inherited fief reflected the weight of that position.

Enormous, sprawling, and excessive from the sheer scope of its blackened walls and high-reaching towers to the near endless - from a mortal's perspective - layers of magical wards and defenses so thick that even the most mundane vermin would be able to sense them.

Artemis had seen infinitely better, but she wasn't here to criticize its former owner's terrible sense of aesthetics.

She'd come to support Apollon's demands for 'reparations' - where the sun went, the moon followed in orbit - but now that she was here, however...

She saw them.

The magic didn't stop her gaze from peering past the veils around the Castle of the East and deep into its bowels, where she sensed a disturbance she had no taste or patience for.

She looked past the wizards and retainers, the guests and the servants, all the various scuttling mice flitting about and scattering in a panic as her twin made his fiery presence known, and there she saw them, deep in the ground beneath all their feet.

Men, women, and even children.

Chained, collared, imprisoned in dungeons too small for comfort or dignity, sallow-cheeked and gaunt beyond any pretence of health or decency.

They were the lucky ones.

The others...

Prisoners. Hostages. Experiments.

Not her people, but nonetheless an affront to her domain more vile than anything she would ever suffer to exist.

Unlike Apollon, Artemis's divinity didn't build as a well-spring of pressure that crushed and crushed all around it before bursting out to consume everything for good measure.

She didn't bother with words or theatrics.

Instead, her presence lanced out brutally, instantly, and without an iota of mercy.

Inside Augusta's castle, every living thing still capable of movement froze at once as they felt it, breaths dying in their very lungs.

That creeping dread seeping in from every direction.

The flickering shadows shifting just out of the corner of their eyes.

The undeniable prickle of skin at the backs of their necks, the kind that would have them scrambling to whirl around and look for invisible eyes they knew with bone-deep certainty were there.

And watching.

Always watching.

The awareness of a hunter.

The hunter.

Good.

Artemis smiled, lightly - an expression that wasn't any kind of amusement, but the righteous rage that had quickly grown so cold and sharp it looped back in on itself and became something altogether more terrifying - and craned her neck to the side.

Considering.

Picking the first target.

Then she lunged and became a streak of brilliant and deadly silver.

With her, the prey never had a chance to scream.

...​

Chiron's Estate:

Deep in the forest, the annoyingly wily old centaur had negotiated as an incentive for him to play nice, Regulas sat.

Well, he wasn't quite sitting so much as lounging in lazy pleasure, happy to soak in the sunlight and enjoy the scents of open greenery at his leisure and the feel of the cool breeze ruffling his re-embodied mane, but the point still stood - and he didn't feel a single ounce of shame admitting that.

As far as he was concerned, he was due thousands and thousands of years of self-mandated vacation days, with interest, and now that he'd regained a corporeal form he fully intended to use them.

Adapting to his circumstances within the biblical bastard's gear and System didn't mean he'd enjoyed them, only accepted the absolute pain in the everything that reality had been while it lasted.

...Though it... wasn't all that bad, always, once he'd gotten past the initial indignity.

Sure, that had taken a few centuries that he'd spent locked into a frothing rage state that was just embarrassing to remember, but he was perfectly happy not bringing that little tidbit up, ever - and eating anybody that tried.

What?

He'll apologize for nothing, and any fool that criticises him probably has it coming in some capacity anyway.

Moving on now...

Time as a glorified tool had eventually hit a balance.

Less spiritually torturous, and more disgustingly tedious to the point that he'd have shaved his own mane if he'd had the chance, just to have something to do.

His wielders, though...

Some of them had been smears of all things pathetic, and their deaths had been hilariously entertaining.

Others were nothing special - just footnotes who'd lucked out and been graced with his magnificence.

And some, like his last and - if he had anything to say about - final one...

...

He closed his eyes and exhaled through his maw.

There was no point bringing those memories up now.

A score was settled, the debt was paid, and he'd gotten even in blood and carnage.

Enough was enough.

Now, he was home free.

In due time, once he was sure this was a permanent deal and not a glitch or a plot by Him and his sanctimonious pigeons, he'd probably hit the road.

Search out some entertainment. Have a little fun.

The Nemean Lion - the only one worth the name, because the rest of his kind were wimps until proven otherwise - was free, and the world and any number of walking problems and acceptable targets just beginning to be swatted around mauled had better brace for impact-

The air shifted.

A familiar scent hit his nose - deceptively tolerable and recognizable in a way that would have had a lesser lion recognize its source as one of theirs.

Kin, even.

But the irritating brat that was trying to sneak up on him was anything but.

For the love of-

Regulus rose and shook out his mane, eyes sharpening with annoyed interest before he barred his teeth and growled, the sound tearing out across the greenery like fine knives scraping against solid rock.

His presence was still contained, but that didn't matter.

When he let loose a sound like that, most smart, sensible creatures ended up fleeing for their lives like death had shown up at the door with a release form in one hand and a ledger of unpaid taxes in the other, but apparently, he wasn't dealing with anyone smart or sensible now.

Case in point?

Instead of bolting, the Vapula - or was it Bael? - brat froze, before sighing and letting his head drop not like a man facing a being who could make him an appetizer in the blink of an eye, but a child who'd been caught with hand in the cookie jar and folded on the spot.

Then he actually started walking up to him, slipping out from behind the trees and marching over with cheery determination in his every step.

"Hello again, Regulus."

"...Brat."

He grinned.

"It's Sairaorg, actually, but I'll allow it."

Cute.

Why was he here?

...

On second thought, he had a better question.

"Why do you keep coming back?"

Three times this infant had come into the forest looking for him - and yes, he knew what he was up to, he wasn't a fool - but Regulus had made a game of ignoring him, and this made encounter number four.

He hadn't paid any attention before, and for good reason:

The boy was to weak to go a few rounds with and would probably taste terrible given Regulus's track record with his species - and even if he wasn't, he neither had a taste for killing children and this one was off-limits for blatantly obvious reasons.

"Well, first, I wanted to check in on you!"

Regulus stared.

He didn't take it back.

Why wasn't he taking it back?

"...So help me, if you interrupted my nap for inane pleasantries-"

"-and I had a favor I wanted to ask!"

He paused.

"...A favor."

...

Well, if nothing else, then points for sheer nerve.

He wasn't even sure if the feeling bubbling up inside of him was amusement or irritation.

Eh, he's curious now.

"I'm listening."

The devil beamed.

"My friend is sparring over with Chiron. He's the new wielder of Incinerate Anthem-"

"Obviously." Regulus drawled.

He'd sensed that disloyal thing jumping ship the instant it made its move, probably helped along at the moment by the draconically greedy nature of the other brat's spear.

Or maybe he was off the mark there and something else was at play, but he genuinely couldn't care less in the long run.

"-and apparently I can't spar him for the next couple of days because of it." He looked begrudging, like he'd just barely accepted an argument presented for his own good. "Too risky. Something about the gear possibly being eager to jump out at me until Dan masters it. He's training with Chiron until he has it in the bag."

Regulus tilted his head to the side and idly licked his chops.

So that was where the stench of Abrahamic Holiness was coming from, way out in the distance.

He'd thought as much.

"And this my problem... how?"

The brat's smile didn't waver.

"I want to spar with you!"

...

"..."

"..."

"...What?"

"If my best friend is sparring with a Longinus to get stronger, it only makes sense that I do it too!" He nodded proudly at that flawless logic. "And since you're here, and probably bored just sitting around all day..."

Sitting around-?

"Do you have a death wish?"

Is that what this was?

Was the average infant devil more challenged in the head than the average adult?

If so, his opinion on the species had somehow managed to drop to a new low.

And he still wasn't sure whether or not his baffled confusion was going to transition into anger, but really, he'd more than earned the right to stop, stand and stare at this new-fangled idiot in disbelief.

"Nah. I can't die any time soon, I have too much stuff to do." the brat crossed his arms and held his expression even as Regulus' presence began to flicker ominously. "And you wouldn't kill me anyway."

"Oh?"

Call it fascination in stupidity, but this, Regulus just had to hear.

"Of course not." He answered easily. "You accepted guest rights from Chiron, right? Xenia?"

...

Damn it, he had.

"So you won't kill me, because I'm his student and I live here, and I have a pretty good feeling that your pride wouldn't let you break your own word like that." The brat hit the nail right on the head with a growing smile, and Regulus resisted the urge to growl again. "Also, you're a lot stronger than me - a lot - but I think I can last at least five seconds against you, which is more than enough time for Chiron to show up and stop you from pulverising me."

He raised a hand and ran it through his hair, and his smile turned a little sheepish.

"And call it teacher loyalty or something like that, but as cool as I think you are, Regulus..."

He looked him dead in the eye.

"Chiron's just plain old cooler."

No hesitation. No doubt.

Just blatant, rock-solid belief.

...

"Is that right?"

A few thousand years ago, that would have been all the provocation Regulus needed to leap in claws and teeth first.

These days, he still found it just a bit galling - but at least the devil had a spine.

"You have a funny way of asking for help."

That just earned him another grin - he did that a lot, didn't he?

"You can try and prove me wrong if you want." His spiritual power rose - Touki - as he held his fists up with barely leashed excitement. "Ready when you are!"

Just like before, no hesitation.

Just stupid determination.

And he was trying to goad him into this farce.

Regulus's jaw almost unhinged as he took the sight in, absent-mindedly raising his own power to match, and then casually exceeding the display in front of him.

This damned, precocious brat!

...

...

...

But you know what?

Why not play along?

His teeth glinted as he barred them again, this time in his own sense of growing delight.

He had been pretty bored - but he wasn't going to waste time on words.

Instead, he roared load enough to jump-scare the dead and dashed forward, and the brat - Sairaorg Bael - leaped gleefully into the worst beating of his life.

And things just got fun from there.

...​
