#1,416
Lots of stuff happening this chapter, and the quest kicks off! Just as planned, naturally. Everything is just peachy.

Trust me.

53 Days Later

Woosh.

Sairaorg and I accelerated from zero to twenty-thousand in no time flat, kicking off into a sprint so blisteringly fast it took less than a handful of seconds for us to zip past the speed where ordinary mortals wouldn't be able to register us anymore - not even as the two streaks of sparking gold and off-white Touki we became as we raced up the slanted mountainside and past the valley where we usually sparred.

The wind whistled past us and then got promptly left behind, and the sound of my blood pounding in my ears in time with the beats of my heart was about the only thing I could focus on past the crazy-overwhelming need for speed.

Probably because it doubled over as a great measuring stick when we clashed.

And boy, did we ever.

Boom.

Boom.

Boom.

We collided multiple times per beat, two blurs of light ramming into and against one another in quicksilver clashes that had the air between us cracking over and over again, the sounds of each hit echoing out like peals of angry cannon fire.

The force of each collision carried outwards too, and the ground underneath us buckled under the shockwaves before violently bursting up and off in every other direction but hitting nothing at all in ours, because we were already long gone and rocketing off into the distance before the impact ever settled in and had a chance to catch up to us.

Every single time.

It was like a dance, almost - the world's wildest supernaturally-powered tango this side of Olympus.

We flitted back and forth over the sprawling terrain, tearing past slopes and tricky ravines, shooting through dense greenery and unevenly jutting rock formations and pretty much zig-zagging across and uprooting everything in our passing until we reached just the right point and - on gut instinct alone - we both decided enough was enough.

One last impact, fiercer and more powerful than the last, and then we broke apart with gusto - Sairaorg's feet carved deep trenches in the dirt and stone under him as he bled off the force of the last double-footed kick I'd landed on him, and I used his rock-solid guard as a springboard to fling myself back through the air and into a flying flip so smooth I barely needed to inhale through it before I landed on the balls of my feet, knees bent and ready to bolt on the spot.

Our eyes met, purple on sky-blue, and we paused across from one another.

His arms stayed raised as he stood still, primed to throw hands on demand, and wordlessly waited for me to make the first move.

A second passed.

Then another.

On the third, I finally exhaled, right in sync with him, and the easy-going grin wormed its way onto my face before I straightened out of my crouch and started casually stretching out my arms and shoulders.

"Man, that was a good warm-up."

Sairaorg matched my energy with a short laugh before he started bouncing on his toes like a boxer who'd just stepped into the ring.

"Right? You've gotten faster."

I didn't deny it.

"Sure did, and right back at you."

And the best part?

I was dead serious when I called this a warm-up.

Neither of us had been going close to all out - not by a metric long shot, but now that we were here...

"Ready to kick things up a notch?"

Or three?

Sai smirked my way for an answer, dropping out of his rhythm and standing deceptively still as he waited, fists just as ready as before.

"Come at me!"

Hah.

Despite the open invitation - and the infectious excitement that always seemed to get to me when we started going at it - I didn't go at it just yet.

Neither of us did.

Part of this game was knowing when to to make a move, and that was almost always two parts instinct, and one part lucky gamble - and these days, I was actually racking up a good streak with those.

Sort of.

Probably.

...

Moving on now.

The breeze blew past us as we tensed and waited, ruffling my hair and brushing against my skin, and a shadow fell over us as a cloud lazily floated past and blocked out the sun.

Almost.

I took another deep breath, and my fingers twitched by my sides.

Sairaorg's smirk sharpened, and his fists bobbed just enough to be noticeable.

Wait for it.

The cloud drifted past, the interrupted streaks of warm sunlight came falling right back-

Now!

-and we moved.

I flew forward and snapped my hand out to my side, letting Serpent's Downfall manifest in my grip with a shower of sparks that never had a chance to hit the ground before I was planting my feet down and abruptly meeting Sairoarg's head-on charge with a wide, sweeping swing meant to drive him back.

It didn't - not really.

He shifted just so and tipped his head back enough
to let the amber-gold blade pass him by with a sharp, cutting whistle, and then quickly jerked forward again and threw a haymaker that could pulverize concrete, crumple reinforced steel like tinfoil and probably rearrange the side of my face into something you'd stop and stare at all funny-like in a modern art museum... right at said face.

Yeah, not today buddy.

Instead of flinching back the way I'd had way too many times before, I darted into the path of the incoming pain train before using the motion to spin around it and out of his guard.

Then I darted in and drove my knee up into his side, hard.

He may be the punching expert between the two of us, but that didn't mean I was a slouch in the monster strength department myself, and it showed.

Credit where credit was due though, because he only winced, grunted under his breath, and pivoted with another straight jab so sudden I only just managed to catch and brace against it with the haft of my spear.

Even then, the power of it still rattled my grip and ran right through my arms and up to the back of my teeth.

Ow.

I darted away the second he cocked the other fist, trying to circle around him before aiming a spear-jab down near his left thigh, then suddenly arcing up for a strike to his side I knew he wouldn't let land.

He hadn't in months.

Sure enough, he outright deflected it with a palm coated in Touki and moved to close in on me, the other fist still ready to mess up my day.

Called it.

I met his eyes, and he smiled.

I did too.

"Flashbang."

Light and overlapping sound burst out of me in a full-bodied wave, harmless in the long run but sharp as knives to all your senses at point-blank range, and he cursed and reared back on instinct.

Not a step back, and not even a stagger, but enough that he didn't press forward when I leaped away, putting space between us before angling my spear forward again and darting forward with a two-handed stab aimed right for his center mass.

"Oh, like hell!"

His palms clapped forward with another crack and a rush of displaced air, and he caught it inches away from his shirt between both of them like something out of a corny martial arts movie.

Very cool, I'll fess up to that much - but also a mistake.

In the heat - heh - of the moment, all up close and personal, it was easy to forget that Serpent's Downfall wasn't just your average reinforced polearm.

"Ignite!"

The blade lit up and burst with orange-gold flames right there in his hold, and Sairaorg ripped his hands away instantly. The Touki would have protected him from the worst of it, but that had to sting.

He also let rip a few choice words that would have had Chiron force-feeding him a bar of soap before making him write a three-thousand-word apology essay on the importance of respectful and courteous language, and in flowery cursive font too, but that's just a side note.

"Dan, you bastard!"

That too.

"Bastard is right, but only technically!"

"Technically my whole entire- rrrgghh!" He cut himself with an irritated growl and blurred into motion.

Whoo boy.

I cackled and sprang out of the way as he thundered towards me, swinging his arm at me in a sharp slashing motion that had his Touki surging out it in a fine, razor-bladed wave I needed to duck under on sheer principle.

It shot overhead anyway and sliced through both the air and the earth behind us with so much power that it probably cut halfway down the length of the mountain in one go.

Yikes.

That would have been hard to walk off, and Sairaorg didn't give me an inch before he was dashing towards me again and gearing back for a brutal kick I didn't even bother trying to dodge.

Instead, I locked on to a spot behind him and teleported in a flash of light, aiming my spear at-

Crack.

- nothing at all, apparently, because Sai didn't even turn around this time before slamming his foot against the dirt beneath him and letting his spiritual aura explode out in a titanic pulse with only a split-second's worth of warning.

The ground rumbled all around me, the grass glittering and writhing unnaturally, and then it was all surging straight up in one solid wave that immediately tried to close in on me like the jaws of a starving predator.

Crap.

I tried to launch myself up, but the air itself seemed to weigh down on me, lancing down in force to swat me out of the air.

Another senjutsu trick - not enough to stop me, but it slowed me down, just a bit.

And a bit was all Sairaorg needed.

I saw him coming - really I did - erupting through the wave of angry mountain he'd deliberately sicced on me as a cover, but I wasn't fast enough to dodge or strike out against him this time.

Or, actually, I was - only he surprised me by accepting the blow as I thrust thee spear tip at him, leaning to the side and letting it slice through his shirt and graze him along the ribs before he wrapped his left hand around the haft and stopped it solid.

It scorched him - enough that I could hear the sizzle - but he just smiled through the pain, right fist present and ready for duty, and finally caught me dead to rights.

Double crap.

I tried to let go, but I was too close and just a breath too slow to light-step away.

And we're three for three on the crap parade!

There was nowhere to go when he broke past my hasty, borderline sloppy defense and nailed me right in the chest, I swear my vision went white at the edges and stayed that way for a good long instant before I realized that I was hurtling back and down towards the earth like a skipping stone - and Sairaorg didn't stop coming.

Oh no - we don't play that nice around these parts.

My back hit the ground, the air in my lungs rushed out like someone had hit the emergency eject button and given it all the boot, and the next thing I clocked was the underside of Sairaorg's trainers coming down and at me, fast.

"Really?!"

I rolled out of the way and scrambled to my feet right as his landed hard enough to drive a crater into the earth, complete with spiderwebbing cracks reaching out all around it.

Then he leaped out and tried to backhand me into next year - tried being the operative word.

Another light step away, and I was thirty feet behind him and back in the game - at least until the hairs at the back of my neck reared up like hissing cats and I decided to make like one too, leaping up into flight before the first lance of hard packed dirt, stone, and natural energy shot towards me and tried to knock me out of the air.

Then it was open season, and a dozen of them were heading my way, courtesy of Sairaorg - each jagged and mean-looking, but nearly as tall as I was and just as wide, with wicked spike-like points that could have bored right through a less durable target.

They were his long-range answer to my arrows and teleportation, shaped entirely with senjutsu - another new trick he was starting to perfect, and probably one of a half a dozen he was hiding up his sleeve.

He didn't even have to move an inch to shape them - just focus and control his energy, and they came bursting out of the ground on command.

Impressive.

Scary too - But if you wanted to use projectiles against a son of Apollon, just plain old scary wasn't nearly good enough.

I threw out my hand in time to meet the next round, and a fiery beam of divine radiance so heavy you could have felt it moving ten blocks away scythed out of my palm and blasted them to dust on the spot, and with a backlash so intense he had to grit his teeth and flare his Touki far and wide just to stay on his feet.

Even then, it was a close call.

"Pretty neat, Sai," I muttered under my breath, eyes narrowing at him before I vanished again. "But let me show you how it's really done."

This time, I appeared higher up.

Much higher up - enough that the clouds were beneath me, the air was noticeably cooler, and Sairoarg was almost a speck hugging the ground far below.

That could change quickly, I know - he had wings and was just as fast on them as he was on the ground - but I had zero intentions of giving him another shot at me before I got my own in first.

And on that note...

Power surged through me on demand, and my eyes flashed gold before I cocked back and readied Serpent's Downfall.

"Archer's Volley."

Then I pitched down and launched it in a furious arc towards the ground, the spell already on my lips.

For half a second, nothing happened.

Then my blazing spear shot down through the clouds, and suddenly its image... fractured. Like shattered glass.

Then it multiplied, almost instantly.

One became two.

Two became four.

Four became eight, and... well, you see where this is going.

In the span of a single blink - less, even - one became hundreds, rushing down in tandem until there was nowhere left to get out of the way.

A conceptual spell that played on Dad's domain of archery and the myths of him blotting out the skies with raining arrows to strike down and smite his enemies.

Each spectral spear was something in between an illusion and a duplicate of Serpent's Downfall - only one was the real deal and had the lion's share of the power, but all of them were linked as one barrage and had their own 'weight'.

Just enough of it to really hurt.

Magic was tricky and trippy like that - but really, so was Senjutsu.

Case in point?

Sairaorg saw the barrage raining down on him from above and immediately raised a hand straight up before yanking it to the side, hard, and the air howled with the motion.

The spears scattered in mid-air like bowling pins, blown every which way as if a giant hand had swept them in no particular direction at all, and even the real Serpent's Downfall was pushed far enough away that it'd have never hit Sairaorg.

Shame that that was exactly what I planned for, and the second spell I'd layered over the first triggered right on schedule..

"Sickly Glory."

Instead of dispersing, the construct-spears did what most things tended to do in our spars and detonated spectacularly.


B̶͚̱͈̮͗̋̋̏̚ͅe̶̼̐͋̔͜h̵̳͖̣̝̄o̶̖̤̪͂̐̌͊l̶͔͐͂̀ḓ̵̞̭̲͆͑ ̵͈̻̮͎̆͋̀͌Ḡ̶̙̈l̶̪͉̜͔̒ͅõ̵̫͇̹̎r̸̳͂͆͒͑y̸͕̼͚̍̽̚t̵̘̋


Light. Sound. Feeling.

All of it swept out in a ceaseless rush, another conceptual spell that made my earlier flash bang look like a total joke.

Probably because it had been just that - a cheap, easy trick.

This used the original as a base, and then added in a sprinkle of the one domain of Apollon's that I'd touched on the least.

Plagues.

Or at least an idea of an aspect of them, focused on how they spread and overwhelmed the senses, bringing sudden - if just temporary - unwellness and generally being a total nightmare to shrug off in the middle of a fight.

Like an instant case of flu, if the virus somehow grew arms and tried to punch you in the brain.

It hit Sairaorg like a freight train to the soul, and his Touki visibly flickered. Underneath it, his skin paled a shade, too quickly to be natural, and his next step was almost a stumble.

A moment of weakness.

I saw all of this in real time, of course, because I'd already teleported in front of him and lunged full-tilt at him, not an ounce of hesitation between us.

Anything less and I'd have been right back to square one.

He met my stride anyway, but this time when he jabbed at me the blow only just succeeded in grazing my cheek, before I tilted out of the way and buried my fist in his gut hard enough that his whole frame shuddered.

Score.

"Two for flinching!"

Then I decked him across the face and watched his head snap back in a way that'd be smarting all day.

I'd have gone for a third, but I had to cross my hands over my chest and brace against the sudden foot he tried to plant there, and then I was suddenly ten feet away and shifting uneasily to regain my balance.

...

There was a pause, and neither of us moved beyond the shaking shoulders and the panting breaths.

"..."

"..."

Sairaorg eventually spit out a small fleck of blood and sighed at me in exasperation.

"...That was just cheating."

I shrugged nonchalantly - mostly bravado, obviously - and wiped some sweat off my brow with the back of my hand.

Ten-and-something months ago, a hit like that would have ended me.

Five months ago, it would have still been devastating and knocked a good chunk of the fight clean out of me.

Now?

It and every other one like it just hurt in a way that was more motivation than deterrent.

"Eh, maybe a little. But you use what you've got, and I'm not the one playing it close to the chest."

Not entirely, anyway.

He snorted at the jab, and I belatedly noticed that his colour was already inching back to normal. Touki was a less immediate form of power when compared to magic, but boy was it convenient when you got going.

"Heh. Fair."

Then he opened his mouth and roared.

Not screamed.

Not yelled.

Roared - with a capital 'R'

It wasn't just sound, or force that smacked into me at speed, but sheer presence.

Some blend of spiritual aura and Touki that felt tellingly familiar, but I didn't have time to focus on that.

My hackles rose. My senses sharpened.

Something big was coming.

Knowing that, I charged back and recalled Serpent's Downfall.

For once, Sairaorg didn't press the advantage and follow after me.

Instead, he took a meaningful step back himself and steadied his stance. Wind swirled around him, and power crackled in the air, first metaphorically, and then very literally as sparks of synergising natural energy started dancing up and down his form from head to toe.

Then it very deliberately started coiling around his fist.

Because where else would it go?

That's about the point where Serpent's Downfall came flying back and slapped into my waiting palm, and I decided to really cut loose.

There's no kill like overkill, after all.

"Ignite."

The spear seemed to vibrate in my grip, almost eagerly, and then its flames began to spill out everywhere, quickly spiralling up into a blazing pyre big enough to give the collective population of Greece's fire fighters the mother of all heart attacks.

This time, though, it wasn't just a wild blaze aimed in one general direction and let loose on demand.

This time, I shaped it.

"Remember," I whispered to the spear, and the vibrations seemed to grow stronger. "Remember your roots."

Behind me, the pyre I'd summoned seemed to jolt sharply, and then it began to warp and transform.

Wings emerged first, ephemeral but blanketing and enormous.

Uneven scales hardened, or tried to at least, and clawed feet took shape beneath the growing body.

A tail shot out next, long and sinuous, and it went from there.

If I'd had more time, it would have come out better.

Bigger. More powerful and structured. Less... blatantly incomplete, because I'd only just had the idea for the spell a little while ago and hadn't had a chance to work out all the kinks.

But Sairaorg had already beaten me to the punch.

Pun, absolutely intended.

He took a step towards me, and it felt like the gravity tripled, and the world trembled. His eyes panned up to the monster taking shape behind me, and he raised his fist in challenge, coated in a miniature sparking tornado that glowed in shades of white and green and radiated danger like an apocalypse just waiting to be let off the leash.

"Ready or not-" He bellowed out loud, half-laughing and half-challenging, and for a moment, I had a flashback to our very first spar.

It felt like a lifetime ago, in the best way possible, and the delighted smile on my face as I finished that old line for him must have been borderline terrifying.

"-Here I co-!"

"Enough, I think."

Instantly, the moment shattered.

I mean it, too - If this were a cartoon, you'd have heard a comedic record screech right about now.

A familiar bolt of green magic lanced in from the right, far too fast to evade. It split down the middle the second we realized it was coming our way, and the first half bounced right for Sairaorg and smacked into him like he owed it money.

"Aagh!"

Aagh was right - something happened, the space around him glitched, and the natural energy just... spilled out of him and across the clearing like water from a broken dam, enormous in quantity but somehow rendered harmless with stupid ease.

The second lunged for me and knocked Serpent's Downfall right out of my grip, and it stung like dipping a cut into icy lemon juice.

"Hey!"

On cue, the pyromanical mess I'd lit into existence popped like a balloon, falling apart and dispersing into nothingness as the flames that made it up winked out of existence.

The whole thing took all of two seconds, and then it was just us, looking all winded and bruised and probably more than a little dumb.

Then we turned around.

Chiron stood a little ways away, arms crossed over his chest and wearing an expression that was basically universal to all teachers who were utterly done with your crap.

'Unimpressed' didn't do it justice.

"Students." He started, and in exactly the tone I knew spelled terrible things for the rest of my downtime today. "When I left you here while I went off to run some errands, I do believe that I instructed you to spar lightly."

Yeah, he had.

Sairaorg and I exchanged a look.

Quick, brain, think of a good excuse!

"We were being... proactive?"

No! Bad brain! Why do you always do me like this!?

Sairaorg cringed and twitched like he desperately wanted to nail me in the shoulder, but he still tried to smile and play along.

"Just the way you taught us, right Chiron?"

The centaur snorted dryly.

"A brave attempt. Points for effort, but you're not getting out of the woods that easily."

We deflated, and his lips curved upwards.

"We'll discuss the consequences back home. Until then," He turned and started trotting down the mountainside. "Lunch."

Slowly, we watched him canter off.

Then I leaned over and nudged Sairaorg in the ribs.

"'Just like you taught us?' Seriously?" I sniggered. "Suck up."

He groaned dramatically and tried to swipe at the back of my head.

"Don't start with me, moron! Next time give me something I can work with!"

Honestly?

Fair enough.

I pressed a softly glowing hand against his shoulder and carefully began patching the pair of us up, and way up ahead, Chiron started to chuckle fondly.

...​

I love magic, and for a whole bunch of reasons too, but one of the best selling points off the top of the list has just got to be the sheer versatility it paid you back with once you put in a little effort to actually get good at the stuff.

I mean, one second you're using it to lob landscape-reshaping fireballs at your enemies, and then the next your millenia old and literally mythical teacher is summoning picnic tables out of thin air and declaring open season on a stack of awesome-looking sandwiches and a pitcher of iced tea.

It was the ultimate pocket tool kit - What's not to like?

Anyway, there we were, scarfing down our food like there was no tomorrow, when Chiron suddenly pulled a surprise on us.

"The reason I told you not to spar too roughly," He began, and the admonishment in his voice was tinged with exasperation. "Was because I'd have preferred that you didn't tire yourselves out or make a mess of one another before an old friend of mine came to visit."

Huh?

Sairaorg's brow rose, and I swallowed a mouthful of sandwich and wiped the crumbs off my face.

"Friend?"

"Visit?"

Then I stiffened a little.

"It's not another god, is it?"

Because for all that I could look back and safely say that my track record in meeting Olympians was - so far - pretty much golden all around, I still didn't want to tempt the fates on that one any time soon.

"No, of course not."

Ah.

I relaxed and took another sip of my lemonade.

"Cool? So who are we meeting?"

"You'll see soon enough." He answered patiently. "Unless he's running late, and I doubt that he is, he should be arriving right about... ah, there we go."

A few feet just outside the small glade where we'd set up our instant picnic, a spell circle began to take shape. Violet geometric patterns locked into an array, and then shapes began to bloom out from its heart - only one actually moved, though, and it was that one that had me pausing and pulling a double-take.

I couldn't help it - the bald, amber-eyed and bearded cyclops was a blast from the not-so-distant past, in appearance at least.

In terms of the power I could sense form him, though, he made the three others who'd nearly murderised me once upon a time look like absolute chumps.

He stood at eight and something feet tall, wearing baggy linen pants and nothing from the waist up to show off a body that looked like a bodybuilder's with lego bricks for muscles and enough gnarly scars and pockmarks across his bronze tanned skin that you'd think someone had lobbed him into a giant fruit blender and left him in there overnight.

Two long rectangular wooden crates hovered behind him, and he was carrying a large metal suitcase in one hand that gave off a strange feeling - familiar, but only just.

A question for later.

"Chiron."

Even his voice matched his looks to a T - deep and gruff, but unbroken.

"Old friend." Our teacher moved forward to greet him, and Sairaorg and I both stood in sync just as their hands clasped against one another's forearms in a strong, meaningful grip. "Always a pleasure to see you."

"Right." The cyclops seemed to brush the sentiment off, but he didn't deny it. Then his eye panned over to us. "You've got company. New students?"

"Indeed."

"Thought as much." He grunted and looked over the pair of us. "Weren't you out of the hero-training business?"

"What can I say?" Chiron smiled enigmatically. "Even the best-laid plans of gods and beings can change with the winds, and sometimes we are all the better for it. But enough of that - introductions first."

He turned to us and clapped a hand on the cyclops's shoulder.

"Boys, I give you Brontes, direct descendant of the Elder Cyclops of the same name."

That's.... hold on.

It only took me a second to place that name.

Brontes - as in, Brontes, Arges, and Steropes, the three Great Cyclopes who forged Zeus's lightning bolt in the fires of Tartarus itself.

Or himself, depending on how you looked at it.

That's...pretty cool, actually.

I didn't say it aloud though, and Chiron pivoted right about then and gestured over at us.

"Old friend, my students. Sairaorg Bael, an abrahamic devil of the Underworld-"

Sai nodded politely and raised a hand in greeting.

"-And Daniel Winchester, son of Apollon."

I threw up a peace sign and smiled lightly.

"Hello."

The cyclops blinked in surprise - or at least I think he did.

It was harder to tell with just the one eye.

"That's...Hmm." His voice didn't lose its gruffness, but there was a smidge of interest there now. "An unlikely lineup. Wouldn't have expected to find one of his kind with you of all people. And one with a strong, infamous name too. Odd."

That was aimed at Sairaorg, but there was no real feeling there beyond curiosity.

Then he glanced back at me.

"And this one - a demigod. His demigod." He leaned back a little to look me up and down. "The sun lord hasn't had one of them in a long while now, not after that mess a few centuries back-"

Mess?

I frowned, but Brontes wasn't done talking yet.

"- and he's here with a devil of all things. That must've gone over well."

The sarcasm was about as dry as a sun-bleached bone in the middle of the Sahara, but Chiron shrugged it off easily enough.

"Lord Apollon has given his approval, if rather indirectly."

"Hah. 'Indirectly." The cyclops grunted again in amusement. "I'll bet."

It didn't take a genius to realize that there was something Sai and I were missing.

A story somewhere in there that we hadn't been clued in on, but I only had to take one look at Chiron's expression to get the message.

Later.

Fine.

I was curious, but I could wait.

"You're staring, boyo. Never seen a cyclops before?"

And there was Brontes, looking at me again.

"I have, actually." The answer came out automatically, and I'd make an excuse for that, but at this point, I've just accepted the fact that my mouth is an autonomous entity stuck to my face that only plays ball whenever it feels like it. "Three of them. They stalked me at my school, and then they chased me home and tried to eat me."

Sure it happened in another world entirely, but that's the beautiful thing about low-key trauma fuel - It was nice and viable no matter where you went!

"..."

"..."

And they would have probably managed it too, if they weren't quite so... you know.

Dumb.

Brontes seemed to take that in for a long, long second.

"I take it they're dead?"

I didn't hesitate, par say, but I was careful about spilling the next part.

"Done and dusted."

Literally

Another quick pause.

Then Brontes surprised me by tipping his head back and belting out a short, sharp laugh.

"Good on you. The world's a messy smear of a place as it is without idiots who go after infants making it more miserable and giving the rest of our kind a bad name."

Goods?

"So I do."

Brontes snorted, before taking a step forward and dropping the suitcase onto our picnic table.

Then he turned around and snapped his fingers.

The two hovering crates behind him jerked, before drifting closer to us and, with a sound like an eggshell cracking, promptly disengaged on the spot.

And inside was...

Was...

You've gotta be kidding me.

Mannequins.

Two of them, plain and unassuming, like pretty much anything you'd see through a storefront at the mall or across a busy street.

That wasn't the stunning part, though.

Instead, it was the two suits of brilliant armour hanging off of each of them that had me gawking.

The helmets were perfectly shaped and open-faced from the front, and the chest plates beneath them gleamed in a shade of brass-like luster that practically spelled Orichalcum, form-fitting in a way that only light-weight, magical metalwork could make practical.

The shoulder guards were only a little more pronounced, and the bracers and greaves glinted in the sunlight in a way that was impossible to miss.

One of them even had a shield hanging off one arm - a Greek Aspis, round and engraved with a pattern of pillars converging in a single circular spot in the middle.

No idea what that was supposed to mean, but it somehow fit anyway.

The rest didn't count as traditionally Greek by any metric, from any era I could name off the top of my head.

Oh, it looked close, but I'd seen pictures before. Both sets had little additions here and there, a hint of mail fusing the metal to make it function better and just stuff added in to make everything more usable in the long run.

Even then, they still managed to hit the broad strokes in a way that meant nobody who wasn't an expert and wasn't looking for them would be able to spot the differences.

It was incredible - enough that I had to open and close my mouth several times before I found the right words to splutter out, and even then Sairaorg beat me to the punch.

"These are for us?"

"No, why would you think that?"

We nearly face-faulted in sync - seriously, a punch to the soul would have been less painful - and Chiron made it three more seconds before cracking up heartily.

"Just kidding."

My eye twitched.

"Really?"

"That was mean, Chiron." Even Sai was giving him the gimlet eye. "Just mean."

Naturally, our teacher was unrepentant.

"The looks on your faces were priceless."

See?

"Hah." Even Brontes looked like he was enjoying the fun, if from a distance off to the side. "You've got a colourful pair this time around, old friend."

Forget the spar earlier - neither of us had ever moved so fast in our entire lives.

...​

The armour slipped on like an old glove.

Form-fitting, just like I'd thought, and every step, movement and little twitch I took in it was almost unfairly easy - effortless, even.

My range of motion didn't decrease an inch.

I even ran around and cartwheeled in it just to push myself a little, and the weight didn't even register.

Gods, I loved magic.

"This is the most amazing gift anyone has ever given me in my entire life." Sairaorg sounded downright reverent once he was down with his jumping jacks. His knuckles rapped against his chest plate with neat, metallic pings. "Amazing."

Like, enough that even I would have felt it, with all the treasure I had under my belt.

Orichalcum wasn't cheap, and having something of this quality forged was a big deal - odds are it got that much bigger when the dude doing the forging descended from someone so legendary.

Brontes seemed to agree.

"It would have, but I owed the old horse a few favours. The materials he provided also helped cut down on costs without sacrificing quality - dragon's blood to light the forge, and that... tricky metal that came with it."

"You used Smaug's blood, didn't you?"

"Huh."

So that's where some of that stuff got off to.

Good to know.

He could have said Erebor, but I got the sense that he was being vague on purpose - Brontes was standing right there, and he wasn't hiding his interest either. Talk about a coincidence.

Good, strong defensive properties, and comfortable to work with, but there's a subtle power to it - potential I haven't learned to tap yet, even. It's given me some inspiration."

Sai had already thanked him for both of us, plenty, but it would have felt wrong and ungrateful not to add my own two cents to that pile.

And he sounded like he meant it too.

Chiron looked pleased - and maybe just a little excited, in that muted, responsible way of his.

He was confused as he walked up to the thing, but I suddenly had a sneaking suspicion that I knew where this was going.

A good one, though.

"Do I just - oh."

Sure enough, the suitcase clicked open as soon as his fingertips brushed against it. The lid popped out in quick succession, and nestled inside were...

Sairaorg sucked in a sharp breath, and I don't think anyone present could have blamed him for it.

Just like the armour, the red leather gauntlets were a work of art.

Laid out in silk, perfectly sized and glinting a shade of red that managed to make every carefully polished scale running across them pop out to the eye, and never mind the familiar feeling and the reek of magic they gave off.

"These are..."

"Hence, these gauntlets. Sairaorg gaped at him.

Heck, I gaped at him.

"Mouths closed, students of mine. You'll catch flies. And do try them on, would you? They're not simple decorations to gawk at."

Good point.

Slowly, I smirked and raised a hand.

"I mean, if he doesn't want them-"

That snapped him out of his funk, and he barely let himself shoot an amazingly grateful look at Chiron before glaring at me in mock-outrage.

"I'll throw you over the horizon."

"I can always teleport back."

"Yes sir!"

As expected, they fit perfectly, all the way up to a point just under the elbow.

"This is so - woah!"

In a flash of red gold light, the gauntlets shimmered and morphed right before our eyes. In an instant, they melted from something hard and slightly menacing in the best way possible into what looked like a pair of nearly skin-tight fingerless biker gloves, complete with faint - very faint - gold accents.

Just like that.

"And that there's the... let's call it an incognito mode, for the benefit of subtlety. Excellent work as always, Brontes."

The cyclops snorted and seemed to wave it off, but I think he was pleased by the compliment anyway.

"I did."

"On their own?"

"Yes."

I almost laughed - now that's an inside joke.

"Hn. Wouldn't have expected that, either. Where would they have even found... ah, to Hades with it. Not my circus and all that." He gave us another collective once over. "Tougher than they look?"

Chiron's smile transitioned into something that was almost a smirk of his own, edged with pride.

"You have no idea."

"So it's like that, eh?"

They kept talking amongst themselves, but Sairaorg wasn't paying attention to any of that.

Instead, he was turning his hands over and back as he checked out his new gear, before he raised his head and looked me dead in the eye with the expression of a devil who had seen the light of God - or gods, take your pick - and somehow not been turned to ashes by it.

It wouldn't be uncomfortable - that's how light the thing was.

We nodded firmly and shook on it for good measure... then we started snickering helplessly.

Behind us, Chiron just shook his head and pinched the bridge of his nose to his nose in a half-hearted attempt to hide his smile.

Behind him, Brontes just sighed.

"Children."

"True." Chiron agreed. "The very best of them, I would say."

The burst of embarrassing warmth that came up in me was something I wouldn't admit to on pain of death.

I stilled.

Sai pretty much stopped breathing.

"...The old Corinthian blend?"

Chiron chuckled good-naturedly and clapped him on the shoulder one last time.

And that was the end of it.

Brontes nodded once at all of us, and then confidently stepped right back into the middle of a quickly forming spell circle, letting himself be whisked away to parts unknown in the blink of an eye.

Then it was just us, standing around in the sudden silence.

Our teacher was, as ever and always, perfectly content to wait for us to ask the obvious question heading his way.

And Sairaorg had been waiting months - and what must have felt like an eternity -to do just that.

He stopped himself short and hesitated, torn between worry and hope, and I picked up the totally warranted slack.

"It's been two months, almost." I reminded him quietly. "And you did make a promise, teach."

We'd sparred every day.

Trained until our bones cried uncle and our bruises had bruises looking to quit.

Pushed past every limit like we were on fire and the extinguisher was on the other end of the line.

Now we just needed an answer.

Chiron knew that too.

"Are we there yet?"

He didn't say anything at first.

Instead, he looked at me, and then at Sai and back again, standing there in our new armour and waiting so patiently you'd think he was on the verge of revealing all the secrets of the universe and then some.

He took all of that in.

Observed.

Considered.

Contemplated.

Drove our combined blood pressure through the roof and beyond as the seconds ticked by.

Then he dipped his head and exhaled, and that small sound was somehow deafening

I inhaled.

Sairaorg reared back so fast the air around him parted with a sound straight out of an electric hair dryer.

A week.

I'd have laughed, but the sudden surge of nerves was sharp and probably something I should have seen coming.

It was real now.

We were going to do this.

Wordlessly, I nudged Sai.

He probably didn't even feel it, and the look in his eyes was a little glassy.

Overwhelmed with so many emotions he didn't know what to feel besides the crippling urgency.

Of course

Chiron didn't look surprised either.

"Then you had better get running. We can cover all the many, many details later."

That was most likely for the best, because Sairaorg wasn't in any kind of a state for a conversation.

He proved it a second later when he nodded in a way that wasn't all there, then turned and started sprinting away.

To the house.

That was miles and miles over the horizon.

"It'll be a good run." Chiron seemed to read my mind as we watched him blur away, already a dot shooting off into the distance "Enough time for him to think, and for us to get a spar out of the way."

Come again?

"You want to spar now-?"

Then I ducked as his staff swiped through the spot where my head had just been.

"This will give you time to think." He reasonably countered my irritated look. "And a chance to test out that new armour. Both are much needed, I daresay. Now, unless you had some other pressing question...?"

About the upcoming quest?

...

Back home?

...

In my world, with all the craziness it had going for it?

...

Yes, actually.

"I...kind of need a favour."

Something that had only just occurred to me on the spot, but was way too important not to bring up right then and there.

Chiron raised a brow.

"Oh?"

I told him.

That made me smile again, finally, because we both knew he was lying.

He was already on board.

"Thanks, Chiron."

He answered that one by coming at me, staff at the ready.

I let my iron control slip, and something inside of my soul immediately answered the unspoken call.

Let's go, Incinerate Anthem.

The world lit up with a purple blaze, and I jumped into action.
...

​
Uncle David stared at me funny, before closing his eyes and scratching at his ear in that same way he always did when someone threw a curveball at him and he had no clue what exactly you were expecting him to do with it.

"Come again?"

What'd I tell you?

It was the middle of the afternoon on a Friday, and we were sitting around the dinner table in the kitchen - and I mean our dinner table, back in Maple.

Besides the remodelled living room - remodelled because it was a total write-off after our van came flying through the wall by way of a homicidal cyclops - it looked almost the same, and they'd moved back in a while ago. Long enough that I'd gotten into the habit of visiting every now and again when I had some downtime to spare, and I'd even spent the night a couple of times here and there.

Kind of had to on that one. Katie and Alex would have mutinied if I didn't.

Such was the terrible tyranny of little sister-figures everywhere.

Fun fact: They actually managed to salvage the van.

Don't ask me how, though.

I've met gods, but that there was a real miracle.

Funner fact - or not: Somehow, because of the Mist and its shenanigans fiddling with the details behind the scenes, people gossiping like it was a professional career and me disappearing for months after the fact, the story of what happened that night... took an interesting twist in the mortal world.

See, just about everyone in town was convinced that I'd gone all crazy delinquent out of the blue and tried to take the van for a joyride, before messing up and driving it into the house like a family-friendly wrecking ball on wheels.

Then, apparently - because this stuff just gets better and better before the end - I got shipped right off to a strict boarding school for being such a colossal screw up, the kind where they dress you up in stuffy uniforms that should qualify as cruel and unusual punishments on their own and spoon feed you discipline after every lecture like cough syrup.

So... yeah.

Thanks, Mist. Real classy.

Sairaorg had laughed until he cried when he found out, and I still wasn't sure whether to find it hilarious or humiliating, but trying to figure out why people were so quick to believe that I was a platinum-class jerk could wait for later, because Uncle David was still staring.

"Well?"

I shrugged and tried to look carefree.

"How do you feel about a vacation?"

"...A vacation?"

"You've probably never been, but trust me, Athens is great this time of year."

I winced.

"Ah, you know about that whole... thing?"

He didn't answer at first, and instead turned off to the side.

Alex was where we'd left her, sitting across from us at the other end of the table and expertly filtering all our 'grown-up talk' the way kids usually did when they found you about as interesting as a pet rock.

Her face was screwed up in an expression of concentration so adorably complete I wanted to reach over and pull her a cuddle, and she had chocolate smudges all over her lips and cheeks from the bar I'd snuck her on my way in.

Turns out that handing her secret treats was easy, but getting her to hide the evidence was a work in progress.

Typical.

Aunt Sarah would make me pay for ruining her appetite with that one later, But I'll deal with that down the line - and by deal with it, I mean bolt when she's not looking and live to fight another day.

Or maybe not, if things panned out the way I hoped they would.

You-know-what?

So many low-hanging fruit right there for the taking. Resisting the urge to drop a joke just about killed me inside.

"Death trap is a bit much, don't you think?" Not at all, he was right. "I mean, sure there are teeth around every corner, but the beaches are to die for-"

"It's a secret. I have to whisper it to you."

She paused and put her crayon down, looking at me carefully before shrugging easily.

"Kay."

"You can't listen in, daddy."

So. Damn. Cute.

"No."

And just like that, she was off like a rocket, disappearing around the corner and down the hallway so fast you'd think she'd awakened her Touki too.

Crap.

Demigod dreams and the way they played fast and loose with prophetic visions were proof that you didn't even have to deliberately spy on someone to see something you shouldn't.

What?

"You're kidding. Since when?"

And did he have pictures?

"Just started this week. She loves it." He cracked a small, proud smile, but it faded too quickly under the weight of something else. "And she'll need it."

The look he fixed me with made something in the air between us change.

Grow colder.

"How come?

"Because she's a demigod legacy, and even if she's connected to that very, very distantly, I'll sleep better at night knowing she can defend herself. Her sister too, someday."

My stomach dropped, even if I tried not to show it.

I thought about Katie and Alex, facing even a single monster between, and I knew that my nightmares suddenly had a hell of a lot more fuel to work with.

"Karate won't help against all the things out there."

Or much of any of them.

"Probably not." He agreed. "But your mother was my sister, Daniel, and my mother was the proactive type. When you stick as close to the craziness as I have, you pick up a thing or two."

Did that mean...

"Like?"

Again, he didn't answer with words.

I watched him stand up instead, following him as he walked up to a cabinet and pulled out an ordinary glass cup before bringing it back to the table and laying it against the wood with a small, predictable clink.

Then he tapped the rim with a finger, and closed his eyes.

Nothing happened.

Not at first.

Then the moment passed, and my breath hitched as the glass shimmered, the air around it flickering like an old TV screen interrupted by static, and a second cup appeared an inch to its left.

Shut the front door.

Uncle David tapped that one too, and rather than go through it, it tinkled with the unmistakable sound of struck glass.

Not an illusion. Not quite a recreation either.

"Magic." My eyes narrowed even as my mind started revving like a race car's engine. "No, Mist."

"Just a parlor trick. Your mom made everything I can do look like an absolute joke, and I never minded." He smiled grimly and took a deep breath, looking winded but satisfied. "But even a trick or two is worth its weight in gold when you need it, and I'm going to make sure both the girls know that motto by heart."

I frowned.

"You're going to tell them."

"Someday. Sooner with Katie rather than later."

"...Makes sense."

Frankly, there's no way the girls wouldn't have figured out something funky was going on when I took them over to Chiron's, even if he promised that he'd keep the supernatural side of things on the down low when they were over at the house.

Somehow.

Still, I didn't know how to feel about this.

About any of it.

My bog standard and ordinary uncle pulling something like this out of the blue should have been a shock, but I swallowed it down quickly, too many things on my mind to stop and stare.

...

My great-grandmother was Hecate, wasn't she?

I hadn't thought about that much in the time since I'd found out, but maybe I should, at some point down the line.

Food for thought.

"So what now? Anything else you want to spring on me?"

Please, don't spring anything else on me.

"That's rich coming from you, buddy, but no. Not today." He waved me off and picked the real cup back up again. The other one vanished in without so much as a whisper of sound. "Go get your cousin, and for the love of all that's good in this world, don't be late. I'm already going to be losing sleep tonight, and I'm not losing time from lunch too."

...​

So.

That happened.

I jogged down the driveway and out onto the streets of Maple with my mind a thousand miles away, trying to deal with a whole bunch of thoughts and feelings that felt three sizes too big for the inside of my skull.

Most of them fit in easily enough with some work.

The parts that didn't were giving me a headache.

I'll let you guess which was which.

Point is, I was distracted, but here's the funny thing: that word meant something entirely different to me than to most people after nearly a year's worth of training with Chiron and his brutal sneak attacks, so the second I sensed something that felt not unlink eyes aimed at the back of my head, I very carefully started slowing down.

Then, just as slowly - and ready to teleport and call out my weapons and armour in a flash if I needed to - I turned around.

There was nobody there.

The street was empty.

Then I turned to the side, and there it was.

I was running past Maple's local Church, only a turn away from Katie's karate class, and I didn't notice anything off until I nearly left it behind.

It was nothing special to look at.

Whitewashed stone walls worn by age, a steepled roof, stained glass windows that were tall and narrow, and all of it built just beyond a cobbled stone path.

And, naturally, one big iron cross just nailed over the large wooden doors.

All very cliché - I'd been inside only once after Aunt Sarah's cousin had come by one time for Thanksgiving. He took us down for about a half hour to pray, and after that, we hadn't set foot in the place again.

Not even once.

I'm pretty sure Uncle David had something to do with that, now that I think about it, because I remember them arguing about it in muffled voices in the middle of the night, but I didn't know why then.

Didn't really care, either.

I have an idea or two now, with the benefit of hindsight, but the point stands.

The Church wasn't a big deal.

Except...

I looked at the iron cross again, and for whatever reason, I felt... wary.

Careful.

Like I was being observed, even though my senses were so sharp at this point that a butterfly couldn't flap its wings down the street without me knowing about it.

An idea bubbled up in my head, wild and more than a little outrageous, and I promptly jumped it and punched it down to size with speed.

No.

Forget about it.

We're not going there.

I quickly walked past the church and turned the corner, heading towards the gym.

I ignored the way a very specific part of my soul - or rather, a very specific something attached to my soul - seemed to... shift, and the way it seemed to tempt me to look back-

"Danny!" Katie slammed into me like a missile, hands wrapping around my stomach in a tight hug, and that mental train of solid nope derailed in a way that almost made me break out into a tap-dancing in routine in relief. "You're back!"

"Yeah, I am. Just for a bit though."

I didn't tell her she'd be coming with.

Not right now.

She pouted, hands on her hips. Her gym clothes were a little sweaty, and her hair was frazzled, but she tried her best to channel Aunt Sarah and it nearly made me pop a blood vessel trying not to laugh.

"That sucks!"

"Don't be like that. I even got you a gift." I winked. "A great one."

That got her to beam again.

"That's awesome! You're the best!"

That time I did laugh, and I waved a hand to her teacher over in the distance to show that she was with me. I guess he must have recognised me alright, because he nodded and gave me a thumbs up.

He also grimaced like he bit into a lemon., but I'm choosing to ignore that.

"Yeah, I totally am, aren't I?"

She kicked me in the shin, already putting those new karate skills to use.

"Not that much."

"Oi! What's that supposed to mean? C'mere!"

She broke out into loud giggles and took off running as I chased after her, always letting her stay ahead by just a few paces.

We made it all the way to the house in laughter, and my nerves eased almost all the way through.

Why wouldn't they?

Things were slotting into place. I could worry about the quest tomorrow, when it was time to leave.

The Church stayed behind, in place and in memory.

Incinerate Anthem had probably been reacting to a place of faith because of its own Holy Nature.

There was nothing else there.

Nothing at all.

...​

That night, I waited until the girls were asleep before I took us over to Chiron's.

It was for the best - if the trip was hard for Sairaorg and I, then it would have been a nightmare and a half for them.

Uncle David and Sarah though...

Yeah, they got the full experience.

Couldn't be helped.

We went in threes, me and one parent per girl, and the only good thing I can say about the jump was that their bags didn't take any space at all - I packed everything into my storage wrist band and there they stayed.

"Grounded." Aunt Sarah rasped, on her knees on the grass out in the garden and looking ready to hurl her soul out. "F-for life."

I winced in sympathy.

And maybe a little pain too, sue me.

"Disowned." Uncle David argued instead, on his feet but only barely. He looked like he'd chugged a carton of curdled milk and then went in for seconds. "You're no nephew of mine."

I raised a glowing hand.

"I can patch you up real quick?"

"Welcome back to the family."

Heh.

Aunt Sarah groaned

"What did I marry into?"

Her husband patted her on the back after I finished laying a Healing Hand Of Asclepius on him and moved onto her.

"You said yes at the altar, woman. No take backs."

"Under false pretences. I barely knew anything about this godly nonsense. For shame."

"False? Please. Unspoken at worst."

"You're sleeping on the couch tonight."

"It's not even our house!"

"Then you're sleeping outside!"

"Can I weigh in on this?"

""Grounded!"" They both snapped.

And to think people believe that I don't come by my sense of humour fairly.

Naturally, that's when Chiron showed up, trotting out of the front door and into the moonlight-

I....

What?

"What happened to you?"

"Whatever do you mean?"

My eye twitched.

Really? Now of all times?

He looked exactly the way he was supposed to from the waist up, decked out in a formal black suit he'd probably, the buttons gleaming in the moonlight.

That was all well and good, but it was from the waist down that things got trippy, because - and follow me on this one - he looked human.

As in, two legs instead of four in a matching set of black dress trousers, and not a hint of horse between them

How even-?

"I thought this appearance would be more appropriate, given that I'd prefer we ease your family into this situation rather than overwhelming them with it all at once. There's been quite enough of that as it is."

...

Good point.

The question still stood though - my eyes weren't quite processing what I was seeing, and I don't think it was just the sheer disconnect of seeing Chiron looking so... I didn't even have the right words for it, but you get the idea.

"Is that shape transfiguration, a perception-altering illusion or some kind of weird spatial warping?"

Maybe even some level of conceptual spell work I didn't know about?

"Why not all three?"

That's... wait.

"Is that it?"

"Jot down your ideas when you have the time and hand them over to me. We'll see how close you get before I give you the answer."

Of course.

Always another lesson, and homework to boot.

I resisted the urge to sigh.

"Excuse me?"

When I looked back, my aunt and uncle were finally up, and looking at my teacher with the kind of guarded intensity of a pair of parents who'd just come face to face with the dude who'd been taking care of their kid for months.

It wasn't pretty, but it wasn't quite hostile.

Right smack dab in between, almost.

"Who are you, exactly?" Uncle David's voice was level, but unyielding. It was actually impressive. "And where are we?"

He didn't hesitate, not that he ever had before.

"I am Chiron, and this is my home." The centaur's eyes twinkled merrily. "Perhaps you've heard of me?"

Aunt Sarah only nodded hesitantly, but my uncle?

His face twisted in shock.

Then in disbelief.

Derision.

Confusion.

And finally, some messy combination of the last three, with a great big heap of something I couldn't place right beneath them as he looked from my nod to Chiron and back again.

"Oh, what fresh hell is this?"

Chiron only smiled politely.

"A whole new world's worth of it, I'm afraid. Now, perhaps you'd like to come in for tea? I have a feeling you're going to have a great many questions for me before the night comes to an end."

And didn't they ever?

...​

I left them with Chiron.

Well, just my aunt and uncle.

Katie and Alex, I tucked into bed myself, and I made sure to leave their new bikes by the front door in the morning.

Chiron would take care of all of them, and that was for the best, because I had no intention of waking them up before Sairaorg and I left.

And speaking of my best friend, I found him after I left the girls' room and closed the door behind me, sitting at the top of the stairs and patiently waiting the night out.

Our eyes met.

"All set?"

"You know it." Everyone I cared about was as safe as could be. I had nothing left to worry about except for what came next. "Packed your bags?"

"Damn straight."

"Awesome. Then we're all set."

"Yeah." His eyes flickered away, looking, and his fists clenched. "Yeah, we are."

In a few hours, the sun would rise, and then it'd officially be time to get this show on the road.

...​

Dawn came eventually.

By the time the first rays of daylight were streaking over to us from the east, we were already outside and nearly vibrating out of our skins in contained pressure.

And excitement.

"Weapons?"

"Check."

"Armour?"

"Check."

"Money in three currencies and assorted treasure for trading if it comes down to it?"

"Check."

"Pet hellhound?"

"Aarf!"

"Atta boy, Courage. Into the shadow you go. What's next- ah. Nectar and emergency healing potions?"

"Check,"

"The amazing Daniel Winchester, to do all the work and look awesome while Sairaorg eats his dust?"

"Go die in a ditch."

"That ditch would become a national monument."

"Don't start." Chiron interrupted us before we really got into it. "You're ready. Or just about there."

Sai and I exchanged a look.

"What's left?

"Me."

Oh.

I kept my face blank as I turned around, and found Regulus himself prowling towards us, an impatient carnivorous snarl pulling his maw.

"Brat." He growled at Sai, who beamed at him with a mega-watt smile so wide my face hurt just looking at it. Then his eyes narrowed at me. "Sun brat."

"Kill stealer."

His eyes narrowed some more.

"Still running your mouth."

"It's how I roll." I didn't sense any kind of anger or bloodlust from him, so I felt perfectly safe. Also, Chiron was right there, and I'd like to see the damn cat try something with me with him at my back. It'd be hilarious. "If you didn't want the name to stick, you shouldn't have earned it."

"I can still eat you."

"Sai, your pity-spar is acting all moody. Tell him to grab a Snickers and leave, we're busy."

"You little-"

"Actually-" Chiron's voice overrode the Nemean Lions' wit a single word, even if it was nothing deliberately overbearing. "-Regulus is coming with you."

...

...

...

"What?"

"Yes!"

"Can we get started?"

"No, hold up, wait." I pointed at the giant yawning lion, who I'd bet good money was only doing that to show off his absurdly sharp-looking teeth. "Why is the living Longinus coming on a quest with us?"

"Think about that question for one second, and you'll have your answer. If you don't, I'll have thoroughly and completely failed as a teacher."

...

Right. That was stupid as bricks.

Because he was a living Longinus, obviously.

"But why would he want to?" I whirled on Regulus. "Why would you want to?"

"I was bored." Credit for theatrics and all, because he even sounded like it too. "The brat mentioned something about a quest, and I decided to tag along. Deal with it."

I turned to Sairaorg, who shrugged unrepentantly.

"Not sorry. Didn't think it was a big deal." He looked at Regulus. "You really want to come?"

"I'm bored." The lion repeated, voice an irritated rumble. "I'd do just about anything for a bit of action, no matter how pitiful it turns out in the long run."

"Great!"

Regulus snorted.

"Where are we going, and who are we going to fight? What's all this noise about?"

That pulled me up short.

"Wait, you didn't tell him anything?" I stressed the word again. "Anything?"

Chiron raised a brow.

"That would ruin the surprise, no?"

"..."

"..."

My lips twitched.

Alright then.

"Tell me what?" Regulus must have sensed the sudden change in my mood because his mane shifted a little and he sounded a lot more suspicious than he had before. "What am I missing?"

"Nothing." I bared my teeth at him in an expression that had to be something close to pure evil. "Nothing at all, kill-stealer. Ready to leave?"

He glared at me.

I glared back.

"Watch your back, sun brat."

Strangely, the threat didn't quite feel like one.

Then he prowled away and started lazily circling Sairaorg.

"...I don't like cats."

"Riveting," Chiron said dryly, before his expression sobered again. "It's time for you to leave."

The air went sharp with tension, and we straightened under his gaze.

It was the only this we could do.

"We've got this, Chiron." I grinned and zipped up my new hoodie, eyes meeting. "We've got all the supplies we could ever need, two Longinus gears between us, and you gave me that thing we talked about the other day, just in case."

A little maybe-trump card that could come in real handy if things go bad.

"We're not going to fail." Sairaorg agreed, standing tall and proud. His new gauntlets gleamed in the rising sunlight as he ran a hand through his "I've been waiting for this forever. We'll be back with the Fleece in no time."

"Fleece?" Regulus murmured, but it wasn't a question meant for us, and nobody answered him anyway.

Chiron was still looking at us all, very carefully.

He met my eyes.

Then Sai's.

He even stared at Regulus, and some kind of understanding passed between them that had even the Nemean Lion himself nodding, not subserviently, but in a gesture that was almost respectful.

At the bare minimum, it was an acknowledgment.

Chiron accepted it easily.

Then he smiled, warmly, proudly, and backed away just a little.

"I have no doubts.'

Four words, but in that moment they might as well have carried all the meaning in the world.

"Still, I expect you back within... let's say two weeks, at the absolute latest. Otherwise, I'll have to find a way to come after you myself, and I'll be most upset when I find you."

And the funny thing is?

I totally believed him.

Time to hit the road.

"See you then, Teach."

I raised a hand and grabbed Sairaorg's shoulder. The other slid along Regulus's muscled back with only a single instinctive warning growl that he swallowed a second later.

Prissy cat.

I took a deep breath.

To infinity and beyond, I guess.

Then a familiar feeling inside of me Sparked and ignited, and we vanished off the face of the planet.

...​

If you're thinking to yourself 'this is the point where something goes hilariously off the rails'... then congratulations, because you're a prophet!

Now shove it and pay attention.

In the end, it was probably Regulus.

No, I wasn't just throwing shade his way this time.

It was his 'weight', or power, or maybe the combination of it with all our gear and Incinerate Anthem to boot.

Whatever it was, I knew something was wrong the second we dropped into the infinite, blinding void between worlds.

And I do mean dropped - just like what happened the first time I tried to bring Sairaorg along on a jump with me, instead of soaring across one world to the next, we tumbled straight down between an endless number of them, drowning in everything and nothing at all.

A misfire.

Damn it, damn it, damn it!

What the hell kind of start is this!

Space ceased to be. Colours that weren't colours rushed by, and existence that had no right existing at all expanded around us without limit as we fell.

It was only a moment, but it lasted forever, and just like before, I couldn't get us back to my world - the one I'd been aiming for - or the one we'd just come from without having 'solid' ground underneath my feet.

A whole new world, then.

And so that's what I did - that's where I took us.

I screamed into the void, distantly feeling Sairaorg do the same, and the force of Regulus's furious roars echoing up my arm, tangled up in his mane.

Then my gut twisted, and my ears popped in a downright spiritual way as we tore headfirst out of the void and into... another void?

Come again?

We slammed down into a floor that was a floor, and immediately froze.

Literally.

We physically could not move, not one of us - Even Regulus couldn't, for all that I could feel his absolute fury mounting with every passing beat, like a bomb gearing up to blow.

There was nothing around us but air and colour - dark, flickering, like endless paint that had run together until everything under it was tinted in shades of grey and black and sparking purple.

Only I didn't think there was anything under it or us either - but there was someone above it all.

I could see him, just barely.

Suspended high in my line of sight, reclined on a seat that was simple and unassuming, and still felt like a throne higher than any I'd ever imagined, staring down at us with eyes that glowed in a shade of pure crimson.

An old man in purple aristocratic clothes highlighted with gold, whose age I couldn't place, face blank, hands idly gripping his seat's armrests and radiating a presence so monstrous I couldn't even fathom the depths of it.

Like Chiron at his most overwhelming, or my dad when he wasn't reeling himself in for my sake.

Spoiler: Spoiler


Well this is off to a great gods-damned start, isn't it?

I stared up at him, frozen, and he stared down at us, assessing, and we stayed like that for the longest and most threatening solid minute of my life.

Then, slowly, almost glacially, his gloved hand rose to stroke at his beard.

"Well." His voice was deep and polished, rumbling with effortless might, and no accent I could place at all. "What an interesting day this is turning out to be."

Then he raised his other hand, and a kaleidoscope of colours exploded out of his palm and swallowed us all in one blast.

...​

Somewhere else entirely:

There was no sense of transition.

I didn't go to sleep, or feel time passing, or any kind of a change at all.

Neither did Sairaorg and Regulus for that matter.

One second we were staring at what had to have been certain death right in the blood-red eye, and the next, reality glitched, and we were spat out somewhere else entirely.

My feet hit the ground hard, and I managed to blink spots out of my eyes and meet another pair - also bright red, because why not at this point?

The spearman looked back at me with an unashamedly gobsmacked expression, weapon held loosely at his side, decked out in a blue body suit, shining silver armour over that and some kind of ceremonial-looking fur thrown over one shoulder.

Spoiler: Spoiler


"Who the hell-?" He started, something more stunned than immediately hostile in his voice, and that's about as far as he got before I moved.

I snapped out my left hand and blasted him with a blast of sunlight so bright it tinted all our surroundings gold - some kind of expansive, indoor garden nearly two stories high, complete with an indoor pond and everything - and Serpent's Downfall materialised in my grip in the same instant.

"Talking isn't a free action!"

The beam smacked him head first and blasted him straight across into the wall behind him, and he rammed into it with a burst of uprooted earth and shattering drywall.

He wasn't down for the count though, I could tell that much.

Not even close.

Where exactly where-?

Something shifted behind me, and I heard Regulus shift and Sai move to shove me aside before the world behind us did what it usually tended to do with concerning consistency and erupted with a burst of light that was absolutely not my own.

And then it expanded, fast.

All of us leaped back, demigod, devil and Nemean Lion at once, instincts screaming.

Something fundamental shifted, something in the pillar of light threatened to blast us all off our feet. It was so bright - unnaturally so - that I couldn't see through it, and that was kind of telling all on its own.

I caught glimpses, though.

A spell circle, not at all like any other one I'd ever seen. A spark of something else, too.

A figure.

Something - someone - important.

Space shifted. The air charged as power filled it, and a fifth presence descended among us.

No, scratch that.

A sixth.

I saw the girl with the glasses right as the light started to fade - fallen across the floor, knees drawing back like she was trying to curl up into a ball and disappear, expression torn between lingering fear and total awe.

She couldn't have been more than a few years older than me and Sairaorg - for crying out loud, she was even dressed in a school uniform!

The person who dropped down in front of her, though...

My eyes widened.

Blonde.

Armoured in shining plate from head to toe, elaborate with something that might have been a hood descending from its back, and more flowing blue cloth drifting down from above its waist, rippling in the breeze his arrival had kicked up.

"Do not fear, master." His voice was calm and measured, and dignified beyond words. Royal, even. "I am Saber, a servant who will protect you."

Spoiler: Spoiler



His eyes, though?

They were a sharp blueish green, and they hardened as they roamed across all of us.

He raised his hands up and closed them across nothing in particular, I could see, before taking a stance that made it look like he was brandishing an invisible sword and preparing to swing it into action.

Somehow, it was more intimidating than just about anything I'd ever had aimed my way.

"Against any and every threat."



​
Well, that's encouraging.

Then something clicked up top for me.

My brain ran back the tapes for a second, and the words finally registered.

Saber.

...

...

...

No. Freaking. Way.




...
