#8,939
Onwards!

Lavinia:

Two in front. Five closing in from above.

More beyond even that.

Lavinia clocked them all in the first heartbeat, even as her wand manifested in her grip with a familiar twist, immaculate and ready for battle.

Whatever else there was to say of it, she had spent her childhood in Oz, and Grauzerber after that.

The ability to fight back when danger came calling had been nigh-literally carved into her through - and regardless of - blood, sweat and tears, and self-defence came in many forms.

Some more proactive than others.

The moment the spell circle shattered, having successfully warped them away, she was already surging into action.

Calculations primed.

Detection spells cast.

Reinforcement matrices deployed.

No time for panic. No time for second-guessing.

In a distant, barely acknowledged way, after the months of slowly winding pressure that had culminated in this black, wretched day, the clearing of thoughts was almost a relief.

"Surrender!"

Then the first black-draped figure punched through the rust-red sand blowing across the air, sword smoldering with the glow to match, and she immediately discarded relief in favor of throwing her arm out in a wide, sweeping arc.

Boom.

Force answered, folding the air backwards in a wave that heaved up sand and stone and hurled them outward with such violence that even their passing could have flayed flesh from bone and ground what was left to dust.

As it was, it bought her a second and change - and that was enough.

Her first opponent was launched away with the wave, his feet clawing for footing and his blade wrenched out of his grip as he disappeared behind a cloud of red.

Two more landed and lunged in from the left in that same heartbeat, synchronised and armed with the same instruments she'd caught sight of before - like writhing rags come to life, wreathed in a film of warping colours - and that was about as far as Lavinia allowed them to come.

Three.

One step, and she pivoted on her heel, wand slashing down in a sharp, unforgiving strike.

Two.

Light that only she could see instantly bloomed in her vision, tracing a straightforward pattern.

Lines, vertical and horizontal, interlocking into a square grid that stretched out across her entire line of sight.

Seemingly simple. Deceptively harmless.

Then, with a thought and a flick of her wand, she propelled it forward at blinding speed.

One.

The first of them - the closest - didn't even have time to scream.

Invisible lines cleaved through him, slicing flesh and bone with surgical, unfeeling cruelty. His blank mask shattered with an implosion of shredded gore, in sync with severed limbs, decimated armour, and a shower of formerly internal organs that splattered into the red sand like wet confetti.

The second tried to surge back, kicking off the air itself with a burst of magic and desperate fervor, but she'd cast wide for a reason.

A lattice of sure-fire cuts sliced into and across him mid-motion, eviscerating his form so thoroughly that all that remained was a splash of mutilated viscera, slowly splashing away in the stream of her accelerated perception.

Utterly dismantled.

Monstrous in effect and efficiency, but the necessity of it would sicken her to her stomach later.

Now, in the moment, there was only survival.

Needs must.

The remainder of the first wave closed in on her.

Another pair shimmered into being at the exact limits of her sensory field,
skimming over the edges at a brutal rush.

A third shadow charged her head on, figure blurring forwards in a dead sprint - bladed again this time, the metal coated in a sheen of white-blue flames fierce enough that she could feel the heat burn against her skin from twenty paces off.

The last of them - the first one she'd swept away, already recovered - fell from far above, riding the curtain of debris she'd hurled into the sky and using it as a smokescreen to drop back into the carnage.

Lavinia adjusted without blinking.

No grid this time - spatial manipulation was too complex, too costly, and best used sparingly.

Instead, vector arrays formed in her mind's eye, half an instant before she actualised them into roving spell circles surrounding the pair rushing in from the left.

Energy poured out on command, spiking their raw speed several times over - well past any hope of control - before their trajectories were abruptly rewritten, snapping sideways and slamming them into each other with a savage burst of impact.

A flash of light followed - not her work - and what looked like strips of fabric snaked out from their point of collision, unfurling like rending cloth that twisted around and swallowed the pair of them in one ravenous pulse.

By the time they hit the ground, it was in a pale, ceramic-smooth cocoon - impermeable from head to toe - that went skidding away wildly as it bled off their combined momentum.

Sealing magic, then, and something almost surely intended for her.

Predictable.

Lavinia had suspected as much, and the confirmation - or the surreal, borderline ridiculous sight it made - didn't so much as put a hitch in her stride.

Two down. Two to go.

One dead ahead, sword ablaze, and another descending from on high.

Without hesitation, she slackened her grip on her Sacred Gear's power, and the temperature of the wasteland around her plummeted like it'd been pitched off the edge of a cliff with a running start.

A torrent of ice and swelling frost thundered out towards the fool coming at her, lethal and overwhelming - and to his credit, he managed to react to it.

It just didn't help.

The fire-coated sword swung out in a fevered arc, and the flames flared and billowed out to meet them, but they might as well have been a candle in the heart of a hurricane.

The frigid deluge snuffed them out in a single flash, and weapon and wielder both disappeared under the rushing roar that followed, with a faint echo of a wail and the shattering shriek of rhime-glazed metal.

Then they were gone.

At the same time, with only a fleeting touch of will, her Doll stirred with her gear's power, manifesting another spectral, disjointed limb that tore out into the world and intercepted her last attacker near as quickly as she herself could register the action.

Long, eerie fingers seized their victim in an inescapable grip, heedless of the violent, desperate flailing, and then - for the second time in as many minutes - they clenched down.

"▂ ! ▂ ! ▂"

The horrendous sound of his death was something she refused to focus on, and a wafting cloud of red streaked mist escaped the hand's grip, raining down against the sand in half-frozen shards.

Which was...

Don't lose focus.

She swallowed once and inhaled lightly - a sharp, steadying pull without lowering her guard, soured all the way through by the scent of iron and death clogging the air, and that was as far as she was allowed to go.

"My, my."

Two words, and Lavinia's lungs and most of the blood turned to ice in a way that had nothing to do with her Longinus.

She knew that voice.

"Look who's all grown up."

She didn't answer with words - she didn't even bother looking.

Her wand snapped up and fired.

"!"

Air ionised and ripped outward with a roar and a hail of white-blue arcs, overlaying and snapping in a cascade that scorched sand to glass and carved a trench through the wasteland.

When it struck, the lightning sheared the jagged spire she'd aimed at nearly in half.

Lavinia was gone before the rest of the ledge crumbled into dust, bending space with a hasty spell-circle and shifting over to the peak of the next one over-

"Boo!"

Something skin-curling ghosted over the nape of her neck, and she lashed out with her ice even as she shifted again, leaping away with an iceberg in her wake and a rush of blood suddenly pounding in her ears.

She landed on the next spire-

Something moved in the corner of her vision-

-and frozen barriers erupted upwards in threefold arrays.

This time, they lasted only until a barrage of flames and something distinctly twisted bored through them like glass.

Thwoom.

Shards fractured off like razors, steam hissed, and she was gone before the smoke even cleared.

She reappeared again-

Another scream of power cut through the air towards her, and this time her Doll manifested an entire limb to intercept it.

Phantasmal fingers closed around something fiery and patched through with green-black rot, and whatever spell sequence held it together immediately destabilized.

Catastrophically.

The desert whited out under the blast, and the gale it kicked off nearly launched her off her feet and into the side of the shattered crag.

Damn it all.

She bit into her reserves and translocated for a fifth time in under a minute, vanishing into a shimmer of warped space just as the trailing winds tore the rock formation behind her apart.

When she materialised this time, it was with a half dozen sigils shimmering in her orbit, her Gear primed on a hair trigger, and her sensory field flared as far out as it would go without risking overload.

But no attack came - not right then.

Instead, it was laughter.

"Hah!"

The sound echoed over the flats, loud and deliberately grating, before its owner shifted in just outside her immediate casting range.

The distortion was powerful enough to kick a cloud of sand ten feet high, but that wasn't a hindrance.

Lavinia could see through it just fine, and what - who -waited beyond made her grip on her wand go white-knuckled.

By appearance alone, the girl was in her age bracket - a year older at most - but that was where the similarities ended.

Dark hair, pale face, and grey eyes blown so wide they seemed pupilless.

A stiff skirt and black layered fabric under open robes accented with streaks of silver.

One hand carried a black wand, but the other closed around the hilt of a jagged dagger with an edge that caught the light like bleached, serrated bone.

And that demented smile.

"Hiya, Lav-lav."

Walburga.

Augusta Hawthorne's prized apprentice, and a mad dog that even that famously ruthless woman had known to keep on a leash, for good reason.

Only right then, that leash was nowhere to be seen.

"Did ya miss me?"

Without a word, Lavinia wrenched her wand up to meet hers, and the desert between them became a cataclysm.

...​

Dan:

'How many people have I killed today?'

Not the kind of thing someone stops to consider in the middle of a fight, but the thought still came to me as I broke through another guard and jabbed Serpent's Downfall through another would-be assassin's side.

His body convulsed, acrid smoke and muffled screaming rising up from under the blank mask.

The fire seared him from the inside out - the armour actually held out somewhat - before I yanked left and tore the spear through his ribs and clean out the rest of his body in the same unbroken motion.

The gaping wound was cauterized with the swipe, and he was dead well before I lashed out and kicked what was left of him into the next idiot coming my way.

One more added to the count - and so what?

They swung first - literally - and they weren't done trying, either.

I leapt forward, and another three came swinging at me.

Or tried to, at least - they scattered like bowling pins when I hurled myself at them, half-coated in light and fire and with all the grace of a Cretan bull in a china shop.

Two of them tried to flank me on either side, but it only took a flicker of will to flare the corona of heat and pressure around me outwards, driving them back and flattening the rock beneath us into a flash-scorched mess.

Then I rounded on the odd one out.

Serpent's Downfall swept up to deflect the sword that streaked for my head, vibrating in my grip as steel glanced off its edge and skidded wide.

Then I rolled my wrists and let it slide, gliding with the momentum and
driving the butt down into his knee.

It folded with a wet crack.

He went down howling, and the next swipe was a wild thing that bounced off my armour harmlessly as I stepped into it, swiveled, and rammed the spearhead straight down through the mask and into whatever it was that passed for face under there.

No resistance.

Grisly sounds echoed out as gore and broken mask fragments scattered everywhere, and I... didn't pay too much attention to the view in the middle.

The action was gruesome enough as is.

Keep going. Process later.

On cue, something came hurtling through my flames at speed - a length of gleaming chain headed right toward me.

I ripped Serpent's Downfall free and twisted to deflect it, but it wasn't aiming for my center mass - instead, it blitzed in at an angle and snapped around my arm guard, catching tightly.

Really?

I saw the heaving yank coming a mile away - who wouldn't?

My feet dug into the ground as my stance firmed and my muscles coiled.

When the pull came - barely a split second later - whoever was on the other end didn't get another to realize I wasn't going anywhere.

Instead, I grabbed the chain, yanked it taut, and swung.

The noisy black blur on the other end followed suit, lifting off and whipping past the smoke and flames between us like a yo-yo swinging into a wall.

Only the wall here was a jagged, unforgiving cliffside.

He caught on a little over halfway there, letting go of the chain and flailing wildly as he tried to stick the landing-

"!"

-before I was suddenly there in a flash of gold, lancing out with another kick that sent him careening headfirst into a world of hurt.

Boom.

The collision went off like a tank shell, driving him through dust and stone and cratering it around him - and going by the way his legs twitched and went slack, that was the end of that.

Another one-

"Pathetic!"

There you are.

I soared back, rising out of the way as another figure bullrushed me, bloodlust pouring like a broken faucet.

The dragon-masked head honcho himself, who landed below and shot me a glare that was all pure murder.

"Finally come back out to play?"

He growled, low and sharp, and I grinned meanly.

For all that he was obviously stronger than the rest, he hadn't committed at the beginning.

Not really.

The rest of them had come right at me, but he'd hung back, skimming the edge of the fight.

Then he'd blitz in quickly, snapping off a slash or a heavy strike before backing off again.

Trying to work out my patterns? Or tire me out?

It didn't matter.

The herd was thinned now, and I'd win either way.

"You will die."

"Right. Never heard-"

I accelerated mid-word, plunging and striking so hard the air tunneled around me.

"-that-!"

Dragon Mask caught it against the flat of his sword - black-bladed, and different from the rest, I could tell - and the wail of power rippling between it and Serpent's Downfall was bloodcurdling.

"-before!"

He snarled and crouched with the blow, folding his body and jerking aside to break the bind, and I followed the momentum, dropping the rest of the way instead of forcing the strike.

Dragon Mask tried to capitalise on that, surging in high and fast, and I snapped the spear across my body to intercept the slash.

Wood shuddered, and metal vibrated as I let it glance off, turning with the force and rounding back with a sharp thrust.

He curved out of its way, blade snapping up to knock the shaft wide - something flickered - and I pressed in, sweeping Serpent's Downfall out to carve space, before reversing it into another jab.

His sword met it both times, first with the flat, and again with the edge, and I felt it every time - the aura it gave off.

Angry.

Rabid.

Chomping at the bit - and my spear was reacting to it, thrumming with the growing pressure of orange-gold fire the longer the fight dragged on.

Like the weapons despised and contested one another on principle.

"I don't suppose you want to call it quits-"

Dragon Mask lunged, and sword and spear met three more times - rapid-fire contacts that had us darting back and forth until my foot met his chest hard enough to send him skidding through a boulder and hissing in absolute fury.

"-and tell me who you are now, do you?"

My eyes narrowed as he straightened into another ready stance.

"Also, nice try."

"Enough."

He swung again, and the vicious stroke carried on past him, projecting a razor-thin band of energy that scythed vertically at both ends and split the spire we stood on clean down the middle.

Of course.

This time, the quality was all different from the rest - more power, more weight - and I twisted to the left as it passed, just as the footing started to crumble out beneath me.

Then, in that one moment of reaction-

"Balance Breaker-"

My stomach dropped.

Excuse you!?

The blade was extended, pointed right at me, but the rest of the words came through even as I reflexively went to hurl my spear at him.

"-Depths Of The Coiling Serpent!"

Too late.

The aura I'd sensed before raged outwards, expanding and glitching without end, and suddenly I was staring down a horizon of roaring water, barrelling right towards me.

...​

Lavinia:

Spellfire collided hard enough to rattle the teeth - rows and rows of clashing lights meeting like arcing fireworks - and Lavinia didn't stop moving once.

Anything less would have been suicide.

She slid sideways through warped space before a whip of corrosive black flame carved through her former footing, wailing through the ice and gouging a molten groove into the ground below.

Then she fired back, throwing her hand down with a flare of cold.

A hail storm swirled to life above them, and jagged icicles began falling out of the sky in a ruinous cascade.

Hundreds - too fast by half - shattering with lethal, vibrational pulses that left everything they touched flash-frozen on contact.

Walburga only cackled again - the deranged lunatic - and began sprinting through them.

The barrage battered against her wards - they flared with light and spider-webbing cracks as she ran - slowing her a hair, but she still bore down on Lavinia like a starving predator scenting blood.

"I can play too, you know!"

The witch's wand arm swung wide, and a cyclone of sand erupted around her, glass-scorched and glittering with superimposed heat.

Lavinia bit down on an ugly curse and thrust her own wand out to counter it.

The sandstorm buckled, yanked back on invisible reins, and another flick of her wrist sent it heaving back-

Just in time for something massive to skitter out at her.

A familiar!?

It was enormous - eight towering and many-jointed legs, a blur of blackened and armoured chitin the size of an elephant for a body, and more poison-green eyes in its mandible-crowded face than Lavinia cared to count.

She'd never been fond of spiders.

Spiders of monstrous size racing towards her with murderous intent didn't do much for her general opinion of arachnids.

The hands of her Doll manifested between her and the rampaging creature on command.

It tried to leap for them with a grace that was terrifyingly wrong for something of that shape or size to possess, only for narrow, pointed fingers to plunge into its chitin mid-motion with a shrill, awful sound not unlike metal being punctured through.

It screeched as they burrowed and twisted inside of it, legs flailing wildly, but it was no use.

Inevitably, the giant carapace quickly came apart from the inside, fragments of broken armour and pulverized internals flying off with every desperate - and futile - scramble for escape.

Then, with one twisting, ferocious tug, the spider was viciously pulled
in half, legs spasming and stilling as its insides spilled out in a wave of foul-smelling and discoloured sludge.

It wasn't a satisfying sight - in any sense.

The myriad eyes hadn't even begun dimming before Lavinia's attention snapped away.

A shimmer.

A tiny, minuscule distortion at the corner of her vision - one that wasn't a haze of heat, or the wafting scraps of spellwash.

That's-!

She threw out a barrier spell just before the illusion peeled away, and Walburga dove at it - at her - with a grin split wide across her face.

The dagger struck the ward and rebounded hard enough to echo, three times in quick succession.

Only each time it did, the blade - wrong and vile, dripping with something dangerous - didn't slide or curve away.

It bit.

Fracture-lines raced out from each point of impact in sudden bursts, ringing with a brittle, glassy notes that had her gritting her teeth and unthinkingly reinforcing it.

Then her mind caught up, and she threw the knee-jerk impulse away in favour of something altogether more immediate.

A flare of ozone was the only tell.

Walburga's eyes grew wide, and she vanished just as another bolt of lightning ripped through the shield, blasting it to fading sparks and lighting up the desert with a brilliant, blinding flash.

Powerful, but useless.

The narrow escape wasn't surprising - Walburga had always been a slippery, twisted little thing.

Granted, they had never duelled one another before, but Lavinia had seen it happen, and that was enough.

When Walburga reappeared in the distance again, all traces of alarm were wiped clean, and the smile was untouched.

Of course it was.

"Whoo! That was sooo close," she crooned, tilting her head this way and that. "You're fun now, Lav-Lav! So much fun!"

The sickly joy radiating off her was almost as thick as whatever it was that still dripped from her dagger.

"I'm glad!" She sounded like a child savouring a new toy, and Lavinia grimaced even as the words registered in her head. "I was afraid this would be boring."

"What is this?"

Despite the shared circumstances, they hardly knew one another.

She had always been unsettling and off in ways that prickled at the skin, and the last time they'd crossed paths had been one of the vanishingly few times they'd interacted at all, at a gathering of Oz's younger talent before Lavinia had headed off to Grauzerberer..

Walburga had been there on her lonesome, master nowhere in sight, and she'd started an altercation with three other young magicians from famed and respected houses - prodding and poking with that barbed tongue until they challenged her in full view of everyone present.

What happened next...

The luckiest of them ended up with a spine so completely shattered it might as well have been reduced to salt.

The second scion had his arms transfigured into unsightly, ravenous things with too many teeth that immediately curled back and tried to devour themselves - and him too.

The last...

The memory was something that had been thoroughly seared into Lavinia's brain.

How could it not?

Walburga had quite literally turned the girl inside out - and kept her alive and screaming after the fact, just like she had the other two.

Deliberately.

It had firmly cemented her reputation, and even her immediate disappearance from the public eye didn't diminish it.

If anything, it only made her all the more infamous.

That had been the last time Lavinia had set eyes on her...

Until now.

"What are you doing here, Walburga?"

"Pursuing gainful employment!" She chirped, spinning once on her heel. "Hazard pay included. Flexible hours. Lots of screaming - and dental too!"

Her grin widened when Lavinia didn't react.

Not visibly, at least, even as her thoughts roiled.

"Oh, don't give me that look. Now that home's gone kaput-"

Oz.

"And all the old fogies are either dead, wishing they were, or... you know, worthless." She sneered quickly, before the expression cleared off. "A girl like me has to make her own way in the world. And I did!"

"Did you?"

It pained her to indulge the unashamed psychopath, but her capacity for spellwork wasn't infinite, nor was her stamina endless.

She wasn't at her limit yet, but the longer Walburga spoke, the more time Lavinia had to recover and prepare.

And both of them knew it.

"Absolutely! Got myself hired by a few try-hard rejects who have a bone to pick with those Principle Clan Shinto nuts to the east." She shrugged carelessly. "Both our old hags worked with them over the years, if you can believe it."

Old hag-?

The meaning hit, and her spine locked ramrod straight.

"What?"

Walburga didn't miss the shift in her tone, and her mood shifted into something adjacent to a cat creeping up on a canary.

Barbed with teeth.

"The more you know, right? Something, something, research collaboration, and blah blah blah." She tapped the tip of her dagger against her shoulder with exaggerated boredom. "Even the human experiments and the lab rats were boring. Can you imagine?"

Lavinia felt bile crawling up her throat, hot and sour, but she held back the urge to strike.

Not yet.

"Then again, if nothing else..."

Walburga glanced off to the side, tapping her wand against her lower lip, and cast her focus on the mangled corpse of her spider familiar.

"The new-fangled pets aren't half bad. Prototype Utsusemi, whatever that means. I wasn't paying attention."

Lavinia wouldn't believe a lie like that on pain of death - the threat of which was very much still on the table - and she didn't know what the name meant herself, but the carcass...

She didn't dare turn her attention away from Walburga, but just a glimpse was enough to realize that it was ... dissolving?

Breaking down, at least in part-?

Wait.

Pets.

Plural.

"There it is!"

Lavinia moved, just as the sand beneath her heaved up, and an enormous maw lunged up to swallow her whole.

How did she not sense-!

No, focus.

Walburga's cackles followed her as she sprinted off to the side, crystallizing the air under her into a temporary foothold and priming another spell array on the fly.

The 'pet' followed through the whirlwind of raining sand - a massive rust-coated salamander with grotesquely engorged pale-yellow eyes and a long, gnarled tongue lashing out after her.

It never made contact.

To hell with restraint - Lavinia aimed at it, and a bubble of crushing gravity snapped into place around it, compressing it inward from all sides.

The salamander froze mid-lunge, limbs thrashing uselessly, tongue folding back from whence it came... for all of one second.

Then its resistance failed, and the shape of it crumpled like a tin can, complete with gushing fluids spraying at grotesque speeds, and-

"Got you!"

-It was all the opening Walburga needed.

The dagger was suddenly right there, punching through her shields.

Walburga was an irrelevant spot of colour, directing it, and the edge nicked just under Lavinia's left temple, carving a line down across her cheek and grazing her jawbone.


Ṕ̵͍Ă̴̡I̸̝͆N̵̟̈
​

There was no delay.

Cold metal parted flesh, and the poison exploded inside her like molten fire, a white-hot surge that mutilated her nerves and turned everything beneath her skin to acid.

Every thought, spell, and ounce of self-control was shredded into nothingness, and her heart may have even stopped dead in its tracks.

That was just the first two seconds.

The third kicked in, and her vision fractured into a spiral of sand, sky, and excruciating agony as she tumbled violently to the ground.

The landing didn't register - for a subjective eternity, she couldn't even tell which way was up.

Then, somehow, it got worse.

She didn't understand how she'd ended up on her hands and knees, wand out of her grasp, heaving and wretching soundlessly - only dimly aware of black, vein-like streams burning their way across her pale skin - but there she was.

She may have been sobbing, too.

Or maybe that was just the blood on her face.

Either way, the suffering continued to burrow in deeper, and Walburga stood over her, drinking it all in with an air of absolute satisfaction.

"Fomorian beast venom. Watered down, but still…" She twirled the dagger in her grip and gave Lavinia a slow, considering look. "Hurts, doesn't it?"

Lavinia couldn't breathe.

Walburga's face twisted with naked delight.

"I always did want to ruin that gorgeous little face of yours - and oh, would you look at that."

She crouched and pressed her fingers against the bloody cut, right along Lavinia's jaw.

The touch sent a fresh spike of hell through Lavinia's skull, sharp enough that it almost drowned out the poison's burn.

Almost.

"We're off to a great start."

"-W-why?"

The sound barely qualified as a word, torn raw from her throat, but Walburga heard it anyway.

"I told you, Lav-Lav!" Another light, almost loving pat. "I've got a job now, and you're it. Some very angry little nobodies want to ask you a few questions - they worked with your old master, and now that she's a goner, you're the runner-up - but don't worry!"

She leaned closer, until their foreheads nearly touched.

"They'll see how much use they can squeeze out of you, and after that?"

Her breath was warm and thick with anticipation as she smiled.

"You're all mine - and so is that Sacred Gear inside you."

...

...

...

Ah.

...

...

...

So it all came back to that.

To Glenda.

And-

...

...

...

"All you have ever been worth... is that Sacred Gear you possess."

...

...

...

It was always the same.

...

...

...


Lavinia's head rose.

Slowly. Like she was moving through molasses, and it lolled out of her control twice before she managed it.

But she did.

She looked right up, and stared Walburga dead in the grey, malevolent eyes.

The monster stared right back, possessive and expectant.

…

…

…

Augusta. Glenda. Walburga.

All the lies and the hideous blackness, overlapping in her mind's eye.

Identical.

…

…

…

They were all the same.

…

…

…

"H-a-ha-ah"

It wasn't a laugh - not truly.

Just a breaking point.

Walburga's expression shuttered into something confused, then irritated, then distinctly panicked - but the damage was already done.

She should have killed her when she had the chance.

"H-av-ve it you-r w̸a̸y̷."

Power ignited.

Reality recoiled with a thunderclap of a wail, and a familiar pair of limbs manifested above her-

But this was different.

The manifestation didn't stop at mere incomplete limbs, but swelled further as those fingers grabbed onto the air itself and used it as a handhold, pulling the rest of itself into existence.

It arrived, and the wailing fell into alien silence.

A glassy, gleaming form.

Four slender arms on either side of it.

An expressionless, mouthless face.

Six voided eyes glimmered on its leftmost side, unblinking, unfeeling, and fixed on the spot Walburga had just flickered out of.

Running?

Where to?

Why even try?

She wanted Lavinia's Longinus, didn't she?

They all did.

By all means - they were welcome to it.


Let them have an Absolute Demise!​

Despite the poison, despite the pain, Lavinia found it in herself to raise her head one more time, and laugh.

Somewhere along the way, it became a s̴̨̑c̵̳͐r̶̘̍͝e̴̲̞̔ǎ̶̜ͅm̷̞̈.

And the unsealed husk of a dead goddess screamed right along with her.


...

B̴a̷l̶a̵n̸c̵e̸ ̸B̸r̴e̷a̴k̵e̶r̴:̵ ̶A̸̛̘s̷̹̓s̴̲̎o̸̗̐l̵̗͠u̴̻̅t̷͔͗o̵̠͊ ̸̰̔Ả̷̞r̷͖͋g̸̝̔ę̷̄n̴̟̂t̶̰̒o̴̝͝ ̷͙̉M̵̟̽ò̵̧ń̸̼d̷̦̓ö̶̹

Dan:

'I was having breakfast an hour and a half ago. Two tops.'

It was another intrusive thought to have right about then, but it snuck in anyway, and stuck around for how surreal it was.

Then the wave hit me like it had something to prove, and I went for a swim.

Whoosh!

...

First impressions?

Water, everywhere.

Dark and heavy - all around crushing - and the currents swirled around me like I was being dragged deeper and deeper into a whirlpool that hated my guts.

The armour didn't weigh me down - Chiron's training made even the idea of that a total joke - but the glow I gave off stuttered and dimmed.

What had he called it?

Depths Of The Coiling Serpent?

Some intrinsic leeching effect then, trying to sap my strength even as it jerked at my limbs, spun me sideways, and twisted me upside down again and again in a loop.

Once upon a time, it may have even worked.

Now?

I don't think so.

I locked in, pulled on the stream of warmth simmering in my heart, and shot right up.

The whirlpool tried to cling on and twist me back down, but I flew straight through it, past the spiralling currents and out into the air with a shower of super-heated steam - then I kept going.

The flight was the easy part.

Then I looked down, and saw the enormous, range-spanning dome of swirling water, stretching out to stupid extents in every direction.

Like a snowglobe big enough to cover a small town, rising high enough to swallow spires whole, and dark almost all the way through.

"Balance Breaker, huh?"

As far as I knew, those things followed a theme - usually - but that didn't tell me much of anything right now.

"Some kind of territory creation? Defensive boundary and that's a dragon."

Not Dragon Mask.

Not something draconically inclined.

A genuine, serpentine dragon came swimming through the dome like it owned the place, with eyes like murky gold, fins running down its scaled spine, and teeth showing just enough to be rude.

Four clawed feet, no wings, and its size scaled to something halfway between Smaug and Cetus, but who even cared anymore?

"Seriously, why!?" I seethed, holding out my arm to recall my spear. "Why is it always dragons!?"

It must have caught that, because it looked straight up at me, eyes narrowing into yellow slits.

"You heard me!"

It reared its head back and roared, flaring its claws and fins, and unhinging wide, barbed jaws lined with teeth that had no business being that long.

Or sharp.

The reverberating shockwave that disrupted the water beneath it and kicked up the wind speed three notches was a nice touch, too.

"Yeah, yeah," I rolled my eyes. "I see you. Very scary. Goldfish from hell."

Classic, really.

...Serpent's Downfall still hadn't come flying back into my grip.

My other fist clenched as soon as I realised it.

The recall spell was snagging on nothing.

Why?

That didn't happen. It should have-

Wait.

My eyes snapped over to the dome.

I'd thrown the thing right as it formed.

And the water had a suppressive effect.

The spell wouldn't take hold.

"Son of a-!"

Then the dragon launched itself at me - fast.

One minute it was hovering over the dome, and the next, I was getting an eyeful of a fang-lined gullet with the reek to match.

Wonderful.

I jerked out of the way, dodging close enough that I was feet away from a baleful, slitted pupil glaring at me with pure, murderous intent.

So I did what came naturally.

I punched the bastard right in the eye.

The enraged war-bellow hit like a truck, and the way it reared back was real satisfying... right up until I realized it was deliberately coiling, cranking its tail back.

Oh.

I crossed my arms to brace right as the wall of scales and muscle whipped out at me, and the impact sent me trailing through the purple-blue tinted sky like a comet.

Ow.

I righted myself in the air, and it was already lunging again, jaws snapping over and over.

This time, though, I didn't just dodge.

I flew out to meet it head on instead, grabbed one of its whipping barbels - whiskers, basically, like a giant, moody catfish - and dug my fingers in hard, fully intending to rip the stupid thing off.

Only it must've seen where that was going, because it abruptly switched tracks and accelerated straight up, shooting through the clouds and taking me along for the ride.

And - I repeat - it was fast.

The sky darkened as we rocketed up, and the pressure spiked hard enough to rattle my teeth.

Gravity and space also got... funky.

I already knew we weren't in the human world - some kind of other realm - but the higher up we went, the stranger it felt, and I had a bad feeling I didn't want to know where the boundaries of this place let up.

So I didn't.

The barbel in my grip snapped and lashed, slick and corded with muscle, trying to tear itself free, and I let it, but not before I used it to tug myself closer to the dragon's head.

Then I bent at the knees, braced my feet against the dark scales, and kicked off like a missile.

Off, and right back down the way we came.

The furious roar followed me as I dropped, and I felt more than saw it twist, folding itself like a pretzel as it turned and plummeted after me.

The thing didn't spiral or feint or get clever about it.

It just dove, snapping itself straight, and the commitment had me grinning like a maniac.

That's it. Come at me.

Serpent's Downfall was my prized weapon, sure, and I couldn't call on it right now, fair enough.

Thing is, I didn't need to.

The spear's current form had been created from a combination of accidental alchemy, and a thaumaturgical foundation I could recast at any time, on any thing.

So I waited, the wind rushing in my ears and dragon hot at my heels as we plunged through the leftover clouds and towards the dome of dark, swirling water growing bigger and closer with every passing second.

Closer.

And closer-

-And closer-

-

-and then I spoke.

"Serpent's Downfall."

Not the Spear - the spell.

I cast it on myself, before flipping in midair - still in a controlled fall - and raising a palm up above.

The jaws were already there, bearing down on me with gleaming teeth.

"Hi."

The beam of light that tore out of my palm and punched upward in a straight, searing line of gold, infused with dragon-killing magic and a little homegrown spite to boot.

Just a pinch.

Those yellow eyes may have widened - maybe - but the moment the spell made contact, it was game over.

The dragon... disintegrated.

Not metaphorically.

Not poetically - or in any other fancy way.

Light. A shimmer. Scales glowing white-hot - and scene.

The beam speared through its snout, and the dragon popped like a soap bubble, dissolving into motes of floating blue-black sparks and the residual feeling of utter anticlimactic disappointment.

I'm not kidding.

I actually pulled a double-take, freezing my flight in place and staring hard.

That's it?

Then I looked down towards the dome.

"..."

...

"Oh, for the love of Dad!"

Can you blame me?

The second dragon was already taking shape beneath the water, serpentine form coming together and taking shape out of nothing at all.

Actually, scratch that.

Not a second dragon.

It was the exact same dragon, down to each individual scale.

I clicked my tongue impatiently.

It didn't take a genius to put the pieces together after that.

An Independant Avatar Type Sacred Gear.

One of the trickier sub-types - most of the famous ones couldn't create multiple avatars, but nothing was stopping a wielder from manifesting the same one over and over again so long as they had the stamina to keep at it.

This one had a dragon for an attack dog, and that Balance Breaker...

My eyes panned over to the dome again.

"That's your gimmick, then?"

I'd eat my shield if Dragon Mask wasn't hiding in there somewhere, probably at its core.

Offence through the avatar, and a defense that sapped vitality to keep enemies at bay.

A chance of victory through sheer attrition.

...

...

...

Yeah, forget that.

"You want to play dirty?"

I reached into my inventory band, and called out my bow.

"Fine by me!"

It manifested in my grip with a flash of light, the quiver over my shoulder, and the rush I got from their presence alone was like a double shot of caffeine and condensed sunlight straight to the brain.

What can I say?

Spearwork was a skill, but archery?

That was a birthright with extra steps, and just holding my bow - a god-crafted, divine-grade artifact others would unashamedly kill for - made me feel borderline invincible.

By the time the draconic avatar pierced through the dome and readied another death charge, I was already nocking a dragon-bone arrow and taking aim.

"Gaze Of The Far-Shooter."

My vision tinted gold, and I cast it outwards and down.

Past the dome's surface and the serpent in its depths.

Through the swirling water and the currents of warped darkness and space.

If my hunch was right-

There you are.

Right at the centre, still holding that ridiculous sword.

Dragon Mask.

I didn't need to deal with the dragon to get to him.

One arrow, and by the time it got anywhere near me, it'd all be over.

Good plan - one of my better ones, even.

Clear cut from A to Z.

So why waste time?

The dragon lunged up at me, and I lined up my shot.

Arrow met silver-gold string, the bow came to life in my hands, fletching warm against my fingertips, and-

...

...

...

B̴a̷l̶a̵n̸c̵e̸ ̸B̸r̴e̷a̴k̵e̶r̴:̵ ̶A̸̛̘s̷̹̓s̴̲̎o̸̗̐l̵̗͠u̴̻̅t̷͔͗o̵̠͊ ̸̰̔Ả̷̞r̷͖͋g̸̝̔ę̷̄n̴̟̂t̶̰̒o̴̝͝ ̷͙̉M̵̟̽ò̵̧ń̸̼d̷̦̓ö̶̹​

...

...

...

It was like a scene change in the movie.

No warning. No noise.

Not even a telltale burst of power.

Just... poof.

The world was overwritten.

The purple sky?

Overcast and iron-grey, heavy with low clouds that looked like they'd bite back.

The desert?

Long gone, switched out with endless plains of snow and jagged frost, ridgelines of ice clawing up from the ground that dwarfed the spires of before three times over.

The dome?

Frozen rock-solid, all the way through.

Every swirl of water was iced in place mid-motion, sculpted like a giant modern art exhibit made of weaponised frostbite and way too much attention to detail.

And the cold.

It was eerily silent and... beyond words.

The kind of unholy, biting chill that could make somebody's blood feel like fire from the inside out, in a way that had nothing to do with magic or sacred gears.

Not that they were suddenly irrelevant, either.

The dragon avatar was suddenly gone - poofed away with everything else.

What that said about Dragon Mask, I had no idea, but it couldn't be anything good - and Incinerate Anthem?

It was going berserk in my soul.

"Lavinia."

The word came out in a misty puff of breath, and my tongue hurt just speaking. it aloud, but I managed anyway.

It had to be her, and Absolute Demise.

I'd sensed her presence before - I knew she was close, but this...

What-?

"Impressive, isn't it?"

-And what now!?

I whirled around, snarling, and came face to face with a whole new kind of nightmare on the spot.

"To be fair, I did plan for the possibility of a Balance Breaker, so this is only mildly inconvenient."

Dark hair.

Darker eyes, and a casual smile - as if he hadn't just appeared out of gods-damned nowhere, without triggering my senses, in the middle of the friggin sky!

And how he was doing it-!

"But then again, Longinus Wielders are always a problem, and I am working with utter idiots - but enough about that."

Wings - eight of them.

Blacker than his hair and eyes put together, and flared wide in clear and unmistakable theatrics.

An Abrahamic Fallen Angel.

Ultimate Class.

He smiled at me pleasantly, like he was trying to make a good impression.

It looked wrong.


"Shall we introduce ourselves properly, little demigod?"

#9,394
Wrapping up this little side-quest before switching over to Sai down in the Underworld.

Onwards!
I've mentioned the system the Devils use to rank power before, haven't I?

The one that popped up when their Rating Games went mainstream, and people quickly decided they needed a neat little scoreboard to keep track of who could blow up what.

Low-Class?

You might as well not exist.

Middle-Class?

Around the supernatural baseline - maybe a few steps ahead - but nothing all that special in the long run.

High-Class?

Getting warmer now, with some serious firepower right out of the gate, and a mile and a half to go between the bottom and the peak.

And Ultimate-Class?

Whoo boy.

That's when you graduate from the kiddie pool stuffed with piranhas and dive into a whole different kind of ballgame - and it only scales up from there.

It wasn't a perfect system, sure.

Things weren't always so cut and dry within and between every class, but it was good enough to pin the tail on the right donkey nine times out of ten. And personally?

An eight-winged fallen angel - ultimate class by default - was one hell of a mean-looking donkey.

"Shall we introduce ourselves properly, little demigod?"

I didn't answer with words.

He wasn't through with his before my arrow was leveled at him, the string pulled back against my cheek.

That was step one.

Step two was the shimmering pulse of brilliant gold that shockwaved off of me on command.

No holding back against someone this dangerous.

I cranked things into high gear, unfurling all the power I usually held in reserve in one go.

The fact that a good chunk of the crippling, unnatural cold in the air recoiled like it'd been slapped - or stabbed, take your pick - was just a side bonus.

"Fallen Angel."

He didn't seem phased by the lightshow, but that wouldn't have made a difference either way.

"I don't know who you are," I glared at him with fire in my eyes - literally. "But you and your friends trespassed on my teacher's home, kidnapped his guest, and bringing me along makes mistake number three."

"Oh?"

"You've broken guest rights and slighted the gods of Olympus twice over - Name and explain yourself."

My glare narrowed into something fiercer.

"Now."

...

...

...

He was silent for a long second - but only one.

Then he smiled.

"...I'd tell you that that's a remarkably rough introduction for one so young..." The words were a lazy drawl carrying over the howling winds, and the tone grated on me from the first syllable out. "But that wasn't much of one at all, was it?"

"I will loose this arrow."

"There's no need for that." The threat washed off him easily enough, but his dark eyes flickered to the gleaming head and back. "We're only talking, and I mean you no harm."

"Then talk." I said flatly. "You have about three seconds."

My aim didn't waver.

"And counting."

Every impulse I had screamed to shoot first and ask questions later, but I could barely sense anything through the raging blizzard around us.

My aura was actively pushing against it, but it felt like wading through half‑frozen molasses - and that was only half metaphorical.

A desert overwritten with a frozen hellscape.

Just...

Props to the ridiculous power of a Longinus, but right now it was only making things harder - and that much more gnarly.

I needed time to lock onto Lavinia, and if it came down to a fight before that…

I needed him to make the first move.

"Aren't you a cheerful one." He huffed dryly, slowly raising his hands in mock-surrender. "I'll go first, then."

Bowing in mid-air was an awkward move to pull off, but he went for it anyway, tipping forward and flaring his wings wide behind him.

"Ezren Vale, at your service." He adjusted the collar of his leather bomber jacket and straightened out again. "Nominally of the Grigori. Fourth-generation descendant of the Original Watcher, Ramiel. May he rest in peace - or in peaceful oblivion, at least. There are worse things than just dying, after all."

That... meant basically nothing to me.

What I knew about the Grigori as a whole was surface-level at best, besides the fact that their internal factions were about as centralized as a flock of overcaffeinated pigeons.

Cooperative and buddy-buddy right up until they very much weren't.

"And you are?"

Ezren gestured leadingly, and I almost scoffed.

"Montoya. First name Inigo."

"That right?"

He understood the reference.

"Absolutely."

"Alright then." He hummed agreeably, "Is this the part where you accuse me of killing your father?"

That had me snorting outright.

"You couldn't come halfway close in your wildest dreams."

What was an Ultimate-Class to an Olympian?

"That said, considering the day I've had, you might as well prepare to die anyway."

"Made that bad a first impression, have I?"

"..."

...Fine, then.

Games it is.

"Your 'first impression' is about five minutes old, and it kicked off with a successful kidnapping on a day that was already well on its way to being a total write-off."

I let that hang for a second.

"And that was before one of your clowns tried to take my head off for jack all, just for the record, so… you tell me."

That actually got a blink out of him.

"Fair enough, honestly."

My eye twitched.

Just a little.

"…So glad we agree. Thrilled, really."

Come on, Lavinia. Where are you?

The only thing I was getting was arctic interference - like TV static crossed with impending frostbite.

The further out my focus seeped, the more it bit back, and the gnawing frost was getting worse by the moment.

"If it's any consolation at all, the 'clowns' you just mowed down weren't subordinates of mine."

What?

"No?"

"Perish the thought - I have standards." He waved it off dismissively. "Those overeager morons make up a handful of 'elite' strike teams for a nascent organisation trying to break in on the other side of the masquerade: The Utsusemi Agency."

The word tripped my translation spell, and I frowned.

Hollow cicada shell?

"Never heard of'em."

"I did say they were new on the scene, didn't I? Formed by the cast-offs and rejects of Japan's famed Shinto-mystic authorities: The Five Principal Clans. Heard of them?"

Yes, but it was a rhetorical question.

"Big names, bigger personalities, and somehow even more xenophobic than the Catholic Church, which is an achievement, I'll give them that much." He snickered, like he was genuinely impressed. "They're especially hard on their own, though. Descendants that don't show the right aptitude for their sacred arts, don't get patience and a reward for participation - they get the boot. And that's if they're lucky."

Lucky.

Dark and ominous implication - always a classic.

"Happens more than the Clans like to admit. The Utsusemi are what you get when enough of those rejects decide they're done accepting it. Like a pack of angry chihuahuas trying to torch the kennel out of pure spite."

He shrugged and stretched his arms over his head, idly rolling his wrists with the motion.

"It's all very poetic, but the gist of it is that they got their hands plenty dirty trying to pull that party trick off. Enough that some of their research caught my boss's attention - he has a taste for the audacity of it all."

Boss?

"Curious?" Ezren must have seen the flicker in my eyes. "Can't say, I'm afraid. Operational security has to start somewhere, and the big man in charge can be a right old tyrant when he wants to be - that's why I'm here. Drew the short straw, and now I'm... on loan, so to speak. Partnered with this quaint little troupe until they sort out some problems and get back to work."

It took me about point-two seconds to figure that one out.

"Lavinia."

"Ding ding!" He clapped on the spot. "Right on the money - yes, Miss Reni is quite the interesting girl. Her master, Glenda Silverbrook, used to hobnob with the Utsusemi. Nothing too strenuous - sharing a bit of book-smarts, stirring a few cauldrons, and generally helping them bumble along in return for resources and favors. Another famous witch poked in and out too, and everything was neat and tidy… until it all went kaput a few months back."

Of course.

Oz.

The gift that just kept on giving.

"You already know?"

Again, the irritating crow seemed to read it right off my face.

"I suppose you would, if you are what I think you are. Oz was smote, things imploded spectacularly, and the muppets I'm working with were left out to dry, so they're looking to salvage what they can."

I don't care.

The words where right on the tip of my tongue, but they would have been half a lie, and an excuse to cut off his monologue anyway.

So I side-tracked.

"This is what salvaging looks like to you?"

"Mistakes have been made." He admitted shamelessly. "The motivation behind them was solid. Your little friend was Silverbook's apprentice, which makes her worth something if they want to recoup losses. Potential valuable intel and all that, never mind the supposed magical skill that she can put to use... and the flashy power source bolted on. "

The Fallen Angel glanced around at the polar fiasco and shrugged, idly shaking the snow of his wings in a sudden ripple

"There was a plan. A good one. Lots of intricate subtleties - I know, because I nearly penned the damn thing myself."

Another look - almost sheepish, this time.

"This... clearly wasn't that."

"You don't say."

"I don't." He agreed with another easy shrug, and something about it was... eerie. Bad. "I'm quite upset about it, actually. I may have to kill a truly phenomenal number of people just to wash the taste of this fiasco out of-"

There.

Mid stand-off, between sentences, and I found what I was looking for just along the farthest edge of my sensory range.

Lavinia.

Just a glimmer of presence, and suddenly abnormal in a way that had my mind flinching with just a brush of awareness, but it was right there.

"-ah."

Somehow, he caught on.

I could tell, because the space between us effectively ceased to exist, and bang.

One arm cracked out like thunder, and both bow and arrow were torn out of my grip so fast it punched the air out of me.

So fast-!

The other hand latched around my neck, squeezed, and my windpipe promptly started screaming.

"I could feel you prodding, but to sense her out so quickly..." He clicked his tongue, digging his fingers into my throat like he wanted to claw it straight out. "Tricky little bastard, aren't you?"

"...!"

He wasn't expecting an answer - strangling the life out of someone usually killed good conversation - but his brows furrowed when I smiled.

With teeth.

"Y-you have no idea!"

He stiffened... and then his eyes blew wide open as I - or the image of me he was holding - flickered and shattered into a shower of scattering sparks.


Phoebus Performance.
​

A new spell I'd cooked up - something that blended Dad's domains of light and artistry into something both subtle and full of flair when I need it to.

Battlefield illusions.

Nothing to write home about yet, and the quality practically cratered with distance, but I didn't have to go far to put this one to good use.

I'd cast it before this conversation had even started, layered in with that very first burst of power, and by the time Ezren's eyes snapped over to me - the real me, hovering thirty feet up and away behind the breaking mirage - it was already too late.

He moved.

My arrow was faster.

It tore through the storm in a straight line, bright enough to make the snow blink.

Ezren twisted, body corkscrewing to slip the shot, and it still punched clean through one of his wings before he could furl it away.

He'd only just had time to feel it - sharp and stupid painful - face twisting in stunned fury-

Then the wake hit.

The arrow didn't just pass through - it dragged, kicking up a violent slipstream of funneled space that wrenched the mangled wing back and swallowed the rest of him whole.

There was no evading it. The sheer velocity hurled them down and sideways in a spiraling arc, straight toward the giant dome of frozen water.

The same one where Dragon Mask was probably perfecting his best impression of a human popsicle.

It never had a chance.

The light outpaced the collision, silver-gold and searing.

Then the impact registered: an explosive crack that split the ice clean down the middle, a jagged fracture racing from crown to base as the entire dome sheared in half under the force of it.

It sounded like a waterfall of breaking glass crossed with an earthquake. The aftershock alone kicked up a rolling wall of snow and frost five stories high and rising.

Not that I stuck around to admire my handiwork.

I was moving as soon as the dome splintered, storing away my bow and diving mid-cast.

Return.

This time, there was no Balance Breaker to leech away the spell. Serpent's Downfall came flying up at me on command, and I met it halfway down at full speed.

That shot wouldn't keep him down for long - no Ultimate Class would fall that easily, and in no universe was this the time to pick a fight I wasn't sure I could win.

Pride and skill were one thing.

Suicidal stupidity was another.

The second I had my spear in hand again, I was shifting away in a flash of gold, reappearing-


H̸͔̫͉̿̃ư̴̘̒̕s̵̜̹̩̊̃̅k̸̨̳̈
​

-what in the fresh hell is that!?

I got half a glance at Lavinia before I catapulted back on pure instinct - and for damn good reason.

She looked like death warmed over.

Or frozen over, maybe, and that wasn't a joke.

Still standing, but only just, and covered in hoarfrost from head to toe, with a sickly grey tinge to her skin, shot through with blackened, crisscrossing veins underneath.

Her arms were also limp at her sides, head hanging forward, hair falling over most of her face, and the little I could see of her eyes was milk-white.

They'd rolled all the way back in their sockets

That was Exhibit A

Exhibit B was the other thing looming just close enough to make my lizard-brain contort like an Olympic gymnast.

A form like polished glass, smooth and light-catching, and upright in a way that hurt to look at.

Two thin arms branching from each side, four in total, and its face was a half-blank mask - no mouth, no nose - with six pits for eyes on its left side.

A woman that wasn't a woman at all.

Absolute Demise's Manifest Avatar.

Yeah, I knew what it was.

Sacred Gears could look like just about anything, but the Thirteen had their mythical stand-out markers, and I knew them all by heart.

Though knowing and seeing it beforehand were worlds apart - and it was staring right at me.

.̴̧̘͇̻̱͓̑͂̀̽̚̚͝.̶̳͗̀͋́̀̿͝ͅ.̴̭̲̣̮̈́̽̋̌͐́̑͝​

My breath hitched, and the air in my lungs felt like it was icing over.

Standing in its presence alone made the cold twenty thousand times worse, to the point where the insides of my bones started to ache under the raw pressure - and it didn't shift an inch.

No attacks. No sudden moves.

Just focus.

Naturally, it was a nightmare.

The hollow cavities on its face locked onto me, and the attention was so twisted that I almost missed the second shape floating off to the side.

What?

Another girl.

My age, probably, with her arms and legs spread wide like she'd been snatched mid-sprint and just… stuck there, hanging a breath away from the Avatar's chest.

Which meant nothing good for her long-term health.

Half of her body was covered in rime so thick it looked sculpted, and her lips were blue and cracking as she grit her teeth like a cornered, frenzied animal.

It didn't stop the frost from setting in further, and when I caught her eyes, they were wild.

Desperate and unhinged.

She tried to speak, but her jaw just cracked - sharp and brittle, like a candy bar snapping in half.

All in all?

It took me one long, long second to snap out of it on my end - which might as well have been an eternity.

"Lavinia-"

Then I caught a fist to the face.

Wham.

The world went sideways in a smear of white and gold, my head snapping back so fast that I felt something pop in my neck.

No wind-up. No warning.

Just eight wings and murderous intent coming in at Mach screw you.

Ezren.

Typical.

The first blow knocked me off my feet like a rocket achieving liftoff. My skull barely started ringing before I caught a flash of black feathers and gaudy leather coming in hot from the right, and I swung Serpent's Downfall at him without thinking.

It didn't get far.

The spear slammed against something bright and staticky, and the next deflection tore it right out of my grip.

What-!?

Before I could react, he decked me in the chest.

Hard.

The vibration rattled through my armour and into my teeth. I careened down, rolled mid-air out of sheer habit, and tried to land on the balls of my feet.

It was like dropping an anvil on a windshield, and I would've punched through the splintering footing if the Fallen hadn't driven into me first.

I braced both arms against the incoming kick, and it hit like a racecar at full throttle. The ice under my feet exploded out like shrapnel as I went skidding back, carving twin trenches twenty yards long before I managed to catch myself.

"Brat."

He was already coming at me again, and this time, I didn't bother recalling the spear.

I willed it, and Serpent's Downfall came blazing in for his side like a firework caught mid-explosion - for all the good that did.

His charge slowed just enough to count as he curved out of the way, and one of his fists - wrapped in that crackling, static-bright light that was nothing like man - collided with the haft.

The flare of heat vaporized the snow, and the burst of pressure that sent it flying away flattened the frozen crust in a perfect ring around us.

Figures.

His other hand shot out, palm first, and aimed right at me.

Crap.

I didn't see the blast coming, exactly. Not past the first ray of off-white light blooming along his fingertips.

I just threw my hands up and fired back.

Sunlight blitzed out like cannon fire, and both beams met in the middle with a white-hot flash that made the one before it look a dying spark in comparison.

The energy locked, and I grit my teeth and pushed against the tide, refusing to give an inch, and hyper-aware of the heat I could feel burning even against my armour and the power beneath it.

"I wasn't sure what to do with you at first."

The words cut through the storm and the supernova between us, nasty and echoing, like they were drilled straight into my skull.

Really cheerful stuff, too.

"I was only after the girl, and Greek demigods are more trouble than they're ever worth. I'd have waited out the balance breaker, roughed you up for the hell of it, and sent you back to your Gods in one piece - but now?"

The shape of him flickered in the distance - distorting and warping, wings bleeding into a hazy blur.

That was the only tell.

"I'll send you back in a casket."

The supernova detonated


"▂▃▂▃▂▃!"​

...

...

...So.

The good news was that, for that one moment right there, I wasn't cold anymore.

The bad news was that the recoil hit like the mother of all gut punches - and that was the fun part.

The heat instantly went from a solid eight to a crime against nature, and every nerve along my skin lit up like I'd been flayed raw all over.

Even through my armour... was this what a sunburn felt like for normal people?

Wow. I hate it.

The air shifted, and I looked up.

Son of a-!

Ezren fell on me like a meteor, and the fists came hammering in.

Punch.

Pain shot through my arms as I braced against the savage haymaker.

Punch.

Lower this time, to my side. My ribs rattled like dice in a cup.

Punch.

Another jab to the face.

Punch.

The blows kept coming, every bit as fast as before, and three times as vicious.

Stronger than me. By an order of magnitude.

I could fight hand-to-hand just fine - pankration training did wonders for that - but this wasn't a fairy tale.

Skill didn't get you all that far when the other guy punched like a mountain you could only track by the skin of your teeth.

Punch!

I grit my teeth, and-

One hand shot out, faster than I could block it, wrapping around my throat with crushing force.

For real this time.

"There." He hissed triumphantly, lifting me right off my feet. The acrid thrum of foreign magic shot through the roof, and I could feel my limbs lock up like he'd tased me with pure vitriol. "Isn't this better?"

The taste of blood in my mouth?

Debatable.

He didn't give me the chance to croak the snark out at him anyway, and as the cold start creeping back in...

I noticed his wings.

All seven of them.

...

The one I'd shot...

Either folded away because of the injury, or... maybe I'd given him a really good reason to hate my guts.

...

Good.

Maybe he sensed the thought, because his grip tightened monstrously. Spots danced around my vision like disco lights.

"What?" The bloodlust was rolling off him in waves. "Nothing left to say?"

Nope. I'm done.

I looked him dead in the eye one last time - just to prove a point.

You shouldn't have got so close.

Then-

I let Incinerate Anthem off its leash, and everything went up in shades of apocalyptic purple.

Fwoom.

Holy Fire erupted everywhere, searing through whatever power kept me in place and striking out at Ezren like the judgment of God.

"!!!"

There was a beat where he saw it coming.

Terror flashed in his eyes, and he tried to hurl me away on instinct.

No dice.

Both of my hands snapped out, one locking around his wrist, and the other clamping onto his face.

My thumb drove into his eye socket for good measure, and by then, it was already game over.

The flames crashed over him, swallowing his body as they raced up his arm and head and out across his wings, and he ignited like a scarecrow stuffed with dry pitch.

B̴͕͛u̷̬̒r̵̰̄n̸̛̮, H̸͖͝ĕ̵͈r̶͙̈ḙ̵̋t̸̬̓ḯ̸͚ċ̶̺!̷̘̕​

The inhuman shriek hit like a sonic boom.

The desperate, flailing backhand hit harder, and I went skipping across the ice like a rock on a frozen lake - but the damage was done.

Ezren was still burning when I slid to a stop and came up on one knee.

Wings crumbling. Skin bubbling and melting off like wax. Shape glowing brighter and brighter to the point of absurdity, and howling loud enough to wake the dead while he was at it.

The whole biblical deal.

A part of me that was more Greek than hero found that vindicating.

Isn't that better, you jackass?

The rest of me was smart enough not to wait his death out.

I teleported.

When I reappeared in front of Absolute Demise's Avatar again, I didn't hesitate.

The feeling of its awareness made my skin crawl. The completed sculpture in its grip was terrifying.

None of that - or it - stopped me from stepping up to Lavinia, and grabbing her by the shoulders.

The cold burned. The weight in the air was crushing.

But I didn't die immediately, and that was as green a flag as I was going to get.

"Time to go."

Maybe she heard me.

Odds are she didn't - she barely looked alive.

It didn't matter.

I summoned my spear back, and the last thing I heard as it came flying through the snow was the sound of a Fallen Angel incoherent, dying wails.

He still didn't sound remotely human, and Incinerate Anthem thrummed under my skin with something like menacing victory.

Then Serpent's Downfall was in my grip again, and we slipped right on out of there and into the void between worlds.

...​

Chiron was already there when I shifted us back home.

I didn't question it.

The wards around this place being what they are, he'd probably sensed what happened the second it did.

He didn't even look at me for the most part - not at first.

Lavinia took center stage.

Chiron swept towards her without a word, and the first spells were already rolling through the air before the adrenaline in my blood had time to settle.

Green light pooled under her, and the cold she gave off died on the spot, replaced by a gentle, vibrating warmth that spread through the air and quickly drove the rest of it away.

The frost went with it, cracking and peeling away in careful little spirals that melted into nothingness before they ever reached the marble floor.

"Chiron."

She looked worse with it gone.

A lot worse.

Skin stark gray and waxy, black veins spreading and darkening beneath the surface, and eyes glazed over and empty.

There was a wound, too - an ugly-looking cut that split a line down the side of her face, along her cheek and jaw, and the edges were jagged and darker than all the rest.

I winced just looking at it.

The moment the last of the ice was gone, her knees buckled.

Chiron caught her before she toppled and lowered her carefully to the floor.

"Poison," he murmured, pressing two fingers to her forehead and letting a spark of green seep into her skin. "Fomorian, if only just. And her soul has endured a truly phenomenal amount of strain."

Exactly what you want to hear.

"I didn't see her fight," I explained quickly, hovering over his shoulder as he worked. "But she used a Balance Breaker."

I told him about the frozen desert and the Avatar, and he only frowned.

"The Remnant of Morana."

"Who?"

"The Slavic Goddess of Winter and Death. Her crystalized Divine Authority makes up the lion's share of Absolute Demise's power."

...

"...Alright then."

What else was I supposed to say?

It wasn't the time for questions.

Chiron pressed his palm flat against her sternum, and the shade of light beneath her shifted again. Tiny, weaving threads rose out of it, seeping over her sides and sinking straight into her chest and temples.

The black in her veins flickered violently and then snapped inward like a rubber band, and her back arched off the ground just as fast.

Like something fresh out of a cheesy exorcism movie.

"Holy-!?"

"Fomorian venom has to be burned out, for a given value of the word." He steadied her with impassive calm, ignoring the silent, ragged gasp and the wild flutter to her eyes. "It is a remarkably unpleasant thing, even when heavily diluted."

"How bad?"

He shook his head.

"It won't kill her. I expect it won't leave lasting damage at that. Certainly nothing beyond my ability to repair. That said-"

Another full-body tremor hit her like a truck, and I grimaced as she started convulsing.

"-I doubt the experience won't be... memorable. Terrible things often are."

Ain't that the truth.

I was almost tempted to offer up the Fleece, but if Chiron needed it, he would've asked.

It didn't take long before the rot popping out along her veins started to draw back in real time.

Not all at once, but it lost ground quickly as the glow moved under her skin. The gray tint faded with it, and color crept back in until she looked less like a corpse and more like someone who'd just pulled an all-nighter in Cocytus.

I hadn't realized I'd been holding my breath until then.

The tremors eased, gradually, and her shallow breathing evened out. Even the cut on her cheek began to mend as the minutes passed - the torn edges knitting together from the inside out until only a faint, fading mark was left.

Not even a scar worth mentioning.

Finally, Chiron pulled away, and the shimmering brilliance winked out.

"That should do it."

"You transmuted the venom, didn't you?"

Alchemically breaking it down into something harmless without ever having to purge it from her system.

"Just a simple trick," he agreed lightly. "I have had my fair share of experience with venoms - and how best to unmake them."

Something about the way he said that niggled at me, but I shoved it aside for now.

Lavinia still hadn't stirred, and Chiron didn't need to follow my gaze to explain.

"She will need rest," he said. "A great deal of it. A few hours of quiet will only help."

He snapped his fingers, and she vanished with a rush of displaced air - probably conked out in some guest room across the estate.

Then he gave me a look.

"Now then-"

"Explanation time?"

"From the top, if you please."

"The Fallen Angel did it."

The look went razor sharp.

...​

It took me all of thirty seconds to run him through the story. A minute, tops.

Hell, it couldn't have been twenty since all of this kicked off, if even that.

Everything moved faster on the supernatural end of things.

Sometimes too fast.

Chiron listened impassively, for the most part.

Then he dropped a hand on my shoulder.

"You did well."

That made me straighten up - which was an achievement, now that I was calming down.

The crash after a battle rush was always a drag, and I felt heavy and dull all over.

"I got the drop on him. Things would have been different without my bow and Incinerate Anthem."

"Most likely." He didn't deny it. "Eight-winged Abrahamic Angels are dangerous enemies, Fallen or otherwise - and otherwise could have been far worse, but that is besides the point. Do you still have a lock on the realm you were taken to?"

The rea-

I blinked.

"Yes?"

To get from Point A to Point B, you usually had to be 'aware' of both, up to a point - which made hopping back and forth not all that hard, once you had a handle on it and the power to spare.

Chiron seemed satisfied with the answer.

"Good. We'll visit it as soon as present circumstances allow for it."

"What?"

"You heard me."

"...I did. Hence, I repeat: What?"

A pause.

The meaningful kind, full of tension and pressure nobody wanted to deal with and still got roped into anyway.

"My student and my guest were taken from the very foot of my home, Daniel."

He didn't raise his voice, but he didn't have to - the tone alone could make steel flinch.

"I will leave neither crime unanswered, and an investigation is due."

"Right now?"

"Sooner rather than later." There was no give there whatsoever. "The time of retaliation will come - having all the facts will only decide the scope of it."

...

He was dead serious.

Not that I expected anything else, ever, and he had every right to be...

Still.

My teacher was angry, genuinely, and the novelty value there had me feeling all giddy and vindictive again.

Fallen Angels. Utsusemi. Who cares who else.

Someone had just signed up for a world of hurt, and they didn't even know it yet.

The karma was going to be amazing.

...

...

...

Except-

Except-

...

Karma went both ways, and I was clearly waving the red cape at fate right there.

Naturally, it took me up on the challenge.

Something changed, and Chiron straightened himself.

Space flashed and parted behind us, and another shower of light broke out - the kind I knew by heart.

My shoulders slumped the second I recognised it.

Of course.

"Daniel."

"Hey, Dad. Just doing some training here." I turned around and smiled innocently. "How's tricks?"

Somehow, Apollon didn't buy my brilliant performance.

He took one look at my face - the blooming bruises, split lip, and the mess of it all - and his expression blanked in a way that probably heralded divine war crimes once upon a time.... and possibly still did.

"What. Happened?"

... Damn it.

I should have stayed with Sairaorg.

...​
